declarations.description:
Content that a row shows and hides in place. One item is a single disclosure; several are a set whose items open by themselves or, with `exclusive`, one at a time. A help page's questions, the sections of a settings screen, the advanced part of a form. Contract: specs/accordion.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: its items are the product's own native `
` elements, which stay in the document. They open and close, are focusable, carry the expanded state, keep their closed content in the page (a field in it keeps its value and is sent with its form) and are opened by a link to a fragment and by the browser's find-in-page, before any script runs and without it. ```html
palette Colors Roles, palettes and the six schemes 48 roles

Every color a component reads is a role.

A label that is a heading

…

A disabled item

…

 ``` An item is a `
` whose first child is its ``: the header. The summary's text is the label, or ONE element in its place — a heading of the level the page's outline needs, or a `` around text with inline content; an element with `data-supporting-text` is the line under the label, one with `data-trailing-text` the short value before the chevron, a `.tanrei-icon` the glyph at the start. `open` is the item's own attribute and property and `toggle` its own event (it does not bubble; `event.newState` is `open` or `closed`) — the browser also sends it when the product sets `open`. A disabled item is ``. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/accordion.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-accordion-*` token — which draws the whole look and every state before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: the system's answer to a press (ripple, dim), the arrow keys, `exclusive` (the `name` it writes on its items), the height motion where the browser cannot move a height to `auto` in CSS, the pressed header kept in place while an item above it closes, focus given to the header when its item closes around it, the supporting and trailing text read as the header's description instead of as part of its name, a disabled header refused, an open item drawn and answered as one target — closed by a press on its content, hovered, pressed and focused as a whole, with the pointer cursor over it (ACC-36; without script only the header is a target), and the debug reports. An accordion in an item's content is content like any other, drawn by its own attributes.
declarations.name: TanreiAccordion

declarations.description:
Frames a page or an app: places a header, the navigation, the main content, an aside and a footer, decides from the window's width how each of them is shown, and lets a keyboard reach the content in one step. It draws the frame and none of what stands in it. Contract: specs/app-shell.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the frame around the product's own regions, which stay in the document and keep their semantics — a `
` is the page's banner and the one `
` its main landmark for a screen reader, a crawler and a page without script alike. ```html Skip to content
…a callout…
menu
…
…
…
…
… ``` A region is a child with a `slot` attribute — the region's name; no shadow root reads it — and the main region is the one `
` without one. They are written in the order a keyboard walks them (APS-22): the skip link, the announcement, the header, the navigation, the aside while `aside-order` is `before`, the main region, the aside while it is `after`, the footer, the navigation bar. The stylesheet places them by name and never reorders focus. `footer-hidden` leaves a filled footer out of the frame (APS-31). Everything laid out is `@tanrei/web/app-shell.css`, before and without this script (APS-24): the window's class is a media condition, a region the class does not show has no box, and the skip link is an anchor to the main region's id. The element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, and what a stylesheet cannot say: - **the class**, as the read-only `windowClass`, the `data-window-class` attribute and `windowclasschange` — from two `matchMedia` listeners of the widths the stylesheet was written with; no resize listener and no frame loop. What the frame holds also inherits it as `--tanrei-app-shell-window-class`, from the stylesheet alone; - **the menu button** — the one icon-only `` in the header — which it answers while the navigation has no place in the layout: `navigationOpen` and the `open` of a `` in the navigation region become true, the drawer's `close` makes them false again, and the button says `aria-expanded` and what it controls; - **the scroll offset**: the header's measured height as `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset` on the document's root (the stylesheet sets the root's scroll padding from it), and the navigation bar's as `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset-end`, so a link's target and a focused element rest clear of both. The product's own sticky parts read the same properties; - **a landmark** for a region whose element does not give one (`role="banner"` on a header that is not a `
`, `aria-label` from `aside-label` on an aside without a name), and `tabindex="-1"` on a `
` that lacks it; - the debug reports of APS-4, APS-21 and APS-29. With `scroll="main"` the main region is the scrolling view: name its id in the app bar's `scroll-target`.

Stands for a person, or for a team or a project, by a small picture — by initials or a glyph where there is no
picture — in a round or a square box of three sizes. A picture, never a control.

Contract: specs/avatar.spec.json. `<tanrei-avatar label="Ada Lovelace" initials="AL" src="/people/ada.jpg">`. It draws
the first of these it has: the picture, once it has loaded; the initials the product gives (at most two characters as
a reader counts them, as written — the avatar never makes initials from the name); the glyph in its `icon` slot; the
system's own glyph. The box never changes size and nothing changes place when the picture arrives or fails. Every
visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-avatar-*` token; how far its corners ease is the system's amount
(`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`).

Alone, it is an image named by `label` (the name in full — never "Photo of", never the initials). Beside the same
name in visible text, set `decorative` and the name is read once. It takes no input and no focus and emits no event:
an avatar that leads somewhere is inside a link, one that opens something inside a Button, and a dot or a count on it
is a `<tanrei-badge>` around it.

declarations.description:
Several avatars drawn as one row in which each lies a little over the one before it, with a gap around each, and a
last box that counts the members it does not draw: the avatar's group form.

Contract: specs/avatar.spec.json (AVT-16…AVT-23). `<tanrei-avatar-group label="Reviewers" max="4">` around
`<tanrei-avatar>` members. The group gives its `size` and `shape` to every member and makes each one named, whatever
its `decorative` says. `max` is the most boxes drawn, the overflow box included (six members with `max="4"` are three
members and "+3"); `total` is the real count where the product gives fewer members than exist. The members it does not
draw stay in the document as its children and are not drawn or exposed. Anything that is not a `<tanrei-avatar>` is
not a member and is not drawn.

It is a group named by `label`, holding one named image per member it draws and then the overflow's text
(`overflow-label` or the product's words `avatarGroupOverflowLabel`, with `{count}` filled by the number not drawn;
else the drawn count). The overflow box is text, not a control: showing the people it counts is a
link or a Button beside the group.

declarations.name: bottomSheetRelease
declarations.description:
BSH-9: where a released drag goes — `close` (below half the lowest height, or a downward fling with no height below
it), else the next height in the direction of a fling, else the nearest. `position` is the sheet's visible height at
the release, `velocity` its vertical speed in px per ms (positive: down).

Shows supplementary content or a short task in a surface that rises from the bottom edge: `standard`, over the lower
part of its parent while the content above stays usable (a layout region), or `modal`, a modal step that dims
and blocks everything else until it is dismissed (a modal overlay).

Contract: specs/bottom-sheet.spec.json. The content is the default slot. The sheet is as tall as its drag handle's row
and its content, up to its `detent`: `partial` takes `container.partial-fraction` of the area, `full` reaches up to
`container.margin-block-start` below its top. The person moves it between the two by dragging (the handle's row, the
content's padding, or the content where it lets the drag through) or with the drag handle, a button while there are
two heights; the element sets `detent` and fires `detentchange`.

A header below the handle's row holds `headline` (a heading, which names the sheet where `label` is empty) and, while
`closable`, an icon-only `<tanrei-button>` of the small size showing the close glyph, named by `close-label`, in the
variant `comp.bottom-sheet.close-button.variant` names (tonal in the default system), as every host's close button
is; a divider below it as `divider-visibility` says (BSH-28, BSH-29). The header stays while the content scrolls.

Controlled: the sheet never closes itself. While `closedby` is not `none` it fires `close` with a reason — a released
drag below its lowest height and, for a modal sheet, a press on the scrim, Escape or the platform's back — and you set
`open` to false. The close button fires `close` with the reason `close` whatever `closedby` says. A product that does
not close it sees it settle back.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with `showModal()`: in the top layer over `::backdrop` (the scrim),
docked to the window's bottom edge, everything else inert, the page held from scrolling and focus kept inside. Focus
goes to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, else the sheet (also when it is mounted open), and returns where it was
when it closes. Standard: a `<section>` named by `label`, docked to the bottom of its containing block — the host fills
the nearest positioned ancestor, so give the parent that holds the sheet and the content `position: relative` — with
presses above it reaching the content; opening it moves focus in, closing it gives focus back, and Tab leaves it open.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-bottom-sheet-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; the sheet sits on the on-screen keyboard (`visualViewport`).
declarations.name: TanreiBottomSheet

declarations.description:
Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy of pages and leads back up it: the levels above as links, in order from the top, with the page itself last. Contract: specs/breadcrumbs.spec.json. The levels are the product's own children, which stay in the document (BRC-2, BRC-13): an `` for a level with a destination, a `` for one without — the current page, or a level that has no page. Before the element is defined, and with scripting off, the page holds the whole trail as links that work. ```html Home Components Button ``` A level's label is its text. `aria-current="page"` on the last level marks the current page; `data-icon` names a glyph of the system's icon set, drawn before the label; `data-icon-only` draws the glyph alone and keeps the text as the level's name; `data-mirror="always"` or `"never"` is the product's word on mirroring that glyph in a right-to-left layout. `underline` says when the links are underlined (BRC-30); a row of the overflow menu is a menu item and never is. A level's `click` is the anchor's own: cancel it and the browser follows nothing (BRC-22). Everything drawn on a level is `@tanrei/web/breadcrumbs.css` (every value a `--tanrei-comp-breadcrumbs-*` token), which draws the trail before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The shadow root holds only what the product did not write: a `
` named by `label`, the ordered list with one item for each level, the separators, and the overflow button with its menu. `overflow="collapse"` (the default) keeps the trail on one line: when it is wider than the width it is given, its middle levels go behind the overflow button, beginning next to the first, as many as the width asks for; then the first; and the last label is cut only when the button and it alone do not fit. The button opens a menu of the levels taken out; choosing one is a click on that level's own anchor. The trail is measured when its width, a label, the text size or the direction changes; at rest it runs nothing. `overflow="wrap"` keeps every level and lets the trail run over as many lines as it needs.

declarations.description:
Lays out a few related Buttons in one row or one column, spaced apart or joined into one shape, places the confirming
and the dismissive ones by the orientation, and names them as a group.

Contract: specs/button-group.spec.json. Every value it reads is a `--tanrei-comp-button-group-*` token: the gap of each
variant, the connected corners, the divider and the padding at a joined row's outer ends. Its items are
`<tanrei-button>` children, labelled or icon-only, each drawn from its own tokens, with its own states, events,
semantics and Tab stop (BGR-5). The group takes no focus, handles no key and keeps no selection; a toggle Button in it
stays independent. It draws nothing of its own but the dividers of a connected group.

Order (BGR-13, BGR-14): a child with the `confirming` attribute (OK, Save, Next, Delete) is placed at the end of a row
and at the top of a column; one with `dismissive` (Cancel, Back) at the start of a row and at the bottom of a column;
the others between them, each run in the order given. The children are not moved in your DOM: each is assigned to a
slot of its own, in the placed order, so focus and assistive technology follow that order (BGR-15).

In a connected group the items are joined as `separation` names (BGR-21): under `divider` they touch, with square
corners where they meet, and no item draws its outline or its elevation's ring along a seam; a seam carries a line
only while the two items it joins rest on the same fill (BGR-24) — between a selected toggle and an unselected one the
edge of the fill already marks it — in `connected.divider.color`, or `connected.divider.on-fill.color` between two
emphasis fills (filled Buttons, selected toggles);
under `gap` they stand `connected.gap` apart with `connected.inner-shape` corners. `auto` — the default — takes
`comp.button-group.connected.separation`, which follows the design system's `sys.behavior.separation`. The group
gives its items their corners, minimum size, seams and outer padding through custom properties the items read
(`--tanrei-group-*`): an internal contract between Tanrei elements, not a styling API.
declarations.name: TanreiButtonGroup

declarations.description:
The open axes (SPB-8): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same functions
as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in debug builds.

Performs a main action with one press, and offers related actions in a menu from a second, joined button beside it.

Contract: specs/button-with-menu.spec.json. Two native buttons in one row: the leading half (the optional icon and the
label) performs the main action and fires `click`; the trailing half (the chevron) asks to open or close the menu and
fires `toggle`. The menu is a Tanrei Menu in the shadow root, holding the `menu` slot's items, placed below the whole
button with menu with the end edges aligned; focus returns to the trailing half when it closes. It never opens or closes
itself: set `open` from `toggle`, and to false from `close`.

With `hover-open`, a mouse or a pen resting on the trailing half for `hover-delay` ms (unset: the
`comp.button-with-menu.motion.hover-open-delay` token) asks to open it too, through the same `toggle`. A menu open from
hover takes no focus, asks to close (`toggle` with false) once the pointer has been off the trailing half and the menu
for `motion.hover-close-delay`, and closes on Escape wherever focus is; a press or a key on the trailing half keeps it
open and moves focus in, as if that activation had opened it.

The halves are joined as `separation` names (SPB-30): under `divider` they touch, with square corners where they meet
and a line on the seam, and neither half draws its outline or its elevation's ring along the seam; under `gap` they
stand `container.inner-gap` apart with `container.inner-shape` corners. `auto` — the default — takes
`comp.button-with-menu.container.separation`, which follows the design system's `sys.behavior.separation`. They are
never stacked. `trailing-width="narrow"` draws a slim trailing half: the chevron and a small inset on each side, with
no padding added at its round end — as wide as a narrow icon-only Button (SPB-32).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-button-with-menu-*` tokens, one set per variant shared by both halves, each
half drawn in its own state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`); all
are read from the cascade, so they follow `data-tanrei-system`.

keeps its variant's emphasis and takes the error role's color in it (BTN-40) — filled in the error color, tonal in
its tonal container, the label of an elevated, outlined or text button (and an outlined button's edge) in the error
color. Disabled, it looks like any disabled button of its variant. It adds a color and nothing else: the label says
what is destroyed (BTN-42). Ignored on a toggle, and reported in debug builds (BTN-41).

members.name: size
members.description: Visual height (small 32 / medium 40 / large 56), which is also an icon-only button's width at its default width. The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: width
members.description:
How wide an icon-only button is: `default` as wide as it is high (32 / 40 / 56), `narrow` its glyph and
`comp.button.container.padding-inline-narrow` on each side of it (28 / 32 / 32 in the default system, whose inset
is 4 at every size; it has no narrow width of its own, so it follows its glyph) for a tight row of icon actions,

not change, and the hit area meets the minimum target at every width — a narrow button is never drawn wider to
reach it. Anything else is drawn as `default` (reported in debug builds, BTN-21).

members.name: fullWidth
members.description:
Takes the whole width its container gives it, its content centred, at the height of its size (the `full-width`
attribute, BTN-39): a form's only action on a narrow screen, the action at the foot of a card or a sheet. A label
that does not fit wraps, its lines centred; an icon-only button centres its glyph and ignores `width`. Ignored while
a host lays the button out (a button group, a toolbar, the actions of a dialog, a popover, a callout or an empty
state), which gives it its width: a button group's own `full-width` is how a row of buttons shares one.

members.name: iconPosition
members.description: Which side of the label the icon sits on, in the reading direction. Ignored without a label or an icon.

members.name: toggle
members.description: Makes the button a two-state control: activation switches `selected`, and assistive technology announces it as pressed or not pressed.

members.name: selected
members.description: Whether a toggle is on. Ignored unless `toggle` is true.

members.name: disabled
members.description:
Prevents interaction and removes the button from the focus order. A disabled submit button sends nothing, and
still stops Enter from sending its form where it is the form's default button (BTN-32). A button that is not a
link is disabled as well by a `<fieldset disabled>` around it. A button disabled while it holds focus keeps it
until the next frame, as the platform's own does, and its `disabled` attribute is written then.

members.name: focusableWhenDisabled
members.description:
Keeps a disabled button in the focus order (BTN-38): drawn and exposed as disabled (`aria-disabled`), refusing every
activation, but reachable by Tab and by a pointer, and keeping focus when it becomes disabled — so that a person can
learn why it does nothing (a tooltip, a description). A disabled fieldset still takes it out of the focus order.
Ignored unless `disabled` is set.

members.name: busy
members.description:
The action it started is under way (BTN-36, BTN-37): it keeps its focus, its place in the focus order and its size,
draws the loading indicator's arc in place of its label and icon, refuses every activation — a submit button sends
nothing, and stops Enter in its form as a disabled one does — and announces `busyLabel`.

members.name: busyLabel
members.description: What assistive technology is told while the button is busy ("Saving"): your words, in your language. Required while busy.

members.name: label
members.description:
The accessible name, where it is more than what the button draws. Required for an icon-only button. Beside a drawn
label it is the whole name in place of the drawn text, which stays drawn — for an action repeated in every row
(drawn "Reset", named "Reset: Spacing") — and it must contain the drawn text, so that a person who says what they
see is heard: a debug build reports one that does not, and the name stays what was given (BTN-16).

members.name: type
members.description:
Web only. What a press does to the button's form: `button` nothing (the default), `submit` asks it to submit as
the platform's own submit button does — after `click`, the form's validation, then its `submit` event — and
`reset` asks it to reset (BTN-27, BTN-28). Anything else is `button` and reported; a toggle and a link ignore it
(BTN-33). `formaction` and its siblings are not read.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only. With `value`, the pair sent with the form when this button is the one that submitted it; nothing is sent while it is empty (BTN-31).

members.name: value
members.description: Web only. What is sent under `name` when this button submitted the form.

members.name: href
members.description:

role, an `<a href>` in the shadow root, activated by Enter and not by Space, drawn exactly as the button it would
otherwise be. Ignored while `toggle` is set; white space is no destination, and a `javascript:` address or one that

members.name: target
members.description:

members.name: download

members.name: form

declarations.name: PROGRESS
declarations.description:
CAL-29: the ONE progress every look between two months is drawn from, a custom property of `.pages` that the element
writes and no one registers — 0 at the first view the grid holds, 1 at the next (and 2 at a third, while a change
begins during another or a drag may go either way). A drag and a scroll write it in each frame; a button's, a key's
or a wheel's change writes it in each frame of the page motion, by a clock of the element's (calendar.ts, `travel`).
The rows' offset, a day's fade and the mix of a day's two conditions are `calc()`s of it — steps and clamps of it,
which no transition of a real property could follow — so a moment of a button's change and a drag held at that place
are one look, and nothing has a threshold. `.pages` holds it and the rows and the days inherit it.

Shows one month as a grid of days, in the page or inside a picker, and lets a person choose one date or one range of
dates from it.

Contract: specs/calendar.spec.json. The calendar draws no surface and no padding of its own: it is seven cells wide
(never wider than its container) and the page, or the picker that holds it, gives it its background. It commits each
choice itself — it sets `value` (or `start` and `end`) and then fires `change` — and is not form-associated: the
product's field is. Months move by the previous and next buttons, Page Up / Page Down, and along the axis the design
system names (`comp.calendar.navigation.axis`, vertical by default) by a wheel or trackpad scroll and by a drag of a
finger, a pen or the primary mouse button: the days follow either point for point — a scroll through month after
month, a drag to the neighbouring month — and settle on the neighbour from a quarter of the way on. A wheel that
reports lines or pages moves one month a step.

Dates are ISO 8601 calendar dates ("2026-09-17") without a time or a time zone. Month and weekday names, digits and
the first day of the week come from `Intl` for `locale` — without it, the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's
language. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-calendar-*` tokens; the navigation buttons are
`<tanrei-button variant="text">` elements that keep their own. `focus()` moves focus to the active day (or the
displayed year in the year view).

cssParts.description: The month-and-year button that switches between the day view and the year view.
cssParts.name: view-toggle

cssParts.description: The day grid (role grid): the weekday row and six rows of days.
cssParts.name: grid

cssParts.description: A day (a gridcell); `data-date` holds its ISO date, `data-adjacent` marks a day of the neighbouring month.

members.name: mode
members.description: `single`: one date, in `value`. `range`: one contiguous span, from `start` to `end` inclusive. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The chosen date in single mode, as an ISO 8601 calendar date ("2026-09-17"); empty when none is chosen.

members.name: start
members.description: The first date of the chosen range in range mode; empty when none is chosen.

members.name: end
members.description: The last date of the chosen range in range mode, never before `start`; empty while only `start` is chosen.

members.name: min
members.description: The earliest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

members.name: max
members.description: The latest date that can be chosen; empty for no limit.

members.name: disabledDates
members.description: Dates inside min and max that cannot be chosen (booked, closed). The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated list or a JSON array.

members.name: isDateDisabled
members.description: A rule no list can hold (every weekend): true for an ISO date that cannot be chosen. Read with `disabledDates`. Property only.

members.name: today
members.description: The date drawn as today; empty reads the device's current date in its own time zone (and again at midnight).

members.name: firstDayOfWeek
members.description: The weekday in the first column (`first-day-of-week`); `locale` takes it from the locale.

members.name: locale
members.description: A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for names, digits and the first day of the week; empty: the nearest `lang`, then the browser's.

members.name: startView
members.description: Whether the calendar first shows the days of a month or the list of years (`start-view`).

members.name: showAdjacentDays
members.description: Fills the spare cells with the neighbouring months' days, drawn quieter; they can be chosen (`show-adjacent-days`).

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the whole calendar ("Check-in date"); a picker that holds it names it itself.

members.name: startLabel
members.description: Range mode: the description of the start day (`start-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ startLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

members.name: endLabel
members.description: Range mode: the description of the end day (`end-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ endLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the day has no description.

members.name: previousMonthLabel
members.description: The previous-month button's accessible name (`previous-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ previousMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: nextMonthLabel
members.description: The next-month button's accessible name (`next-month-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ nextMonthLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: yearViewLabel

declarations.description:
The open axes (CLO-30): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in
debug builds. A variant a layer adds has no edge: only `outlined` draws one (CLO-4).

A notice that is part of the content and stays there, as a quiet fill or an outline, in a status's colors with its glyph.
A note, a caution, the reason for something or a summary of what is wrong, in the flow of the page, with an optional
title, actions and a close button.

Contract: specs/callout.spec.json. `<tanrei-callout status="warning">…</tanrei-callout>`: the body is the element's
own content (text, or the product's blocks — long-form blocks in a `<div class="tanrei-prose" data-measure="false">`),
the title is the `headline` attribute or the `title` slot, a glyph of the icon set goes in the `icon` slot, and the
product's Buttons or links in the `actions` slot. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-callout-*` token, one set per
variant and status; how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`). Its close
button is a small icon-only `<tanrei-button>` in the variant `--tanrei-comp-callout-close-button-variant` names, drawn
on a filled look in the body color of the callout's form (a tone): its container that color made translucent, its
glyph that color, its states the Button's own.

It is a note (`role="note"`), read where it stands and never announced. With `live` it is a live region instead: it
is announced once when it is shown after the page was presented and when its title, body or status changes — politely
(`role="status"`), or assertively for warning and error (`role="alert"`). It never takes focus.

A status is never told by color alone: a status form draws the status's glyph, and the title says it or
`statusLabel` adds it in words for assistive technology ("Warning, …") without drawing it.

`title` is the `headline` property and attribute, because HTML's global `title` would show a tooltip over the block.
`open` defaults to true; `open="false"` is how markup starts a callout closed.

The open axis (CRD-7): a variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same function as the

Sets a group of related content apart from its background, and can be one action that opens what it shows.

Contract: specs/card.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-card-*` tokens, one set per variant and
state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a press is answered and
how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far its
corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`), read from the cascade.

The content is the default slot: any layout. The card insets it by `comp.card.container.padding` (not with `flush`),
clips it to its corners and hands it the variant's content color as the inherited `color`. With `interactive` the
whole card is one action with the button role — its content must then hold nothing interactive (reported in debug
builds) — and it can be `disabled`, which dims it as a whole. Without `interactive` it has no role (a named group
with `label`) and leaves its content's semantics alone.

With `href` the whole card is one link — a link card (CRD-19), whether `interactive` is set or not: the
shadow root holds an `<a href>` around the slot in place of the element with the button role, drawn as an interactive
card is. Enter activates it and Space does not; `click` fires first and cancelling it cancels the navigation.
`target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), and reads `target-label` as the link's description; the card
draws no mark, because its content is yours — put the icon set's `open_in_new` in it. Its content must hold nothing
interactive, as an interactive card's.

members.description:

centred hero or a row that snaps; otherwise (fixed widths at the start, free scroll) the first item wholly in view.

members.name: position
members.description: The scroll position p for a scroll offset: within the range, and whole when it is within a hair of it.

members.description: The scroll offset of a position.

members.name: logical
members.description: p as the ring sees it while loop is in effect (0 up to N), else p itself.

members.description:
CRL-12, CRL-27: item `index`'s slot position s at `position`: i − p, or, while loop is in effect, the one value that

members.description: CRL-17: the resting item — the item at slot 0, or the first item wholly in view (fixed widths at the start, free).

members.name: revealPosition
members.description:

position nearest it, the shorter way round while loop is in effect; or, for fixed widths at the start with free

members.description:

members.name: indicatorPosition
members.description:

to j + 1; while loop is in effect it is p less a whole number of turns, from 0 up to N.

members.name: dotDistance
members.description: CRL-29: how far q is from dot j, around the ring while loop is in effect.

members.name: nearestResting
members.description: CRL-31: the index of the resting position nearest `position` (a dot's index), 0 up to D − 1.

members.name: restingPosition
members.description:
The position of resting position `j` (a dot): the resting position itself, or, while loop is in effect, the whole
position of that ring value nearest `from` (the shorter way round).

members.name: stepResting
members.description:
CRL-30, CRL-32: the resting position one step from `position`'s nearest (`direction` 1 or −1): beyond the ends it
wraps while `wrap` is true — forward round the ring while loop is in effect, else to the other end — and otherwise

members.name: adjacentResting
members.description:

neighbour; between two, the nearer of them on that side. Round the ring while loop is in effect; otherwise the ends
are where it stops.

members.name: atEnds
members.description: CRL-43: whether `position` is at (or before) the first resting position, and at (or beyond) the last; never under loop.

members.name: recentre
members.description:

come within a turn of either end; otherwise `position` itself. Moving by whole turns draws nothing new.

declarations.description:
Lets people browse a row of visual items that scrolls sideways around one item in focus — the hero, in the centre (the
default) or at the start, the others narrower (fluid widths) or smaller (scaleOthers) as they move away, every two
neighbours one gap apart at every scroll position (CRL-40) — each item opening what it shows. A featured row may loop, show its position in dots and advance by itself, with a control to stop it.

Contract: specs/carousel.spec.json. The items are `<tanrei-carousel-item>` children, in order. The carousel is a native
horizontal scroller — wheel, trackpad, touch and pen scroll it as the platform does — whose track is as long as the
scroll range; it places every item from the scroll offset (CRL-12), and settles at a resting position when a scroll
ends while `snap` is true (CRL-14). The items are one Tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End move between items and
bring the focused one into place (CRL-17, CRL-18). Over the ends of the row, a previous and a next control move it one
resting position (CRL-41 – CRL-43). Below the items, a controls row holds the page indicator (one
slider, CRL-29 – CRL-31) and the playback control (CRL-35). Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-carousel-*`
tokens.

members.name: heroAlignment

members.name: itemWidth
members.description:
The width the hero is laid out at, in CSS px (the `item-width` attribute); null takes
`comp.carousel.container.large-width`. With fixed widths every item is this wide (at most the inner width); with
fluid widths the hero is kept between a floor and a cap (CRL-9). Not a positive number: treated as null and
reported (CRL-24).

members.name: fluidWidth

members.name: contentAlignment

members.name: scaleOthers
members.description: Draws the items other than the hero smaller, down to `comp.carousel.container.min-scale`, following the scroll (CRL-26).

members.name: snap
members.description: Whether the row settles at a resting position when a scroll ends (CRL-14). False (the `free-scroll` attribute) lets it rest wherever it ends.

members.name: loop
members.description: Whether the row is endless (CRL-27). Takes effect only with two or more items.

members.name: navigation
members.description:

members.name: autoplay

declarations.name: measured
declarations.description:
What depends on one line of the typing area's text (CCM-2, CCM-3, CCM-41), for a line of `line` (a CSS length):
the capsule's corners and its glow, which follow the one-line height, and the least height of each group of
Buttons, which is the typing area's with one line — so that a Button is centred on a single line and, as lines
grow, stays at the bottom edge at the distance it had. The stylesheet has it for a line of no height, which is
`container.height` alone; the element writes it again, as a rule of its own, once it has read the member's line.

Lets a person write a message and send it, in one capsule that holds everything. Built from an Embedded text input (``) — the typing, which grows with what is written — a File picker (``) and File items (``) — the attachments, as a strip at the top of the capsule — and Buttons (``): the send button, the stop button in its place, the attach button, and the product's own in its slots. It adds what ties them: the capsule, which is its own part and shows the typing area's focus on its edge; whether what it holds can be sent, and why not; the files it keeps; the counter; one live region; and the form's value. **It never sends**: `send` hands the text and the attachments to the product. Contract: specs/chat-composer.spec.json. ```html alternate_email ``` `layout="inline"` (the default) puts every action on the line being written; `layout="stacked"` keeps the send button on that line and puts everything else in a row beneath it, inside the capsule. A capsule narrower than `comp.chat-composer.layout.inline-min-width` is laid out stacked whatever `layout` says; a stacked composer with nothing for the row beneath is drawn as an inline one. Tab moves through it in the order it is drawn. Enter sends and Shift+Enter begins a new line; with `send-key="modifier"` Enter begins a new line. Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter send under both. An input method's Enter never sends, and neither does the return key of an on-screen keyboard: both are the embedded text input's to tell. A request by the keyboard while the message cannot be sent emits `sendblocked` with the reasons, unless there is simply nothing to send. `attachments="own"`: the composer keeps the files a person attaches — chosen, dropped on the capsule or pasted — and draws a File item for each (`attachment-form`: a tile with its picture for an image, a row for anything else); a refused file is a failed row with the product's sentence for its reason. `files` reads the kept files, `addFiles(files)` hands files over and answers with the refused, `clear()` empties the text and the files. `attachments="given"`: the File items are `` children the product adds on `select` and removes on an item's `remove`, each with its status and progress; nothing can be sent while one is uploading, or has failed and can be tried again. Form-associated: it submits the text under `name` and, while `attachments` is `own`, each kept file under `files-name`; after `send` — unless that was cancelled — it asks its form to submit, and then does not empty itself. slots.name: leading

slots.description: The product's own Buttons before the send button in the inline layout, and at the end of the row beneath the typing area in the stacked one. Laid out and never restyled.
slots.name: trailing

slots.description: The product's own Button in place of the attach button the chat composer brings. Exactly one; it opens the browser's picker. Not drawn while `attachments` is `none`.
slots.name: attach

slots.description: The product's own Button in place of the send button the chat composer brings. Exactly one; it sends, and is disabled while nothing can be sent.

slots.description: The product's own Button in place of the stop button the chat composer brings, shown in the send button's place while `sending` and `stoppable` are set. Exactly one.
slots.name: stop

slots.description: While `attachments` is `given`: the attachments, `<tanrei-file-item>` children, in order. Anything else is not drawn, and while `attachments` is `own` or `none` nothing here is.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: CCM-36: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, or are the product's own children, and take no part in a form.

members.name: value
members.description: The text. Setting it shows it and fires nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name. Required: the input draws no label and asks no Field for one, so this is the only name it has. Never drawn.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint drawn while the value is empty. Never the name. A multi-line input is as tall as the placeholder's lines, within `min-rows` and `max-rows`.

members.name: layout
members.description: Where the actions stand in the capsule. `inline` (the default, and every value it does not know): on the line being written — the attach button and the leading actions before the typing area, the counter, the trailing actions and the send button after it. `stacked`: the typing area and the send button on one line, and everything else in a row beneath them, inside the capsule. A capsule too narrow for inline is laid out stacked whatever this says; the number of lines never changes the layout.

members.name: minRows
members.description: The fewest lines a multi-line input is tall (`min-rows`). Anything below 1 is 1.

members.name: maxRows
members.description: The most lines the typing area grows to before it scrolls inside itself (`max-rows`). Given to the embedded text input as its `maxRows`, with a default of the chat composer's own: six lines. 0 sets no limit.

members.name: maxLength
members.description: The most user-perceived characters a message may hold (`max-length`); 0 is no limit. It refuses no edit and shortens no paste: text beyond it stays, is marked, and stops sending until the person has cut it.

members.name: counter
members.description: Draws the number of characters, and `maxLength` where one is set, before the trailing actions.

members.name: sendKey
members.description: What Enter does on a hardware keyboard (`send-key`). `enter` (the default, and every value it does not know): Enter sends and Shift+Enter begins a new line. `modifier`: Enter begins a new line and Ctrl+Enter or Command+Enter sends. Ctrl+Enter and Command+Enter send under both.

members.name: attachments
members.description: Whether files can be attached, and who holds them. `none` (the default, and every value it does not know): text alone. `own`: the chat composer keeps the files a person attached and draws a File item for each, and `send` carries them. `given`: the product gives the File items as children and the chat composer lays them out and keeps no file.

members.name: attachmentForm
members.description: The form of the File items the chat composer draws itself, while `attachments` is `own` (`attachment-form`). `auto` (the default, and every value it does not know): a tile with its picture for an image, a row for every other file. `tile`: every file a tile. `row`: every file a row, and no picture. A refused file is a row under every value.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether more than one file can be attached. Given to the file picker as its `multiple`; the default is true (`multiple="false"` says false).

members.name: accept
members.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

members.name: maxSize
members.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

members.name: sending
members.description: What was sent is on its way, or its answer is still arriving: the product's to set and to clear. While it is set nothing more can be sent; the typing area stays open.

members.name: stoppable
members.description: While `sending` is set, puts a stop button in the send button's place, which asks the product to stop what is under way (`stop`). Ignored while `sending` is not set.

members.name: blocked
members.description: The product's own reason that nothing can be sent now. The send button is disabled and the send key sends nothing; the product says why in its own words.

members.name: keepAfterSend
members.description: Keeps the text and the attachments after `send` (`keep-after-send`), for a product that clears them itself (`clear()`) once it knows the message arrived.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Nothing can be written, attached, removed or sent: every member and every Button in a slot is disabled. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

members.name: error
members.description: Draws the capsule in its error condition and exposes the typing area as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. It does not stop sending by itself: `blocked` does.

members.name: sendLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the send button the chat composer brings (`send-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ sendLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the button is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: stopLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stop button the chat composer brings (`stop-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ stopLabel })`).

members.name: attachLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the attach button the chat composer brings (`attach-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ attachLabel })`).

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.name: retryLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: typeErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused for its kind (`type-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileTypeErrorText })`).

members.name: sizeErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused for its size (`size-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileSizeErrorText })`).

members.name: countErrorText
members.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the sentence on the File item of a file refused because no more can be added (`count-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileCountErrorText })`).

members.name: announcement
members.description: A message assistive technology hears through the one live region when the product sets or changes it. Not drawn.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the text is submitted under.

members.name: sendable
members.description: Whether what it holds can be sent now, read-only: what the last `sendablechange` said.

members.name: clear
members.description:
CCM-15: empties the chat composer as it empties itself after `send` — the text, every file it keeps and every File
item it drew — for a product that set `keep-after-send` and now knows the message arrived. Emits nothing and
announces nothing. The product's own File items (`attachments="given"`) are the product's to remove.

members.name: files
members.description:
CCM-22: the files it keeps while `attachments` is `own`, in order, as the browser's own `File` handles: a new array
on each read. Never a refused file. Empty while `attachments` is `given` or `none`.

members.name: addFiles
members.description:
CCM-22: hands files over, as a product does whose own action in a slot makes a file — a photograph, a recording.
They are judged by its file picker (FPK-31) and are then an arrival: kept or refused, drawn and announced as a
choice is, with no event. Answers with the refused files and their reasons. While `attachments` is not `own` it
does nothing and is reported.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: CCM-36: a reset empties it, and emits nothing.

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback
members.description: CCM-40: the text is restored with the page; it begins with no file.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

events.name: sendablechange
events.description: Whether what the chat composer holds can be sent changed, or the reasons it cannot did: `detail.sendable`, and `detail.reasons` by name — `disabled`, `sending`, `blocked`, `empty`, `length`, `uploading`, `failed`. Bubbles. Never when it is first drawn.

events.name: sendblocked
events.description: The person asked to send by the keyboard while it could not be sent for a reason other than being empty or disabled; `detail.reasons` says why. Bubbles.

events.name: send
events.description: The person sent what the chat composer holds, by the send button or the keyboard, while it could be sent. `detail.value` is the text exactly as written; `detail.attachments` the kept `File`s (`own`) or the values of the File items that have not failed (`given`), in the order of the strip. Bubbles; cancelable — a cancelled one keeps the content and asks no form to submit.

events.name: select
events.description: Files were chosen in the picker, dropped on the capsule or pasted, and passed. Once per arrival; `detail.files` is a `File[]` — while `attachments` is `own`, the files newly kept. Bubbles.

events.name: reject
events.description: Files of one arrival were refused. Once, after `select` where both happen; `detail.files` is `{ file, reason }[]`, the reason `type`, `size` or `count`. Bubbles.

events.name: attachmentschange
events.description: While `attachments` is `own`: the kept files changed by what a person did — an arrival that kept a file, or a kept file removed by its File item. `detail.files` is the `File[]` now kept. Bubbles. Never for `addFiles()`, `clear()`, the emptying after `send` or a reset.

The person changed the text: the typing area's own `input` event, which leaves the element as it is. Read the new text from `event.target.value`. Never when `value` is set, and not when the chat composer empties itself after `send`.
events.name: input

events.description: The person activated the stop button while `sending` and `stoppable` were set. The product stops what is under way and sets `sending`. Bubbles.
events.name: stop

attributes.name: files-name
attributes.description: Web only: the name each kept file is submitted under, while `attachments` is `own` and the chat composer stands in a form. Without it no file is submitted.
The id of the form the chat composer belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.

attributes.name: attachments
attributes.description: Whether files can be attached, and who holds them. `none` (the default, and every value it does not know): text alone. `own`: the chat composer keeps the files a person attached and draws a File item for each, and `send` carries them. `given`: the product gives the File items as children and the chat composer lays them out and keeps no file.

attributes.description: The form of the File items the chat composer draws itself, while `attachments` is `own` (`attachment-form`). `auto` (the default, and every value it does not know): a tile with its picture for an image, a row for every other file. `tile`: every file a tile. `row`: every file a row, and no picture. attributes.description: Whether more than one file can be attached. Given to the file picker as its `multiple`; the default is true (`multiple="false"` says false).

declarations.description:
Asks one question that may have several answers among a few choices shown all at once. Built from a field group
(`<tanrei-field-group>`) and checkboxes (`<tanrei-checkbox>`): the field group's label, requirement, description and
one error around the product's own checkboxes, whose checked values the group holds as one list under one name, and —
where `select-all-label` is given — one more checkbox before the first that checks them all.

Contract: specs/checkbox-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-checkbox-group name="notify" label="Notify me by"><tanrei-checkbox
value="email" label="Email" checked></tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-checkbox-group>`: the checkboxes are the element's
children and stay in the product's light DOM; each stands for its `value`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the field group's own element around the
select-all checkbox and a slot, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every
`--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` and `--tanrei-comp-checkbox-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one
instance is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each of the eleven props of the frame is the
field group's, set on it unchanged. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field-group label="Notify me by">
<tanrei-checkbox name="notify" value="email" label="Email" checked></tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-field-group>` — for
checkboxes that each need a name of their own, a set that holds something else, or another rule for "all".

`value` is a property only: an array of the checked values, in the order of the checkboxes, followed by the entries
no checkbox stands for, which are kept; it is copied in and out. The first value is written as `checked` on the
children; once the product has set `value`, `value` decides. A person's switch — of one checkbox, or of the select-all
checkbox — sets `value` and fires `input` and one `change`; the checkboxes fire nothing of their own.

Form-associated: it submits one entry per value under `name` — what checkboxes of one name submit — and its
checkboxes submit nothing; a checkbox disabled by itself keeps its entry; a disabled group submits nothing. It
returns to its first value when the form is reset, is restored on navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>`, and
reports `valueMissing` while `required` and the list is empty, with `error-text`, else the required
text, else `label` as its message. It never sets `error` itself.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: every checkbox is a stop of its own, `focus()` goes to the first
enabled one, and the group, its name and its description are the field group's (`label`, never `aria-label`).
declarations.name: TanreiCheckboxGroup

declarations.description:
CHK-4: the condition drawn follows what the native input says, so what is drawn and what is announced cannot disagree:
indeterminate wins over checked, and `error` prefixes whichever applies. Later and more specific blocks win.

Lets people turn one independent choice on or off, show a parent choice that is only partly on, and mark a required
choice left unmade.

Contract: specs/checkbox.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-checkbox-*` tokens, one set per
condition (unselected, selected, indeterminate and their `error-` forms) and state: how a state looks is the active
design system's decision. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind
(`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value` (default "on") while checked, resets to its `checked` attribute,
honours `required` and a disabled `<fieldset>`, as a native checkbox does. It switches its own `checked` (and clears
`indeterminate`) before it fires `input` and `change`. The semantics are a native checkbox in the shadow root, named
by `label`; a click on the visible label toggles it.

Inside a `<tanrei-checkbox-group>` (CHK-23) it is a choice of that set: its `checked` is the group's — whether the
group's list holds its `value` —, it submits nothing itself whatever `name` it carries, `required` is not read, and
it fires no `input` and no `change`: the group fires one `change` with the list. A checkbox that carries no `value`
has none there (the "on" a bare checkbox submits is not read). Taken out of the group it is as it is anywhere.

declarations.description:
Collects a list of short texts — e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, keywords — typed one after another in one
field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`), the Text input it frames (`<tanrei-text-input>`) and one Chip
(`<tanrei-chip>`) for each entry, standing in the Text input's box before the typing part: each text the product's
check accepts becomes a chip that can be removed or taken back, and the list is the field's one value.

Contract: specs/chip-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-chip-field name="to" label="Recipients" type="email"
remove-label="Remove {entry}"></tanrei-chip-field>`, with `field.separators = [',', ';', ' ']` (or the attribute
`separators='[",", ";", " "]'`).

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the members' own elements, so it draws
nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`, `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-text-input-*` and `--tanrei-comp-chip-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one chip field is set apart by setting such a
property on this element. One level down, the same picture by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Recipients">
<tanrei-text-input type="email"><tanrei-chip slot="entries" kind="input" size="small" label="ada@example.com"
remove-label="Remove ada@example.com"></tanrei-chip></tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>`. What the chip field adds
to that: making entries, the keys among them, the one Tab stop, the announcements, and the list as one form value.

**An entry is made** of the typed text by Enter, by a separator the product lists (`separators`; none by default),
by focus leaving the field, and from pasted text that holds a separator or a line break. Each candidate is trimmed,
refused where the list holds the same text (`duplicate`) or is full (`maxEntries`: `limit`), and otherwise asked of
the product with `check`: `event.preventDefault()` refuses it (`invalid`), and `event.detail.reason = '…'` gives the
words. The chip field knows no grammar: what an e-mail address is, is the product's check. A refused text stays in
the typing part, and while it does the field is in error with the words of the refusal — `error` and `errorText`
themselves do not change.

**Keys.** The typing part is the one Tab stop. Backspace, or the arrow that points to the line's start, at the start
of the text moves focus to the last entry; there the arrows, Home and End move among the entries, Backspace and
Delete remove the one that has focus, Enter and Space take it back into the typing part to be changed, Escape and
Tab return to the typing part.

`value` is an array of strings (assign a new array to change it); the `value` attribute is read once, as a JSON
array. `inputValue` is the text being typed. Form-associated: it submits one value per entry under `name` — none
while the list is empty, never the typed text —, resets to the list it was first given, is restored on navigation,
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `required` is set and the list is empty.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the typing part, and its name is `label`.
declarations.name: TanreiChipField

members.description: CHF-24: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: value
members.description:
The entries, in the order they were made: the one value the chip field holds. Each is a text; none is empty. The
chip field writes it as the person makes, removes and takes back entries, and fires `change`. What the product
sets is shown as given and is not checked — assign a new array — and fires nothing; an entry that is empty or only
white space is left out. The `value` attribute is read once, as a JSON array of strings, and is what a form reset
returns to.

members.name: inputValue
members.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: separators
members.description:
The texts that end an entry when they are typed or found in what is pasted, as the product names them for what
its entries are: `[',', ';', ' ']` for e-mail addresses, `[',']` for keywords that may hold a space. The
attribute is read as a JSON array. Empty, the default: Enter and a line break alone make an entry — a name such as
"Lovelace, Ada" must not be cut in two by a default. A line break always ends an entry.

members.name: maxEntries
members.description: The most entries the list may hold (`max-entries`); 0 is no limit. An entry that would exceed it is refused with the reason `limit`; the typing part stays usable. It never cuts a list the product sets.

members.name: variant
members.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

members.name: size
members.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: type
members.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

members.name: placeholder
members.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

members.name: autocomplete
members.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: required
members.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

members.name: optional
members.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused by the product's check and the check gave no reason of its own (`invalid-text`). This field's own: it reads no word of the product's. Empty, `errorText` is shown.

members.name: duplicateText
members.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused because the list already holds the same text (`duplicate-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ duplicateEntryText })`); with neither, `errorText` is shown.

members.name: limitText
members.description: The error text shown while an entry was refused because the list holds `maxEntries` already (`limit-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryLimitText })`); with neither, `errorText` is shown.

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of each entry's remove action (`remove-label`): the whole name in your language, with the place `{entry}` that the chip field fills with that entry's text. This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryRemoveLabel })`); with neither the action is drawn, works and has no name.

members.name: addedText
members.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when one entry is made (`added-text`), with the place `{entry}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryAddedText })`); with neither nothing is said.

members.name: addedCountText
members.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when several entries are made at once (`added-count-text`), with the place `{count}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entriesAddedText })`); with neither, `addedText` is said for the last of them.

members.name: removedText
members.description: The sentence assistive technology is told when an entry is removed (`removed-text`), with the place `{entry}`: this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ entryRemovedText })`); with neither nothing is said.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name each entry is submitted under.

members.name: formResetCallback

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback

events.name: change
events.description: The list changed by the person: an entry was made, several were made from pasted text, one was removed, or one was taken back to be changed. `detail.value` (and the element's `value`) is the new list, `detail.added` and `detail.removed` what the act added and took away. Never fired when the product sets `value`, nor for typed text.

events.name: reject
events.description: A candidate entry was refused: `detail.text`, `detail.reason` (`invalid`, `duplicate` or `limit`) and `detail.message`, the words shown. Once for each refused candidate.

The user changed the value (typing, deleting, pasting, dictation, autofill, an input method); `value` is already the new one. A date or time field fires it when its value changes — its last segment is filled, a filled row is edited, or it is emptied — not for a segment that leaves the value empty. Never fired when the product sets `value`.
events.name: input

events.description: Asked once for each candidate entry, before it is made: `detail.text` and `detail.values`, the entries so far. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` refuses the candidate, and `detail.reason`, set by the listener, gives the words shown. Read when the event returns; an answer given later is not read.

events.description: The action key (Enter) was pressed in a single-line field. Cancelable: cancelling it keeps an enclosing form from being submitted.

attributes.description: The id of the form the chip field belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
value
attributes.description:
The entries, in the order they were made: the one value the chip field holds. Each is a text; none is empty. The
chip field writes it as the person makes, removes and takes back entries, and fires `change`. What the product
sets is shown as given and is not checked — assign a new array — and fires nothing; an entry that is empty or only
white space is left out. The `value` attribute is read once, as a JSON array of strings, and is what a form reset
returns to.

attributes.name: input-value
attributes.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: separators
attributes.description:
The texts that end an entry when they are typed or found in what is pasted, as the product names them for what
its entries are: `[',', ';', ' ']` for e-mail addresses, `[',']` for keywords that may hold a space. The
attribute is read as a JSON array. Empty, the default: Enter and a line break alone make an entry — a name such as
"Lovelace, Ada" must not be cut in two by a default. A line break always ends an entry.

attributes.name: max-entries
attributes.description: The most entries the list may hold (`max-entries`); 0 is no limit. An entry that would exceed it is refused with the reason `limit`; the typing part stays usable. It never cuts a list the product sets.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (CHP-7): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same functions
as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in debug builds.

Shows a compact choice, a suggested action or an item the user entered as a small labelled control.

Contract: specs/chip.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-chip-*` tokens, one set per variant, look
(plain, or `selected.` for a filter chip that is on) and state, and the `remove.` parts of an input chip's remove
action in its own states: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`).

`kind` decides what the chip does and its parts; `variant` only how it looks. An action chip is a button. A filter chip
is a button with a pressed state: activation switches `selected` and fires `change`, and when on it shows a check in
its leading position. An input chip has a remove action, a second button named by `removeLabel`, pressed by pointer,
touch or assistive technology and not a Tab stop: an input chip is one stop, and Backspace or Delete on it removes it,
which the chip tells assistive technology with `aria-keyshortcuts`. Both fire `remove` — the chip never removes itself
(the page does, and moves focus). By default the remove action reads as destructive (`destructiveRemove`; the attribute
`no-destructive-remove` turns it off): it looks the same at rest and takes the error color while it is hovered,
focused or pressed — a color only, never a change of name, glyph or size. The label is the visible text and the
accessible name; the icon (the `icon` slot) and the avatar (the `avatar` slot, input chips only) are decorative.

An action chip with `href` is a link and not a button (CHP-33): the shadow root holds an `<a href>` in place
of the `<button>`, drawn from the same tokens in every state. Enter activates it and Space does not; `click` fires
first and cancelling it cancels the navigation. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), draws the icon
set's `open_in_new` at the chip's inline end and reads `target-label` as the link's description. A filter chip and an
input chip take no destination.
declarations.name: TanreiChip
