members.name: kind
members.description: What the chip does: action (a button), filter (on or off) or input (an entered item the user can remove). Kind decides the role and the parts, not the look.

members.name: variant
members.description: Look: outlined sits flat on a plain surface; elevated is raised for chips over media or a busy background.

members.name: size
members.description: Visual height (small 24 / medium 32 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: selected
members.description: Whether a filter chip is on. Ignored unless `kind` is filter.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents interaction and removes the chip, and its remove action, from the focus order.

members.name: label
members.description: The visible text and the accessible name.

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of an input chip's remove action; it should name the item ("Remove Ada Lovelace"). Required when `kind` is input.

members.name: destructiveRemove
members.description:
Whether an input chip's remove action reads as destructive: the same at rest, the error color while hovered,
keyboard-focused or pressed. Set `no-destructive-remove` where removing loses nothing (a filter the user can add
back in one step). Color only: the name, glyph, size and behaviour are the same either way. Ignored unless `kind` is input.

members.name: removable
members.description:
Whether an input chip draws its remove action. Set `not-removable` for an entry that cannot be taken away now (a
read-only field's): no remove action is drawn, so none stands there doing nothing, none is a stop, Backspace and
Delete ask for nothing, and the chip is padded as one without a remove action (CHP-38). Ignored unless `kind` is input.

members.name: href
members.description:
The destination of an action chip: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the chip is a link and not a button
(CHP-33): the link role, an `<a href>` in the shadow root, activated by Enter and not by Space, drawn exactly as the
action chip it would otherwise be. Ignored unless `kind` is action; white space is no destination, and a
`javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported in debug builds (CHP-37).

members.name: target
members.description:
Where the destination opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which the chip marks
with the glyph `open_in_new` after its label and says through `targetLabel` (CHP-35). HTML's `_self` and `_blank`
are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`; `target="new"` adds `noopener` to it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates the chip as a person would — through its native button, or its anchor, so a link is followed — and does nothing while disabled.

events.name: change
events.description: A filter chip was activated; fired after its `click`, as a native checkbox does. `detail.selected` (and the element's `selected`) is the new value.

events.name: remove
events.description: The user asked to remove an input chip, with its remove action or with Backspace or Delete. The chip stays until the page removes it.

The chip itself was activated by pointer, touch, keyboard or assistive technology. Never fired by the remove action. A link chip fires it before the browser follows the address; `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_BEFORE_CSS
declarations.description: The stylesheet text of a block that is not upgraded, in the components' layer: `code.css` alone carries it, first.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: sizeBlock
declarations.description:
The members of the size axis (COD-2, COD-3): the code's text style, taken whole, and the two paddings. The weight is
named apart, because a syntax role adds its emphasis to it (COD-18).

declarations.name: variantBlock
declarations.description:
A look (COD-1): the container's fill, and the ground — the opaque color the gutter and the copy button's patch stand
on while code scrolls under them (COD-10, COD-13). A filled look's ground is its fill. The outlined look has none of
its own (its fill is transparent): it is read on whatever it is placed on, which a stylesheet cannot know, so the
ground is `--tanrei-code-block-ground` where the product names it and the surface color otherwise.

declarations.name: layoutBlock
declarations.description:
What the element's shadow styles change by its props, at the values of a block with no header and no copy button:
the padding above the first line (COD-3; COD-8 puts the header's own there) and the padding before and after the
lines (COD-10 widens the one at the copy button's side).

declarations.name: SYNTAX_ROLES
declarations.description:
The syntax roles a run may name (COD-18), besides `plain`: the values of the token axis `comp.code-block.syntax`,
as every design system has them. Data, not selectors: each is drawn by ONE rule from the two tokens that carry its
name — `syntax.color.<role>` and `syntax.emphasis.<role>`, a step of weight added to the code's own. The list is
held to the generated tokens twice: the build refuses to write `code.css` while it differs from the roles
`src/generated/tokens.css` names (scripts/build.js), and a role a layer ADDS to the axis gets the same
rule from `roleRule` — in the build of a product's own stylesheet, and in the element when it first meets a run of
that role whose tokens the cascade has.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_DRAWN
declarations.description:
A name these rules set on the block: a root whose cascade gives it draws the block's lines already, and the element
does not add the rules to it again (src/primitives/sheets.ts). No shadow style of the element sets it.

declarations.name: layered
declarations.description: Rules in the components' layer, as a stylesheet's text.

declarations.name: CODE_BLOCK_CSS
declarations.description: The stylesheet text: the rules in the components' layer, as `code.css` carries them and the element adopts them.

declarations.name: BARE_BLOCK_CSS
declarations.description:
A bare `pre` — rendered Markdown that the product did not wrap in the element: the filled look at the medium size
with the code's text, scrolling in its own box (COD-1 to COD-4, PRS-15). Declarations only: the build writes them
under prose's own `pre` (scripts/build.js).

declarations.description:
The open axes (COD-25): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in
debug builds. A variant a layer adds has no edge: only `outlined` draws one (COD-1).

Shows lines of code to read, compare and copy: in the code face, on a quiet fill or inside one hairline, scrolling inside itself or wrapping, with an optional header, line numbers, marked lines, a prompt and a copy button; given the code and its language it highlights the code by itself, in the system's syntax colors. Contract: specs/code-block.spec.json. The code stays in the document, as an ordinary `
`:

    
      
const sizes = ['small', 'medium', 'large'];

    

so it is there without script — for a reader whose script failed, for crawlers, for find-in-page — and the element
draws the frame around it. `@tanrei/web/code.css` draws a block that is not upgraded yet where the element will: its
fill, corners, paddings and face, the header's row with the title and the language label, the room of the copy
button, and — for lines written where the page was made — what stands beside them; nothing moves when the element
is defined. A block built by script sets `code` instead, and the element writes the `
`.

**It highlights by itself** (COD-19). Three sources of color, in this order: runs the document gives —
`` in the ``, or a `` written by `highlightToHtml` where
the page was made — are drawn as they are and never read again (COD-29); otherwise, while `highlight` is true and
`language` names a language the highlighter knows, the block imports `@tanrei/web/highlight` and colors the code
(COD-27); otherwise the code is plain. The code is drawn at once, plain; its colors arrive in one frame and move
nothing (COD-28). A role is one of `comment`, `keyword`, `string`, `constant`, `function`, `type`, `tag`, `property`,
`punctuation` — or one a design system added — colored from `--tanrei-comp-code-block-syntax-color-*` and weighted
from `…-syntax-emphasis-*`. `language` is not drawn: the header's words are `language-label`.

**Lines.** The element gives each line a box of its own — `` holding `` — by
moving the code's nodes and splitting text and runs at line breaks, without adding or removing a character of the
code; `[data-line]` children a highlighter already wrote are used as they are, and lines that `highlightToHtml`
wrote with the block's props are left untouched. Numbers, signs and the prompt are
drawn, not text: never selected, copied or read. A marked line's label (`highlighted-label`, `added-label`,
`removed-label`) is the one thing it adds for assistive technology, before the line.

The body is one focus stop, with the block's name, only while it can scroll; it is left to right in every layout,
and the frame mirrors. The outlined look is read on whatever it is placed on: where that is not the surface color,
name it in `--tanrei-code-block-ground`, which the gutter and the copy button's patch stand on while code scrolls
under them.

declarations.description:
Lets people set one color as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Color
input (`<tanrei-color-input>`) it frames: the box — a sample of the value, the value as text, a button that asks
for a picker — under the Field's label, or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it,
with the Field's help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one
control. It looks and measures like a text field.

Contract: specs/color-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-color-field name="brand" label="Brand color" value="#0f766e"
supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e." invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."
picker picker-label="Choose color"></tanrei-color-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-color-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one color field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's; `variant`, `size`, `value`, `invalid-text`, `picker` and
`picker-label` the color input's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Brand color"
supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."><tanrei-color-input name="brand" value="#0f766e"
invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e." picker picker-label="Choose color"></tanrei-color-input>
</tanrei-field>` — and the box alone, where a row or a column names the color, is `<tanrei-color-input>` with a
`label` of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (CLF-43): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the color input's — a number sign and six lowercase hexadecimal digits, or empty: a
value set as `0F766E` is read back as `#0f766e`, and one that is not a color as empty, with no event. The four
events are that input's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every
listener, and `pickerrequest` stays cancelable. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports what its color input reports: a missing value
while `required` is set and it is empty, and a bad input while a committed text is not a color. Enter in
the input presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input — never to the picker button —,
and its name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. It has two focus stops,
its input's: the input, then the picker button while it is shown. A press on the label row, on the box, on the
swatch or on a floating label focuses the input; a press on the help, the error text or the gap between a row and
the box does nothing.

members.description: CLF-44: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: required
members.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

members.name: optional
members.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]

The open axes (CLI-41): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported
in debug builds.

declarations.name: INSET
declarations.description:
CLI-43, FLD-26: how far the value's text stands from the input's own start edge — the padding beside the swatch, the
swatch and the gap, the sum the box itself is laid out by (`--_text-start` below) — and the text padding it keeps at
its end edge, with or without the picker button, as lengths written from the size's tokens so that the Field that is
told them resolves them where it stands: custom properties are inherited. A size a layer added falls back to the
default's token, as its styles do.

The box in which people set one color: a text value they can read, type and paste, a sample of it beside the text, a
button that asks for a picker and — in the looks that float one — its label inside the box. It looks and measures
like a text input. It has no label row, no help and no error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which
names it, describes it and marks it — or use `<tanrei-color-field>`, which is the two together.

Contract: specs/color-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a token: the box is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (CLI-45) — the swatch has the box's icon
size — and the swatch's shape and hairline from `--tanrei-comp-color-input-*`; the swatch's fill is the value itself; the picker
button is a `<tanrei-button>`, drawn from Button's own tokens.

```html
<!-- A row of a list of colors that names each: the box alone, named by its own label. -->
<tanrei-color-input label="Primary, tone 40" value="#0f766e" picker picker-label="Choose the color of Primary, tone 40"></tanrei-color-input>

<tanrei-field label="Brand color" supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e.">
  <tanrei-color-input name="brand" value="#0f766e" invalid-text="Enter six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."></tanrei-color-input>
</tanrei-field>
```

`value` is a number sign and six hexadecimal digits in lowercase (`#0f766e`) — an opaque sRGB color — or the empty
string for no color, and never anything else. The text is the person's: nothing typed is refused, replaced or
reformatted. It is read on every edit — six hexadecimal digits in either case, with or without the number sign, the
white space around them left out — and `value` is the color it reads as, or empty. `input` fires when that changes
`value`. When focus leaves or Enter is pressed the input commits: a color is rewritten in the value's own form and
`change` fires if the value differs from the one last committed; a text that is not a color is kept, marked as an
error and reported with `entryerror` — and to the Field that frames it, which shows `invalidText` (FLD-28).

With `picker`, a button at the end asks for a picker: it fires a cancelable `pickerrequest` and, unless that was
cancelled, presents the browser's own color picker. A pick is an edit by the person. The input draws no picker
surface of its own: a product that has one cancels the request, presents it and sets `value`.

Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes the Field's name, description and states — required, invalid, disabled — through
the connection every framed control uses (`src/primitives/field.ts`), and says what only it knows: that it draws the
label itself while its look floats one, how far its value's text is inset — past the swatch — and its own refusal
of a text that is not a color, with its words (CLI-43). Bare, `label` names it, and a filled or outlined input
draws that label floating.

It is a block as wide as its place, and exactly as tall as its box (CLI-44). It is a form-associated element: it
takes `name`, submits its value, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while its Field says it is required and `value` is empty, and
`badInput` while an entry error lasts.

It has no words of its own: `invalidText`, `pickerLabel` and `label` are the product's, in the product's language.

declarations.name: read
declarations.description:
CLF-18: reads a text. The white space before and after it is left out; what remains is a color when it is exactly
six hexadecimal digits in either case, with or without one number sign before them, and the color is those digits in
lowercase after a number sign. Nothing at all is `empty`; every other text — fewer or more digits, a three-digit
form, an alpha, a name, a functional notation, any other character — is `invalid`.

It is the one rule: what is typed, what is pasted and what the product sets are all read by it.

declarations.name: readCommitted
declarations.description:
CLI-19: reads a text as a commit does. The rule of `read()`, and besides it the three-digit form CSS has (#fff, fff):
the color whose six digits are each of the three written twice (#ffffff). Only a commit reads it: while the person
types, three digits are on their way to six and read as no color (CLI-18), so the swatch does not flash a color
that was never meant.

declarations.name: valueOf
declarations.description: CLF-17: the value a text makes — the color it reads as, or the empty string while it reads as no color.

declarations.name: isValue
declarations.description: CLF-16: `value` is in the value's own form — a color, or the empty string.

declarations.name: sameColor
declarations.description:
CLF-16: two values are the same color exactly when they are the same string, because the value has one form. (A text
in capitals or without its number sign is the same color as its lowercase form: compare what `valueOf()` gives.)

declarations.name: given
channels

type.text: [red: number, green: number, blue: number] | null

declarations.description: The three channels of a value, 0 to 255 each; null for no color.

declarations.name: fromChannels
declarations.description: A value from three channels: each is rounded and held within 0 and 255.

declarations.name: PICKER_START

declarations.name: picked
declarations.description:
CLF-29: a pick of the platform's picker, as the value holds it. The platform reports an opaque sRGB color as a number
sign and six digits (it has converted a pick with an alpha, or one outside sRGB, already); the field reads it by its
own rule, so capitals are taken too. A report it cannot read is no pick: null, and nothing changes.

Lets people find one value by typing, as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and
the Combobox (`<tanrei-combobox>`) it frames: the box with its list of options under the Field's label — or, in the
filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it — with the Field's requirement mark, its help and its
error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/combobox-field.spec.json.

```html
<tanrei-combobox-field name="city" label="City" required supporting-text="Where the order is sent." value="tokyo">
  <tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-combobox-field>
```

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-combobox-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one combobox field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the combobox's. One level down, the same by
hand: `<tanrei-field label="City" required supporting-text="Where the order is sent."><tanrei-combobox
name="city" value="tokyo"><tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>…</tanrei-combobox></tanrei-field>` — and
the box alone, where a label stands elsewhere, is `<tanrei-combobox>` with a `label` of its own.

**The options are this element's own children** — `<tanrei-option>`, optionally in `<tanrei-option-group>` — and
they stay there: nothing moves, copies or reads them here. They reach the combobox through a slot, and the combobox
reads them as its own, again whenever one is added, removed or changed (CBF-2).

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (CBF-1): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value`, `inputValue` and `open` are at every moment the combobox's (CBF-3): this element keeps no copy, so each is
the new one in every listener and where the combobox writes it with no event (a text given up on leaving). The four
events are the combobox's own, with this element as their target; `toggle` does not bubble. It dispatches none
itself.

Form-associated: it submits the committed value under `name` — never the text of an edit, and nothing while
disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports
a missing value while `required` is set and the value is empty. Enter with no option active presses the
default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row or on the box focuses the input;
a press on the label row while the list is open is a press outside the combobox, and closes the list; a press on
the help or the error text does nothing.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: CBF-4: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: required
members.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

members.name: optional
members.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label above it is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the combobox does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The committed choice: the chosen option's value, or, with `allowCustomValue`, a text the person typed that names no option. Empty while nothing is chosen. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: inputValue
members.description: The text in the input (`input-value`). The combobox writes it as the person types and when a value is chosen or restored; the product may set it, and reads it from `input` to load options.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value is shown, can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and neither the chevron nor the clear button is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the list is shown. The combobox opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it (to open on focus, for one). Ignored while the combobox is disabled or read-only or has nothing to show. Reflected.

members.name: allowCustomValue
members.description: False: the value is always one of the options, and a text that names none is given up when the person leaves. True: the options are suggestions, and a text that names none becomes the value as typed (`allow-custom-value`). Reflected.

members.name: filter
members.description: Who decides which options answer the text. `contains`: the combobox shows the options whose label contains what was typed, ignoring case, width and marks, and marks the match. `none`: it shows every option it is given and the product filters, on `input`. Reflected.

members.name: noChevron
members.description: Draws no chevron (`no-chevron`: the spec's `chevron`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for a field whose suggestions exist only for what was typed. The list then opens by typing and by the arrow keys alone. Reflected.

members.name: clearable
members.description: Draws a clear button while the text is not empty, for a combobox whose value may be none. Without it, emptying the text and leaving the field clears the value. Reflected.

members.name: clearLabel
members.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language (`clear-label`). Required while `clearable` is true.

members.name: status
members.description: What the product's source of options is doing: `idle`, `loading` (the status row shows a loading indicator and the list is marked busy) or `error` (the status row shows `statusText` as an error, announced at once). Reflected.

members.name: statusText
members.description: The status row's text, in the product's language (`status-text`), announced when it changes: a count, that loading failed, or, while loading, the loading indicator's name.

members.name: emptyText
members.description: Shown in the list while the text names nothing the combobox can show, `allowCustomValue` is false and no status is set (`empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ emptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no such row is drawn.

events.description: The person changed the text: the native, composed `input` of the text element as they type, delete, paste or an input method commits; one more when the clear button empties the text and when Escape restores it. `inputValue` is already the new text. events.description: The committed value changed by the person: an option was chosen, a custom text was committed, or the value was cleared; `value` is already the new one. `detail.value` and `detail.inputValue`. events.description: The list was opened or closed by the person, or closed by having nothing left to show; `open` is already the new one. `detail.open`, and for a close `detail.reason`: `select`, `commit`, `escape`, `outside`, `press`, `tab`, `focus-out`, `anchor-hidden` or `empty`. label
attributes.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

attributes.name: supporting-text
attributes.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

attributes.name: optional
attributes.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

attributes.name: required-mark
attributes.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

attributes.name: required-text
attributes.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

attributes.name: optional-text
attributes.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box that draws no label — the label above it is the row of the Field that frames it; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the combobox does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The committed choice: the chosen option's value, or, with `allowCustomValue`, a text the person typed that names no option. Empty while nothing is chosen. The `value` attribute is the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: input-value
attributes.description: The text in the input (`input-value`). The combobox writes it as the person types and when a value is chosen or restored; the product may set it, and reads it from `input` to load options.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value is shown, can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but cannot be changed: the list does not open and neither the chevron nor the clear button is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the list is shown. The combobox opens and closes itself and emits `toggle`; the product may also set it (to open on focus, for one). Ignored while the combobox is disabled or read-only or has nothing to show. Reflected.

attributes.name: allow-custom-value
attributes.description: False: the value is always one of the options, and a text that names none is given up when the person leaves. True: the options are suggestions, and a text that names none becomes the value as typed (`allow-custom-value`). Reflected.

attributes.description: Who decides which options answer the text. `contains`: the combobox shows the options whose label contains what was typed, ignoring case, width and marks, and marks the match. `none`: it shows every option it is given and the product filters, on `input`. Reflected.

attributes.description: Draws no chevron (`no-chevron`: the spec's `chevron`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for a field whose suggestions exist only for what was typed. The list then opens by typing and by the arrow keys alone. Reflected.

attributes.name: clearable
attributes.description: Draws a clear button while the text is not empty, for a combobox whose value may be none. Without it, emptying the text and leaving the field clears the value. Reflected.

attributes.name: clear-label
attributes.description: The clear button's accessible name, in the product's language (`clear-label`). Required while `clearable` is true.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: What the product's source of options is doing: `idle`, `loading` (the status row shows a loading indicator and the list is marked busy) or `error` (the status row shows `statusText` as an error, announced at once). Reflected.

attributes.name: status-text

attributes.name: empty-text

declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: INSET
declarations.description:
CMB-61, FLD-26: how far the combobox's input text stands from its own start edge, and the padding it keeps at its
end edge, as lengths — the sums the box itself is laid out by (`--_text-start`, `--_end` below), written from the
size's tokens so that the Field that is told them resolves them where it stands: custom properties are inherited.
Beside a leading glyph the text starts after the glyph's padding, the glyph and its gap; the clear button or the
chevron changes the end padding. A size a layer added falls back to the default's token, as its styles do.

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => `${variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT)}\n${optionVariantRules(PREFIX, value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT)}`, probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-${value}-container-color`, }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (CMB-56): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported
in debug builds.

Lets people find one value by typing: a box that looks and measures like a text input, with a list of options that
narrows as they type and that they choose from, or, where the product allows it, a value of their own. The bare
control: it has no label row and no message of its own.

Contract: specs/combobox.spec.json. The options are `<tanrei-option>` children, optionally in
`<tanrei-option-group>` elements (the pair a select holds too); the combobox reads them — and reads them again when
they change — and renders the rows itself. A `<slot>` among its children stands for the elements assigned to it, so
that an element composed around it passes its own children on as the options. Every visual value is a token: the box is
drawn from `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (CMB-63), and the list and the
status row from `--tanrei-comp-combobox-*` — the list's hold the menu's values and the status row's the search's, in
every shipped design system.

```html
<tanrei-field label="City">
  <tanrei-combobox name="city" value="tokyo">
    <tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option>
    <tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option>
  </tanrei-combobox>
</tanrei-field>
```

In a form it is framed: by a Field, as above, or as `<tanrei-combobox-field>`, which is that pair as one element.
The Field gives it its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states, and draws the label
row, the requirement mark, the help and the error; the combobox says back that it draws the label itself where its
look floats one (`filled`, `outlined`), where its input text starts and ends, and that it is drawn focused for as
long as its list is open (`src/primitives/field.ts`). Bare — a filter in a toolbar, a cell of a table — it is named
by its own `label`, which a stacked combobox does not draw.

It holds two things: `value`, the committed choice, and `inputValue`, the text in the input. Typing changes the text,
opens the list and filters it (`filter="contains"`; with `filter="none"` the product filters, on `input`); a press on
an option or Enter on the active one chooses; leaving the box resolves the text — a typed label chooses its
option, any other text is kept as the value (`allow-custom-value`) or given up. The value changes only by a choice,
a commit or the clear button.

It is a block as wide as its place, with no width of its own. It is a form-associated element: it takes `name`,
submits `value` (never an uncommitted text), resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while the Field that frames it says it is required and `value` is
empty. It never validates beyond that, and is never required by itself.

The pattern is the editable combobox with a list box: focus stays in the input while the list is open and one
option at most is the active one (`aria-activedescendant`). While an input method composes, every key is its own.

members.name: text
members.description: The text to copy, exactly as it will be pasted. Plain text only.

members.name: label
members.description: What the button does, in your language ("Copy", "Copy link"): the accessible name of the icon-only form and the visible text of the labelled one. Required.

members.name: copiedLabel
members.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the text has been copied ("Copied"). Required.

members.name: failedLabel
members.description: What is announced, and shown in the labelled form, when the browser refuses the copy ("Could not copy"). Required.

members.name: iconOnly
members.description: True draws the glyph alone, named by `label`. False (`icon-only="false"`) draws the glyph and the label as text.

members.name: labelWidth
members.description:
How wide the labelled form's text box is. `widest`, the default, keeps it as wide as the widest of its three texts
at all times, so the button never changes its width (CPY-7). `fit` makes it as wide as the text it shows, and eases
its width to the new text when the form changes (CPY-19). Ignored while icon-only.

members.name: variant
members.description:
The Button variant it is drawn as — `filled`, `tonal`, `elevated`, `outlined` or `text`. The default, text, is the
quiet icon action beside what it copies; a copy that is a view's main action takes another.

members.name: size
members.description: The Button size it is drawn at: `small` (32), `medium` (40) or `large` (56).

members.name: disabled
members.description: Prevents the copy; the button is drawn and exposed as a disabled Button.

declarations.description:
Lets a person choose a date, a time, or a date and time — or a span of any of them — from a Calendar and time wheels
or a clock dial, in a dialog or in a surface that drops down from a field.

Contract: specs/date-time-picker.spec.json. `modal` (the default) is a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with
`showModal()` — `::backdrop` is the scrim, everything else is inert, focus is trapped — with a start-aligned title row,
the pending value (in a mode with a date) and Cancel and OK; the choice is pending until OK. `docked` is a manual
popover in the top layer, placed below the element whose id is `anchor` with the menu's placement (flipped above when
there is more room there, shifted to stay in the viewport, following the anchor); it is not modal: Tab and focus
leaving close it, and a docked picker that sets a date only commits by choosing it. Both move focus in when they open
and give it back when they close.

The picker never closes itself: it fires `close` with a reason and you set `open` to false. When one activation
commits a choice, the element takes the new `value` (or `start` and `end`) and fires `change` before `close`.

Values are the strings of `<input type=date>`, `type=time` and `type=datetime-local`: "2026-09-17", "19:30",
"2026-09-17T19:30" — no seconds, no time zone. The date is a `<tanrei-calendar>`; the time is set on two wheels (spin
buttons that also take a typed number: press a wheel's chosen value, or type a digit) or on a clock dial with an hour
and a minute selector, chosen by two icon-only `<tanrei-tabs variant="secondary">` at the end of the title row while
the design system offers both (`comp.date-time-picker.time.entry-modes`) — the keyboard glyph for the wheels, the
clock face for the dial, `wheelsLabel` and `dialLabel` their accessible names. They are the picker's only tabs. The
period of a 12-hour time (AM, PM) is a part of the time, after the minute or — where the locale writes it first —
before the hour: a third wheel of two rows in the wheels mode, and in the dial mode a narrow selector that shows the
pending period and changes to the other when pressed; either is a spin button of two values named `periodLabel`, and
neither is ever drawn as selected. The two ends of a range that has a time are two range fields joined by an en dash
("9:00 AM – 5:30 PM") across the whole time section, with no word for start or end; the one the wheels or the dial set
is drawn as selected, and pressing the other sets it. Names, digits, forms, the separator and the preferred clock come from `Intl` for `locale`
(without it, the nearest `lang`, then the browser's language). Every visual value comes from
`--tanrei-comp-date-time-picker-*` tokens; the calendar, the tabs and the Buttons keep their own. The `inline`
attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open surface in place without the overlay's behaviour.

declarations.description:
Presents what is known about one thing as named facts — a quiet term and the value that answers it — with the terms in one column beside their values, above them, or under a large figure. An order, a file, an account, a component; the few numbers a screen opens with. It is laid out by its own width and is never a control. Contract: specs/description-list.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the product's own native `
`, which stays in the document and is never given a role — the description list a screen reader, a crawler and a page without script meet is the browser's own. ```html
Category
Actions
Owners
Aiko Tanaka
Samir Haddad
Status
 ``` A fact is a `
` around one `
` and its `
`s. The term and each value hold text or any view of the product's; a fact may have several values, and a value may be empty. A `
` without groups — `
` and `
` as its children, as some Markdown renderers write it — is drawn in one column, inline or stacked; `columns` and the stat layout need the groups. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/description-list.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-description-list-*` token — which draws the list before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds the one thing a stylesheet cannot say: an inline list whose values would be left less than `comp.description-list.column.min-width` draws its terms above their values. The element measures the widest term and writes that width as a container query of the list, so the browser itself draws the other form as the list is resized. Without the script such a list wraps its terms instead. The list takes no input and emits no event.
declarations.name: TanreiDescriptionList

slots.description: The native `<dl>`: one `<div>` per fact around a `<dt>` and its `<dd>`s. It is a child in the document, not a slotted node: the element has no shadow root.

members.name: layout
members.description:
How a fact is drawn. `inline`: the term beside its value, every term in one column as wide as the widest term; the
list draws its terms above their values by itself while it is too narrow for that. `stacked`: the term above its
value, for long values or long terms, and for facts in several columns. `stat`: the value first, as a large
figure, with the term under it as its label.

members.name: columns
members.description: The most columns of facts the list draws in the stacked and stat layouts; it draws fewer while it is too narrow for that many, and never more than it has facts. An inline list is one column.

members.name: density
members.description: How close the facts are and how large their text is: regular for facts a person reads, compact for facts a person scans. A design system may add values.

members.name: separation
members.description: How a fact is told from the fact below it: `divider` is one hairline, `gap` empty space and no line; `auto` takes `comp.description-list.separation`, the design system's answer.

declarations.description:
Stops a person for a decision or a few details that the task cannot go on without, in a surface that dims and blocks
everything behind it and always offers at least one answer, until one is chosen or the dialog is dismissed.

Contract: specs/dialog.spec.json. A native `<dialog>` in the shadow root, opened with `showModal()` while `open` is
true: in the top layer over `::backdrop` (the scrim, `comp.dialog.scrim.color`), with everything else inert and the page
held from scrolling. Focus goes to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, or to the dialog itself, stays inside it
(Tab wraps), and returns where it was when the dialog closes. It is an operated modal overlay.
Centred in the window, or at the bottom of a window narrower than `comp.dialog.compact.window-width` (DLG-17).

While `closedby` is not `none`, Escape, the platform's back and a press on the scrim fire `cancel`, whose
`detail.reason` says which (`escape`, `back`, `scrim`). It is cancelable: the dialog then closes itself unless you
call `preventDefault()`, as a native `<dialog>` does. Actions never close it: close it from their handlers with
`open = false`. `close` follows every close.

A dialog has no close button (DLG-28): it asks for a decision, and its way out without one is a dismissive action
(Cancel, or Close where there is nothing to cancel). Content that needs only a way out belongs in a side sheet or a
bottom sheet. `width` is `content` (the default: as wide as its widest part, between the minimum and maximum width)
or `small`, `medium` or `large` (`comp.dialog.width.*`), never wider than the window less its margins; a compact
window places every width alike.

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive`, placed as a
full-width button group places them: dismissive at the start and confirming at the end of a row, confirming on top of
a column when they do not fit in a row. Focus and assistive technology follow that order. A Button without a
`variant` attribute takes the dialog's (`comp.dialog.actions.variant`, tonal in the default system).

When the parts do not fit, the supporting text and the content scroll between the header and the actions, with a
divider below the header and one above the actions (DLG-11): for as long as that part scrolls while
`divider-visibility` is `always` (the default system's), only while content lies beyond each line while it is
`scroll`; `auto` takes `comp.dialog.divider.visibility` (DLG-24).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-dialog-*` tokens.

Contract: specs/divider.spec.json. The line's color, thickness, inset and the lengths of its dots, dashes and wave are
`--tanrei-comp-divider-*` tokens; one divider may be given a thickness of its own (`thickness`, DIV-16), which also
scales the pattern lengths it takes from tokens, so a thicker dotted, dashed or wavy line keeps its proportions. The divider has no margin of its own (DIV-2): put the space around it in the layout
that places it. It spans its container's inline size when horizontal (in block flow, a flex column or a grid) and its
container's block size when vertical (in a flex row or a grid, which stretch it; elsewhere give it a block size).

`aria-hidden="true"`; with `decorative="false"` (or the property set to false) it is `role="separator"` with its
`aria-orientation`. It is never focusable.

declarations.description:
Wraps any part of a screen so that files can be dropped anywhere on it, while what it holds is used exactly as
without it: it draws nothing at rest and adds no hover, no press, no focus stop and no role (DRZ-1, DRZ-2). While
files are dragged over it, one overlay covers it and says they can be dropped (DRZ-4); on the drop it judges them by
the File picker's rule and hands over what passed and what was refused (DRZ-9). It keeps nothing (DRZ-10), and it is
never the only way to add a file: the page also has a File picker or a File upload (DRZ-13).

Contract: specs/drop-zone.spec.json. `<tanrei-drop-zone multiple accept="video/*" drop-text="Drop videos to upload
them"> … the screen … </tanrei-drop-zone>`. The content stays in the product's light DOM and is laid out by styling
the host, which is `display: block`, `position: relative` and one stacking context of its own (DRZ-6).
`select` and `reject` carry the File picker's details, so one listener serves both; `judge(files)` judges files that
came another way and emits nothing (DRZ-15).

Contract: specs/fab-menu.spec.json. The toggle is a native `<button>` in the shadow root, drawn as a collapsed main
action button of the variant and size: it says it opens a menu (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), and while open takes the
variant's open look, round corners and the close glyph. The items are `<tanrei-fab-menu-item>` children, presented as
a column above the toggle in a manual popover — the top layer, so nothing clips them and no content moves — with role
`menu`. The FAB menu is an operated overlay that is not modal: it moves focus to the first item when it
opens (to the last, the one nearest the toggle, when Up Arrow opened it) and back to the toggle when it closes, never
traps focus and draws no scrim. It never opens or closes itself: set `open` from `toggle`, and to false from `close`.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-fab-menu-*` tokens: per variant three looks (the closed toggle, the open
toggle, the items), each in every state. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's
choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far corners ease is its amount.

The element does not position itself (FBM-12): it is inline, at the toggle's size, and the page places it — as a main action button.
The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open items in place above the toggle instead: with
their elevation, without the top layer, open motion, focus on opening or light dismiss (FBM-13).

Names a set of controls that answer one question — checkboxes, switches, or fields that belong together — with a
label that can say the set is required or optional, a description, and one error for the set, and lays the controls
out in a column or a row. It frames the set and never selects, moves focus or holds a value.

Contract: specs/field-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-field-group label="Notify me by"><tanrei-checkbox label="Email">
</tanrei-checkbox>…</tanrei-field-group>`: the controls are the elements of the default slot. They stay in the
product's light DOM, so each keeps its place in a `<form>`, its `name` and `value` and its events; the group is not
form-associated, holds no value and emits no event. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` token.

The shadow root holds a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` around the slot, so the controls are inside the group the
label names. A group has neither a required nor an invalid state: its description is `supporting-text`, then
`error-text` while `error` is true, then the requirement in words (`required-text`, `optional-text`); `error` puts
each checkbox it holds in the checkbox's own error condition and gives it the error text as its description. A
switch, which has no error condition, stays as it is drawn, and a field keeps the error the product gave it.
`disabled` disables every control. The group gives these through the composed `tanrei-field-connect` event a control
asks with (`src/primitives/field.ts`), or as attributes on any other element, and takes back exactly what it gave.

It answers no press and no key and adds no stop to the focus order.

`kind="radio-group"` (FGR-25) makes the same element the radio group of the radio buttons it holds — a set of radio
buttons of one `name`, written by hand, or the radio buttons of the `<tanrei-radio-group>` built around it: the
`<fieldset>` carries the radio group's role with `aria-required` while the set is required, `aria-invalid` while
`error` is true and `aria-orientation`, and `required-text` is left out of its description, because the state says
it. Nothing that is drawn changes, and the group still holds no value, moves no focus and handles no key: selection,
the arrow keys and the one tab stop stay the radio buttons' own group's.

declarations.description:
Frames one control with what a form gives every field: a label above it that can say the control is required or
optional, a line of help, and the reason a value was refused, each tied to the control for assistive technology. It
is a frame, never a control.

Contract: specs/field.spec.json. `<tanrei-field label="Volume"><tanrei-slider></tanrei-slider></tanrei-field>`: the
control is the one element in the default slot. It stays in the product's light DOM, so it keeps its place in a
`<form>`, its `name` and `value`, its events and its styles; the field is not form-associated, holds no value and
emits no event. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-field-*` token.

The label names the control; the help describes it, with the error text after it while the field is in error and
`optional-text` after that while the control is optional. They are given as values, because an id cannot be referenced across a shadow root: a Tanrei
control asks for them (the composed `tanrei-field-connect` event; `src/primitives/field.ts`) and writes them on the
element that carries its semantics, its own `label` winning; any other element receives `aria-label` (only where it
has no name of its own), `aria-description`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and, where it has the property,
`disabled`. The field takes back exactly what it gave when the element leaves the slot.

`required` exposes the control as required and draws the required mark beside the label — a small filled tag, an
asterisk or nothing, as the design system or `required-mark` says; `optional` draws the optional tag, and is ignored
while `required` is set. Neither validates: `error` is the product's to set, and `error-text` says what is wrong in words. While
the field is in error the error text takes the help's place, so a form in error is no taller than at rest; a design
system whose `--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement` is `append` keeps the help and draws the error text below
it. A disabled field draws its requirement tag as a tag inside something disabled. An error that appears while
focus is inside the field is announced once, politely — the error text alone, never the help again.

A press on the label moves focus to the control and never operates it; a press on the help, the error or the count
does nothing. A control that names itself (a checkbox with its own label) takes a field with an empty `label`, which
then adds help and an error only. A control that is a field already — a composed field such as
`<tanrei-text-field>`, which is this element around `<tanrei-text-input>`, or anything with a `supportingText` of its
own — needs no field.

A control may say of itself what only it knows, through the same connection (`src/primitives/field.ts`): that it
draws the label itself, floating in its own box — the field then draws no label row and gives the control the name,
whether it is hidden, and an asterisk or none for a required one (FLD-25); how far its content is inset — the
supporting row starts and ends there (FLD-26); and that it refused what was entered, with its words — the field is
then in its error condition and shows them as its error text (FLD-28); and that it is drawn focused though focus is elsewhere — a
combobox or a select for as long as its list is open — so that the field's rows are drawn focused with it (FLD-13).
`count-text` is a count about the control's value as it is to
be drawn ("12/40"), at the end of the supporting row: the field draws it, never counts, and keeps it from assistive
technology, which hears the count from the control (FLD-27). `value-text` is the control's present value in words
("40 %"), at the end of the label row, for a control whose value cannot be read from the control itself (a slider):
the field draws it, never reads or formats a value, and keeps it from assistive technology, which hears the value
from the control (FLD-29, FLD-30).

declarations.description:
Shows one file: a glyph that says its format, or a small picture of it; its name; a second line with what the
product says of it — its format, its size, where its sending stands, what went wrong; a bar while it is sent; and
the actions to take it back and to try it again. As a row of a column of files (`form="row"`, the default) or as a
tile of a strip of pictures (`form="tile"`, a box of `width` by `height`). **It never reads, keeps or sends the
file** (FIT-7, FIT-33): what it shows is what its props say.

Contract: specs/file-item.spec.json. `<tanrei-file-item name="brief.pdf" size-text="820 KB"
remove-label="Remove"></tanrei-file-item>`; a tile: `<tanrei-file-item form="tile" preview width="160" height="90"
name="floor-plan.png"></tanrei-file-item>`. `progress` absent is null: the bar is drawn as under way.

The glyph is chosen by the file's format — `media-type`, else the end of `name` — in ten kinds (FIT-5); `glyph`
names another of the icon set, and the `icon` slot holds one the set does not have. With `preview` the picture at
`preview-src` stands in the glyph's place, or — for an image — a picture of `file` (a `File`, a property and never an
attribute), for which the element makes one object URL when it first comes near the viewport and revokes it when it
is taken out of the page, given another file or no longer asked for the picture. Until a picture can be drawn, and
where it cannot, the glyph stands there. A picture that moves is played by the browser's image element: give a still
`preview-src` where a strip must not move.

The body — the glyph or the picture, and the texts — is a button with `interactive` (it emits `click`) and a link
with `href`; the two actions stand beside it, never inside it, and emit `remove` and `retry`. The element
removes nothing and changes no status: whoever holds it does. `readonly` draws no action; `disabled` disables them
and the body and leaves what is shown as it is.

Alone it is a group named by `name`. A component that holds it as an item of a list of its own — a File upload —
says so through an internal channel, and gives it there what every one of its rows shares.

Without script, and until the element is defined, nothing is drawn: the name is an attribute.

members.name: form
members.description: How the file is shown. `row`: one line across the width its layout gives — for a column of files. `tile`: a box of `width` by `height` holding the picture or the glyph, the texts beneath it and the actions at its corner — for a strip of pictures. Anything else is `row`.

members.name: value
members.description: What identifies the file to the product: given back by `click`, `remove` and `retry`.

members.name: name
members.description: The file's name as the person knows it ("report-2026.pdf"). The file item's name for assistive technology in every form, also where it is not drawn. Empty, it is read from `file.name`.

members.name: mediaType
members.description: The file's kind as the browser reports it ("image/png"), from which the glyph is chosen (`media-type`). Empty, it is read from `file.type`, and then from the end of `name`.

members.name: glyph
members.description: The name of a glyph of the icon set, drawn in place of the one the file's format would choose. Empty lets the format choose.

members.name: formatText
members.description: The file's format in the product's words ("PDF"), drawn first on the second line (`format-text`). Empty draws none.

members.name: sizeText
members.description: The file's size as text, formatted by the product for the reader's locale ("1.2 MB"); the `size-text` attribute. Empty draws none.

members.name: status
members.description: Where the file stands: `pending`, `uploading` (the bar is drawn), `done` or `error` (`errorText` says why). Anything else is `pending`.

members.name: statusText
members.description: The status in the product's words ("Waiting", "Uploading", "Uploaded"), drawn last on the second line; the `status-text` attribute.

members.name: progress
members.description: How far the sending has come, from 0 to 1, while the status is uploading. Null (no attribute) draws the bar as under way.

members.name: errorText
members.description: Why the file failed and what to do, in the product's words; drawn in the status's place while the status is error (`error-text`), in every form, and never cut.

members.name: retryable
members.description: Whether a failed file offers the retry action.

members.name: preview
members.description: Whether a picture of the file is drawn in the glyph's place: the one at `preview-src`, or — for an image — a picture of `file`. False draws the glyph, also for an image.

members.name: previewSrc
members.description: The address of a picture of the file (`preview-src`): a small rendition the product's server made. With `preview` it is drawn for a file of any format. Empty, the picture comes from `file`.

members.name: fit
members.description: How the picture fills its box. `cover`: it fills the box and is cut at the edges. `contain`: the whole picture inside the box, on the box's ground. Anything else is `cover`.

members.name: nameHidden
members.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

members.name: width
members.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

members.name: height
members.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

members.name: interactive
members.description: Makes the body — the glyph or the picture, and the texts — one button that emits `click`, for a product that opens the file where it is. The actions stay their own.

members.name: href
members.description: The destination: the address of the file. Not empty, the body is a link to it whether `interactive` is set or not: an `<a href>`, followed by Enter and not by Space.

members.name: target
members.description: Where the destination opens. `same`: where the person is. `new`: a new tab, which a row marks and `target-label` says. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words (`target-label`).

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.name: retryLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: disabled
members.description: The actions are disabled and the body cannot be pressed. What the file item shows of the file stays as it is and stays readable.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The file is shown and cannot be taken back: no remove action and no retry action is drawn (`readonly`). The body can still be pressed where `interactive` or `href` says so.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `rel`. `noopener` is added while `target` is `new`. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: forwarded to the anchor's `download` (the file name; empty for the address's own), so that the link saves the file in place of opening it. Ignored without `href`.

members.name: file
members.description: The file itself, as the browser's own handle: what a picture is drawn of (with `preview`, for an image), what `name` and `media-type` are read from where they are empty, and what a File upload submits for the item. A property, never an attribute; no byte of it is read.

members.name: focus
members.description: Moves focus to the file item's first stop: its body where that is pressable, else its retry action, else its remove action.

events.name: retry
events.description: The person asked to try a failed file again. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value.

events.name: remove
events.description: The person asked to take this file back. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value. Whoever holds the file item removes it.

The body of a pressable file item was activated. Bubbles and is composed; `detail.value` is the file item's value. A link fires it before the browser follows the address; `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose files through the browser's own picker — from the product's Button and, where there is room, from
a place files can also be dragged onto — says the limits in words before the choice, judges what was chosen against
them, and hands over what passed and what was refused. **It keeps nothing, lists nothing and takes no part in a
form** (FPK-7): whoever holds the files shows them — a `<tanrei-file-upload>` does, with a list and a form value.

Contract: specs/file-picker.spec.json. `<tanrei-file-picker accept=".json" constraints-text="…"><tanrei-button
slot="trigger" variant="outlined">Choose a file</tanrei-button></tanrei-file-picker>`. `layout="drop-area"` draws a
bounded place around the trigger that takes a drop and opens the picker when pressed. `select` carries the files of
one choice or one drop that passed `accept`, `max-size` and the count of one choice; `reject` the ones that did not,
each with a reason that is a name and not words (`type`, `size`, `count`). `judge(files)` judges files that came
another way — pasted, dropped elsewhere — and emits nothing. A second choice is judged as if it were the first.

`selection-text` stands beside the trigger in the button layout: what is chosen now, written by whoever holds it.
Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes the field's label as its group's name, and gives its trigger the field's help,
error, requirement and `disabled`.

Without script, and until the element is defined, the trigger is a button that opens nothing: a page that must take
files where script does not run writes a native `<input type="file">` in its own form.
declarations.name: TanreiFilePicker

members.name: layout
members.description: How choosing is offered: `button` is the trigger alone with the line of limits below it; `drop-area` is a bounded place around the trigger that also takes files dragged onto it and opens the picker when pressed. Anything else is `button`.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether more than one file can be chosen at a time. False: the picker offers one, and a drop of several is refused whole.

members.name: accept
members.description: The kinds of file that are taken: extensions with their dot (".pdf") and media types ("image/png", a family as "image/*"). The attribute is a comma-separated list, as a native file input's. Empty takes every kind.

members.name: maxSize
members.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes (`max-size`). Null sets no limit. Judged from the size the browser reports; the file is not read.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The most files one choice or one drop may bring, while `multiple` is set (`max-files`). Null sets no limit; zero refuses every file — the room a full list has left. Nothing is counted across choices.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the file picker as a group ("Photo"). Not drawn. Leave it empty inside a Field, whose label names the group; left empty elsewhere, no group is exposed and the trigger stands as the button it is.

members.name: judge
members.description:
FPK-31: judges files that came neither through the picker nor onto the area — pasted, dropped on another part of
the page, made by the product — as one arrival, by the rule a choice is judged by. Answers with the files that
passed and the refused files with their reasons, each in the order given. Emits nothing and keeps nothing. Works
while disabled: disabled stops the person, not the product.
