declarations.description:
Lets people choose files and shows what was chosen. Built from a File picker (`<tanrei-file-picker>`) — the trigger,
the drop area, the limits in words, the judging of a choice — and File items (`<tanrei-file-item>`), one for each
file, in a column of rows or a strip of tiles; it adds the state that ties them: which files are kept, the room that
is left, one form for all its items, one message for many changes, where focus goes after a removal, and the form's
value. **It never uploads**: it opens no connection and reads no byte of a file (FUP-7).

Contract: specs/file-upload.spec.json. Who holds the rows is `rows`, and the product says which.

`rows="own"`, the default: the element keeps the chosen files and makes a file item for each itself, so a plain form
works by placing it — `<form><tanrei-file-upload name="attachments" multiple remove-label="…"><tanrei-button
slot="trigger" variant="outlined">Choose files</tanrei-button></tanrei-file-upload></form>`. With `multiple` a second
choice adds and `max-files` counts the files kept; without it a file that passes takes the place of the one kept. The
same file (name, size, time of last change) is kept once. A refused file is a failed row with the product's sentence
for its reason (`type-error-text`, `size-error-text`, `count-error-text`, else `setWords`), is not kept, and leaves
when it is removed, when files next arrive or on `clear()`. The remove action removes. `files` reads the kept files,
`add(files)` hands files over and answers with the refused, `clear()` empties, and `formatSize` — a property — writes
a row's size; without it none is drawn. A kept file's row shows no status and no progress: the element sends nothing.

`rows="given"`: the rows are `<tanrei-file-item>` children the product adds on `select` and removes on a row's
`remove`, each with its status, progress and error; the element adds, changes and removes none and keeps no file —
for a product that sends files itself.

Every row is of one form: `item-form` (`row`, `tile`), `item-preview`, `item-fit`, `item-name-hidden`, `item-width`,
`item-height`, with `remove-label`, `retry-label` and `disabled`, are given to every file item it holds — the
product's own included — through an internal channel; a product's item that says one of them otherwise is drawn as
the file upload says. The picture of an image row is made and released by its file item, never by this element.

`select` carries the files that passed `accept`, `max-size` and the count and found room, `reject` the ones that did
not, each with a reason that is a name and not words (`type`, `size`, `count`); while `rows` is `own`, `change` then
carries the files now kept. None is emitted for what the product did itself (`add()`, `clear()`, a reset, a change
of `rows`). The file picker's own two events do not leave the element.

Form-associated: under its `name` it submits the kept files, in order — or, while `rows` is `given`, the `file` of
every row that has one; it is invalid for its form while `required` and there is none. A reset empties the kept
files and changes nothing of the product's rows. Nothing is restored with a page. Inside a `<tanrei-field>` it takes
the field's label, help, error, requirement and `disabled`.

The rows are the items of a `<tanrei-list>` in the shadow root — a column, or with `item-form="tile"` lines that
wrap. With `reorderable` people can put them in another order (FUP-59): every row gets the List's handle, the whole
row can be dragged, and the handle offers the moves in a menu and to the keyboard. While `rows` is `own` the file
upload reorders the files it keeps and fires `change`; while it is `given` it fires `move` and you move your file item.

One level down, the same by hand: a `<tanrei-file-picker>` and `<tanrei-file-item>`s the product arranges, alone or
as the content of a List's items.

Without script, and until the element is defined, the trigger is a button that opens nothing and no row is drawn: a
page that must take files where script does not run writes a native `<input type="file">` in its own form.

members.name: itemNameHidden
members.description: In a tile: the name is not drawn beneath a tile that draws a picture (`name-hidden`). It stays the file item's name for assistive technology, and is drawn all the same wherever no picture is. Not read in a row.

members.name: itemWidth
members.description: In a tile: the width of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) makes it as wide as it is high.

members.name: itemHeight
members.description: In a tile: the height of the box, in CSS pixels. Null (no attribute) reads the token of a tile's height.

members.name: moveBeforeLabel

members.name: moveAfterLabel

members.name: moveToEndLabel

members.name: removeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the remove action (`remove-label`): your sentence with the place `{name}`, which the file item fills with the file's name ("Remove {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ removeLabel })`).

members.description: The accessible name of the retry action (`retry-label`), with the place `{name}` filled by the file's name ("Retry {name}"). This instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ retryLabel })`).

members.name: announcement
members.description: A message assistive technology hears through the one live region when the product sets or changes it ("3 files added"). Not drawn. Set in the same turn as rows change, it is said in their place.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Nothing can be chosen or dropped: the trigger is disabled and the area answers nothing. Inside a Field, disable the Field.

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the file picker in the error condition: the drop area's edge is drawn in the error role and the trigger is exposed as invalid. A Field sets it with its own error. Never set by the element.

members.name: required
members.description: Exposes the trigger as required; a button has no such state, so it is said by a Field's required text in the trigger's description. Draws nothing and validates nothing.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the files are submitted under: the kept files while `rows` is `own`, the files of the product's rows while it is `given`. Web only. A product that sends files itself gives none.

members.name: rows
members.description: Who holds the rows. `own` (the default, and every value it does not know): the file upload keeps the files a person chose and makes a file item for each itself — choose, see the list, remove, submit, with nothing written. `given`: the product gives the rows as `<tanrei-file-item>` children and the file upload keeps no file — for a product that sends files itself and shows each one's status. Never guessed from the children.

members.name: typeErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its kind (`type-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileTypeErrorText })`); with neither the row is drawn without a sentence.

members.name: sizeErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused for its size (`size-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileSizeErrorText })`).

members.name: countErrorText
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the sentence on the row of a file refused because no more files fit (`count-error-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ fileCountErrorText })`).

members.name: formatSize
members.description: While `rows` is `own`: the product's function from a size in bytes to the text a kept or refused file's row draws ("820 KB"). A property, never an attribute. Null draws no size: the file upload writes none itself.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The native constraint validity: `valueMissing` while it is required and no row carries a file.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: FUP-31: while `rows` is `given` a reset changes nothing — the rows are the product's to clear. FUP-49: while it is `own` a reset does what `clear()` does, and emits nothing.

members.name: formStateRestoreCallback
members.description: FUP-31, FUP-49: nothing is restored: no state is kept with the form — a handle does not outlast the page.

members.name: files
members.description:
FUP-48: the files it keeps while `rows` is `own`, in order, as the browser's own `File` handles: a new array on
each read, so changing it changes nothing that is kept. Never a refused file. Empty while `rows` is `given`.

members.name: add
members.description:
FUP-48: hands files over, as a product does that takes them elsewhere — a drop target of its own, a paste. They
are judged by its file picker (FPK-31) and are then an arrival (FUP-43): kept or refused, drawn and announced as a
choice is, with no event. Answers with the refused files and their reasons. Works while disabled. While `rows` is
`given` it does nothing and is reported.

members.name: clear
members.description:
FUP-48: lets go of every file it keeps and removes every row, kept and refused. Emits nothing and announces
nothing; focus that was on a row goes to the trigger. Works while disabled. Does nothing while `rows` is `given`.

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

events.name: select
events.description: Files were chosen or dropped, passed and found room. Once per choice; `detail.files` is a `File[]` — while `rows` is `own`, the files newly kept. Bubbles.

events.name: reject
events.description: Files of one choice or one drop were refused. Once, after `select` where both happen; `detail.files` is `{ file, reason }[]`, the reason `type`, `size` or `count`. Bubbles.

events.name: change
events.description: While `rows` is `own`: the kept files changed by what a person did — a choice or a drop that kept or replaced a file, or a kept file's row removed. Once, after `select` and `reject`; `detail.files` is the `File[]` now kept. Bubbles. Never for `add()`, `clear()`, a reset or a change of `rows`.

While `rows` is `given` and `reorderable` is set: a person asked for a row to stand in another place, by the move menu, the keyboard or a drag. `detail.from` and `detail.to`, from 0. The file upload has moved nothing: put your file item in its new place. Bubbles.

The mark a person drags, or moves from the keyboard, to change the size of what it stands on: a sheet's top, a text
field's corner, a pane's or a preview frame's edge. One axis is a short capsule; two axes are a quarter-circle arc that
bows toward its corner.

Contract: specs/handle.spec.json. It never sizes anything itself: it tells its owner how far it was dragged
(`resizestart`, `resize`, `resizeend`), which step a key asked for (`step`) and that it was pressed without a drag
(`activate`); the owner keeps the size and gives it back as `value`, which assistive technology reads. With a `value`
it is a focusable separator (the window splitter pattern); without one, a button, with `expanded` where the owner has
two sizes. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-handle-*` tokens.

Out of sight until it is used (HDL-23): drawn while a mouse is over it, while it has keyboard focus and while a press
or a drag holds it, and always on a touch screen (HDL-25) or with `revealed`. It is one Tab stop all the same.

A press takes no focus and selects nothing, so a field keeps its caret while its handle is dragged. The drag follows
the pointer anywhere (pointer capture); an owner that holds an iframe sets `pointer-events: none` on it between
`resizestart` and `resizeend`, or the iframe takes the pointer as it passes over it. The events bubble within the
tree the handle stands in and do not leave a shadow root: an element that puts a handle in its own shadow root hears
them on the handle and says what it means in its own events.

Assistive technology's increment and decrement (HDL-10) reach a web page as the arrow keys, which HDL-9 answers.

declarations.description:
Shows one picture of a set over the whole window when the person presses its thumbnail, to be looked at closely —
enlarged and back by a double tap, a pinch, a control or a key, moved about while enlarged — and moved on to the
next picture or back, until it is closed.

Contract: specs/image-preview.spec.json. A feature: its stage — the picture, its zoom and its place —
and its pager are its own; its five controls are real `<tanrei-button>` elements and its placeholder a real
`<tanrei-skeleton>`, each reading its own tokens. The images are `<tanrei-image-preview-item>` children.

The product opens it from its own thumbnail — a `<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">` around its own
picture, named for what it does — by setting `index` and `open`, and closes it in answer to `close` by setting
`open` to false: the preview never closes itself. It is a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with
`showModal()`: in the top layer over the whole window, everything else inert, the page held from scrolling, focus on
the stage and kept inside, and returned where it was when the preview closes. It writes no history entry.

Every gesture has a control and a key: the zoom controls and `+` `−` `0` for a double tap and a pinch; the previous
and next controls, the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End for a sideways drag; the arrow keys for a drag
over an enlarged picture; the close control and Escape for the downward drag by touch. `index`, `zoom` and
`controlsHidden` are plain values the element writes itself on a person's change, before the event.

Only the image shown and the one before and after it are asked for. An item without a `src` is asked for nothing
and waits. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-image-preview-*` tokens.

Shows the keys that perform a command, as keys or as text, in the modifier symbols and names of the keyboard the

Contract: specs/keyboard-shortcut.spec.json. Write the keys once, in neutral names — `<tanrei-keyboard-shortcut
keys="mod+shift+k">` draws ⇧⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+Shift+K elsewhere; `keys="mod+k mod+c"` is a sequence of
two chords. It only shows keys: it takes no focus and no input, and does not make them work (KBS-14). Every visual value
is a `--tanrei-comp-keyboard-shortcut-*` token.

What is drawn is hidden from assistive technology; one visually hidden text is read in its place, where the shortcut
sits: `label`, the shortcut in the product's own words ("Shift Command K", KBS-10) — and without it the notation of
`aria-keyshortcuts` ("Meta+Shift+K", KBS-11), because Tanrei has no names for keys in any language. The convention is `convention`, or under
`auto` the nearest ancestor's `data-tanrei-keyboard-convention` (`apple` or `standard`), else the platform's (KBS-2).

One item of a list — the spec's item kind `list-item`: a box around your own content (its children). Placed as a
child of `<tanrei-list>`, which decides whether it is an option; otherwise it is static, one action with

option, and hands its content a color and a text style (LST-8) — every value a `--tanrei-comp-list-*` token, one set
per condition (unselected, selected) and state.

Semantics: the host is a `listitem` — or, in a selectable list, an `option` with its selected state, which takes focus
itself. An interactive item draws one element with the button role inside its list item; a link item an `<a href>`.
Each is named by `label`, else by the text of its content, which is then presentational (LST-19). The list sets each
item's position and the list's size (`aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`) and which one is the tab stop.

menu of moves and, with Space, lifts the item for the keyboard. The whole item can be dragged.

declarations.description:
Holds a set of your own items in one column, one line, or lines that wrap into a grid; people read them, open them
one by one, choose from them, or drag them into another order.

Contract: specs/list.spec.json. The list draws nothing and adds no space around its `<tanrei-list-item>` children
(LST-1): `orientation` lays them out as a column or a line, `wrap` lets them run onto further lines (a grid, LST-2),
`gap` sets the space between them and `dividers` a hairline between them (LST-3). It carries the semantics — a
`list`, or a `listbox` named by `label` while `selection` is `single` or `multiple` — and moves keyboard focus among
the items that are actions, links or options: one tab stop (a roving tabindex), the arrow keys of the arrangement
without wrapping, Home, End and typeahead (LST-17). Moving focus never changes the selection; Space or Enter chooses.

The selection is the list's: `value` names the selected option of a single-select list, `values` those of a
multiple-select list, each by the options' `value`. The list sets them before firing `change`, as a native control
does; set them yourself to select from script (a new array for `values`).

With `reorderable` (and `selection` none) people can put the items in another order (LST-31): every item is static
and draws a handle. The whole item can be dragged — a mouse after a few pixels of movement, a touch or a pen after a
long press or at once from the handle — while the other items slide aside; the handle opens a menu of four moves
(start, before, after, end), and with the keyboard Space on the handle lifts the item, the arrow keys carry it, Space
or Enter drop it and Escape puts it back, each step announced. Every way fires `move` with `from` and `to` and changes
nothing: the order is your data. Reorder your items in answer (move the elements, or let your framework render the new
order) and the list draws them changing place, keeps focus on the moved item's handle and says `moved-text` through
its one polite live region. A move you have not made within `--tanrei-comp-list-motion-reorder-duration` is taken as
refused. The words are yours (attributes, or once with `setWords()`).

it on a raised circle of its own, for waits over content. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-loading-indicator-*`
token. When the length of the wait can be measured, use `<tanrei-progress-indicator>` instead.

Insert it when the wait starts and remove it when the wait ends. From its insertion it waits `showDelay` (null takes
`motion.show-delay`) with its box kept, drawing nothing and exposing nothing (`aria-hidden="true"`); then it enters
(`entrance`: fade, or grow from its center, over `enterDuration`) and the arc starts turning. Moving it within the
document starts a new delay; hiding it (`hidden`, CSS, scrolling) neither restarts nor pauses it. A change of
`showDelay`, `entrance` or `enterDuration` applies from the next insertion.

Once shown, the host is a progressbar with no value (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-label` from `label`,
`aria-busy="true"`). It is never focusable and never announces itself: mark the region being loaded `aria-busy` and
announce its arrival in the product. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the arc stops turning and the whole circle
pulses, and grow enters as a fade; the delay is kept. Off screen, the turning is paused (the entrance is not).

Performs the single most important action of a screen on a raised container that floats above the content, showing its icon and its written name (extended), or collapsing to its icon alone. Contract: specs/main-action-button.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-main-action-button-*` tokens, one set per variant and state — the container color, the label color (the icon's too) and the elevation: how a state looks is the active design system's decision, not this component's. How a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), and how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`); all are read from the cascade, so they follow `data-tanrei-system`. `label` is the visible text while extended and the accessible name in either form. The icon is the `icon` slot: a glyph of the system's icon set, given as its ligature text (`edit`), drawn in the label color at the size's icon size, on the side `iconPosition` names. `extended = false` (the `collapsed` attribute) collapses the button to a square holding only the icon, over the resize motion. Without an icon it stays extended; without a label it never extends (both reported in debug builds). It is an action, never a toggle: it has no pressed, selected or expanded state, and collapsing changes no role, name or focus. The element does not position itself (MAB-18): it is inline, at its own size, and the page places it; which edge stays put while it collapses is the layout's decision too (an element anchored at the inline end collapses toward it).

type.text: { anchor: MenuBox; surface: { width: number; height: number }; viewport: { width: number; height: number }; placement: TanreiMenuPlacement; offset: number; margin: number; rtl: boolean }

declarations.description:
Where the surface goes (MNU-2): `offset` from the anchor on the placement's side, flipped to the other side when this
one has less room than the surface needs within `margin` of the viewport's edge and the other has more; aligned by its
start or end edge with the anchor's (mirrored in right-to-left), then shifted along the anchor to stay `margin` inside
the viewport; its height limited to the room left. Coordinates are the viewport's (`left` is physical).

declarations.name: placeAtPoint

type.text: { point: { x: number; y: number }; surface: { width: number; height: number }; viewport: { width: number; height: number }; placement: TanreiMenuPlacement; margin: number; rtl: boolean }

declarations.description:
Where the surface of a context menu goes from the point it was asked for at (MNU-61): with no offset, a corner on the
point — the block-start corner for a `bottom-*` placement, the block-end one for `top-*`, the inline-start one for
`*-start` (mirrored in right-to-left) — flipped to the other side of the point, along each axis by itself, where its
side has less room than the surface needs within `margin` of the viewport's edge and the other side has more; then
shifted to stay `margin` inside the viewport, its height limited to the room left. Coordinates are the viewport's.

declarations.name: placeSubmenu
declarations.description:
Where a submenu's surface goes (MNU-46, MNU-47): beside the surface that holds its item (`parent`), `offset` from that
surface's inline-end edge — or from the side `prefer` names, the side its parent surface was itself placed on — and on
the other side when this one has less room than the surface needs within `margin` of the viewport's edge and the
other has more. Where the side it is on has room for `minWidth` but not for the surface, the surface is narrowed to
the room. Where neither side has room for `minWidth` it is laid over `parent`: on the side with more room, as far
towards it as the margin allows, as wide as leaves `touch` of the parent uncovered on its other side and never
narrower than `minWidth`. Its first row (`lead` below its own block-start edge) is level with the item's `row`, then
it is shifted along the block axis to stay `margin` inside the viewport, its height limited to the room.
Coordinates are the viewport's (`left` and `side` are physical).

declarations.description: Whether `p` lies in the triangle `a`, `b`, `c` (its edges included). MNU-45: the pointer's path to a submenu.

declarations.description:
An action in a menu — the spec's item kind `item`: it does something and closes the menu.

With `href` it is a link item (MNU-53): the row is an `<a href role="menuitem" tabindex="-1">` in the shadow
root, drawn exactly as an action is and moved to with the same keys, and the browser's own link in everything else —
its context menu, a new tab by a modified or a middle click, its address shown on hover. It is exposed as a menu
item, not as a link: a menu is read by its items. A plain activation — a click, a touch, Enter, and Space too, which
activates every row of a menu — fires the item's `click` (the anchor's own: `preventDefault()` cancels the
navigation, as a router does), then the menu's `close`, and then the browser follows the link (MNU-54). A modified
or a middle click is the browser's: no `close`, and the menu stays open. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely
(`noopener`), ends the row with the icon set's `open_in_new` in the trailing icon column unless `trailing-icon` names
a glyph, and is said through `targetLabel` (MNU-55). A disabled link item is the anchor without `href` (MNU-56).

declarations.description:
Offers a short set of actions or choices on a temporary surface that opens from the element that asked for it, with
further levels in submenus where the set needs them.

Contract: specs/menu.spec.json. The surface is a manual popover in the top layer, placed against the anchor (the
element whose id is `anchor`) by script: below or above it as `placement` says, flipping and shifting to stay inside
the viewport, scrolling when it is taller than the room, following the anchor while it moves. The menu is an operated
overlay that is not modal: it moves focus to its first enabled item when it opens and back to the anchor
when it closes, never traps focus and draws no scrim. It never closes itself: it fires `close` with a reason — Escape,
a press outside the surface and the anchor, Tab, focus leaving it, an item's activation — and you set `open` to false.

A `<tanrei-submenu>` among the items opens another level beside its row (MNU-42 … MNU-52), by the WAI-ARIA menu
pattern: the arrow key that points to the inline end, Enter, Space, a press or a tap open it and move focus in; the
opposite arrow key and Escape close one level and return focus to its item; a pointer that rests on the item opens it
after `comp.menu.motion.submenu-delay`, and may then cross other items on its way in. Every surface of the tree is
inside the menu: a press in a submenu is not a press outside, and whatever closes the menu closes every level with one
`close`.

A group is told from what is next to it as `separation` names (MNU-35): a divider, or a gap of
`comp.menu.group.gap`; `auto` takes `comp.menu.separation`, which follows the design system's choice.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-menu-*` tokens, the items' by condition (unselected, selected,
current, destructive, expanded) and state. The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws the open surface in place
instead: at its natural size, with its elevation, without an anchor, placement, open motion, focus on opening or light
dismiss, each open submenu beside its item.

With `trigger="context"` it is the context menu of an area — the element whose id is `anchor` (MNU-60 … MNU-63): a
secondary click, a touch or a pen held still for the long-press duration, Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key on the
element of the area that has focus, or the context-menu command of assistive technology fires `contextrequest` with
the point, and the browser's own context menu is cancelled unless you cancel the request. You set `open` to true; the
surface opens with a corner on the point (against the focused element for a key), flipping away from the window's
edges, and focus returns, when it closes, to the element that had it. The area gets no popup state.

A component that holds a menu in its shadow root may forward its own children into it: a `<slot>` child of the menu
stands for the elements assigned to it, each forwarded child in a slot of its own (the split button, SPB-15).

declarations.name: titleStyles
declarations.description:
A title (MBR-2 … MBR-8, MBR-17, MBR-28, MBR-29) — a menu's, the overflow item's, and the copies the bar measures —
as three boxes:

  .title      the room the title takes in the row and everything of it that answers a pointer: at least the minimum
              target long, and by its `::before` as tall as the target and half the gap further toward each
              neighbour, so that two hit areas meet in the middle of the gap and never overlap (MBR-17)
  .container  what is drawn and what carries the states: the title's height, paddings and corners, centred in .title
  .content    the label, or the overflow item's glyph; a bar item's label and, for a link item that opens a new
              context, the mark after it (MBR-37)

A bar item (MBR-32) is a title in all of this: the same three boxes, the same rules, always unselected. Its link
form is the product's own anchor, slotted into `.label` (`itemStyles` below gives the anchor the title's box).

`focused` names where keyboard focus is read, given the condition: the element that takes the title's focus is the
menu's host, and for the overflow item its own box in the bar's shadow root. Every state selector has the same
specificity, so the order `stateRules()` writes them in is the precedence (MBR-4).

declarations.name: menuStyles
declarations.description:
A menu of the bar (MBR-2, MBR-9): its title in the row, and — at no size of its own — the Menu it opens. Folded into
the overflow item (MBR-22) it has no box: the submenu item it draws is a row of the overflow item's menu.

declarations.name: itemStyles
declarations.description:
A bar item (MBR-32): a title in the row, drawn by the title's rules; folded (MBR-43), a row of the overflow item's
menu that it draws of itself, with no box of its own.

Its link form (MBR-35) is the product's own anchor, in the document, slotted into the label. The anchor is drawn as
the label is — the title's text style and the color of its state, no underline, no look of its own for a link or for
a visited one — and by its `::before` it is given the whole of the title's hit area (MBR-17: the target's height and,
on each side, half the gap beyond the room the title keeps), above the mark, so that every press on the title is a
press on the link and what a browser gives a link it gives anywhere on it. The focus ring is the container's, as for
every title: the anchor draws none. A product's own rule for its anchor wins over these, as over any slotted rule.

declarations.name: barStyles
declarations.description:
The bar (MBR-1, MBR-21): one row across the inline size its parent gives it, the bar's fill behind it, the titles
from the start edge a gap apart inside the paddings; the overflow item, a title of the bar's own, at the end of the
row; and the copies the fold is measured from.

One menu of a menubar — the spec's item kind `menu`: its title in the bar's row, and the items that open below it.

It holds the menu's own item elements as its children, exactly as `<tanrei-menu>` holds them, and forwards them — each
in a slot of its own, none of them moved — into a Tanrei Menu in its shadow root, a manual popover in the top layer
placed below its title. The host is the title: `role="menuitem"` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`,
`aria-disabled`, its position among the bar's titles, and the bar's roving `tabindex`; it draws its label in its shadow
root from the `--tanrei-comp-menubar-*` tokens of its condition (unselected, or expanded while its menu is open) and
state. The bar it is in does the rest: the keys, the pointer, which menu is open, and folding it into the overflow
item when the row has no room — it is then drawn as a submenu item of the overflow item's menu, with the same label
and the same items, and `open` and `toggle` mean the same there.

`open` is its own: the bar sets it when the person opens or closes the menu and fires `toggle`; the product may set it
to open or close the menu itself, which fires none. The items' own `click`, `change` and `toggle` bubble through it.
declarations.name: TanreiMenubarMenu

declarations.description: A bar item of a menubar — the spec's item kind `item`: an entry of the row that acts by itself instead of opening a menu. It is drawn exactly as a menu's title is and reached by the same keys; nothing at rest tells them apart but their words, so name an action with a verb ("Run") and a link with its place ("Documentation"). **An action** is written with a `label`: ``. The host is the entry — `role="menuitem"` with neither `aria-haspopup` nor `aria-expanded`, `aria-disabled`, its position among the bar's entries and the bar's roving `tabindex` — and `click` is the host's own: a press, Enter, Space (on key up, as a button) and assistive technology produce it, once, after the menu of the bar that was open has closed. **A link item** is the same element around the product's own anchor, which stays in the document: `Documentation`. The anchor is the entry: the element writes `role="menuitem"`, the roving `tabindex` and the position on it and `role="none"` on the host, and draws the title around it. Everything a link is, is the anchor's — its text is the label, `href`, `target` (`_blank` opens a new context: the element adds `noopener` to `rel` and draws the icon set's `open_in_new` after the label), `aria-current="page"` (drawn at the emphasized weight, with no fill), `rel`, `download` — and the properties `label`, `href`, `target` and `current` of the host read the anchor and write it. `click` is the anchor's own click: `preventDefault()` cancels the navigation, a click with a modifier key or the middle button is the browser's, and so is Enter with a modifier key; Space follows the link as Enter does. The link works before the element is defined and where script does not run (`@tanrei/web/menubar.css` lays it out there). `disabled` on the host is the one statement that the entry is disabled; a disabled link item's anchor is written without `href`. Folded into the overflow item, a bar item is an item of that menu, which it draws of itself; its `click` is the same event of the same element.

declarations.description:
Keeps an application's commands within reach in one persistent row of named menus (File, Edit, View…), each opening
a menu below its title, with the arrow keys moving along the row and into each menu.

Contract: specs/menubar.spec.json. The host is `role="menubar"`, named by `label`; its children are
`<tanrei-menubar-menu>` elements, each of which is its title and holds its menu's items, and — for the one or two
entries that act by themselves — `<tanrei-menubar-item>` elements, an action or the product's own anchor as a link
item, drawn and reached as the titles are (a press, Enter or Space runs or follows one; the block arrow keys do
nothing on it; from a menu the inline arrow keys land on it and open nothing). The bar is one Tab stop: the
inline arrow keys, Home, End and a typed character move along the titles; Enter, Space and the block arrow keys open
a title's menu; from inside a menu the inline arrow keys go on to the neighbouring menu; Escape returns to the title
and Tab leaves the bar. While one menu is open a pointer that moves onto another title opens that one at once. It
shows one menu at a time, sets each menu's `open` and fires its `toggle`.

Titles that the row has no room for are folded whole, from the end, into one overflow item — the icon set's
`more_horiz`, named by `overflow-label` — whose menu holds each folded menu as a submenu. The bar measures what fits
and decides again when its size, its menus, a label, the text size or the direction changes. It draws no position,
edge or elevation of its own: you place it. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-menubar-*` tokens; the
surfaces the titles open are Menus, drawn from `--tanrei-comp-menu-*`.

The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws an open menu in place below its title instead of in the
top layer, as the menu's own does: without placement, open motion, focus on opening or light dismiss.
declarations.name: TanreiMenubar

declarations.description:
Shows where a known value stands in a known range — storage used, a battery's charge, a quota, the strength of a
password — as a bar or a ring that looks like the progress indicator, without saying that anything is under way.

Contract: specs/meter.spec.json. Drawn as the progress indicator's determinate form is (the two share the drawing,
`src/primitives/range-track.ts`), from `--tanrei-comp-meter-*` tokens, which by default are the progress
indicator's; the meter never runs an indeterminate animation. `status` (default, info, success, warning, error)
changes the indicator's color and nothing else: the meter has no thresholds of its own, and what the color means is
said in words by `value-text`, `label` or the text beside it (MTR-9).

The host is the meter (`role="meter"`, `aria-label` from `label`, `aria-valuemin` / `-max` / `-now` and
`aria-valuetext` from `value-text`); never a progressbar, never busy, never focusable, never a live region. A change of
value or status moves the end and fades the color over `motion.value-duration`, from the second frame on; under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the end moves at once and the color still fades.
declarations.name: TanreiMeter

declarations.description:
The layer under every modal surface: it dims the window behind what it presents, makes everything there inert, moves
focus in, keeps it there and gives it back, and asks to close on Escape, the platform's back or a press on the dim.
The dialog, the modal sheets, the modal drawer, the image preview, the modal picker and the search's modal views are
built from it; use it alone for a modal surface Tanrei does not have (a command palette, a takeover of the window).

Contract: specs/modal-layer.spec.json. A native `<dialog>` in the shadow root, opened with `showModal()` while `open`
is true: in the top layer over `::backdrop` (the scrim: `comp.modal-layer.scrim.color`, blurring what is behind by
`comp.modal-layer.scrim.blur`), with everything else inert and the page held from scrolling. Focus goes to the slotted
element marked `autofocus`, or to the container, stays inside it (Tab wraps), and returns where it was when the layer
closes. The container draws nothing: it is as large as its content, centred in the window's safe area; place or size
it with `::part(container)`.

Controlled: the layer never closes itself. While `closedby` is not `none`, Escape, the platform's back and a press on
the scrim fire `close` with a reason, and you set `open` to false.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-modal-layer-*` tokens.

declarations.name: barStyles
declarations.description:
The bar (NVB-11, NVB-18): the parent's full width, at least container.height above the bottom inset, on its color and
elevation with its top edge — the same whichever destination is selected and while the indicator moves; its width,
less container.padding at its start and at its end, divided into equal cells in reading order (logical, so RTL
mirrors). The color reaches under the bottom and side insets, the destinations stay inside them.

The active indicator while it moves (NVB-15, NVB-27): one layer under the destinations, an item container's size, in
the selected destination's item container color, which the element places between the destinations' item containers —
sliding to a new selection, or where a dragged pointer is. At rest it is not drawn: the selected destination's item
container is the indicator, so it is never painted twice.

NVB-27: a sideways drag on the bar is the indicator's and a vertical one the page's (`touch-action: pan-y`).

declarations.name: itemStyles
declarations.default: [ destinationStyles(PREFIX, { lines: 1, shareWidth: true, parts: { ii: 'item-icon-indicator-color', ci: 'item-covered-icon-color', cl: 'item-covered-label-color' }, variants: ['filled'], focusWithin: `var(${PREFIX}-container-padding)`, }), boxStyles, ]
declarations.description:
A destination (NVB-4…10, NVB-12…16, NVB-23): the shared destination styles with the icon indicator and the covered
colors as parts of every condition and the filled conditions, its cell the bar's full height and an equal share of its
width, narrower than the touch target when the bar is (NVB-6), its focus indicator held inside the bar (NVB-5: the room
around the item container is container.padding); then the item container that is the whole cell.

One destination of a navigation bar — the spec's item kind `destination`: an icon, a label under it and an
optional badge on the icon, inside the item container. Placed as a child of `<tanrei-navigation-bar>`, in order; the
bar decides whether it is the selected one and answers its activation.

It is a button, or with `href` a link (NVB-30): an `<a href>` in the shadow root, drawn exactly as the button
is, whose context menu, new-tab gestures and address are the browser's own — except that it is not dragged as a link,
because a sideways drag moves the active indicator. A link is not selected by a press (NVB-31): a plain activation
makes the bar fire `change` (or `reselect`) — cancelable, with `detail.href`, before the browser follows the link —
and the page shown next sets the bar's `value`; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a
download fire nothing. Without a `value` a link's `href` is its value. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely
(`noopener`), and draws no mark — a cell has no place for one — so `targetLabel` says it (NVB-32). Space does not
activate a link.

It is named by its label whether or not the label is drawn, the selected one `aria-current="page"`, its badge's
text and then, for a link that opens a new context, `targetLabel` its description; its host is a list item of the
bar's list. Its icon and label are drawn twice: the second copy, in the covered colors and clipped to the active
indicator, is hidden from assistive technology (NVB-23).

Its properties are the shared destination's (`src/primitives/destination.ts`): `value`, `label`, `icon`, `disabled`,
`badge`, `badgeCount` (`badge-count`), `badgeLabel` (`badge-label`), `href`, `target`, `targetLabel`
(`target-label`) and the web-only `rel` and `download`.
declarations.name: TanreiNavigationBarItem

declarations.description:
Three to five top-level destinations along the bottom edge of a compact window, one of them the current screen.

Contract: specs/navigation-bar.spec.json. `<tanrei-navigation-bar-item>` children are the destinations, in order. The
bar's `value` is the selected destination's value; the bar sets it when a destination is activated — pointer, Enter,
Space, `item.click()` — and then fires `change`, or `reselect` when the selected destination is activated again. The
host is a navigation landmark named by `label`.

A bar of links (NVB-30…33): a destination with `href` is a link, and the selected destination is the current page
(`aria-current="page"`) — one state, which in a site of separate pages the page says, through `value` (a link without
a `value` takes its `href`). The bar never writes `value` for a link: a plain activation (Enter, not Space) fires
`change` or `reselect` with `detail.href`, cancelable, before the browser follows the link (a router cancels it, goes
to `detail.href` itself and sets `value`), and the active indicator stays on the destination `value` selects until
`value` changes; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a download are the browser's and
fire nothing.

The bar is the ground the active indicator moves on: one constant color. Each destination's item container is its
whole equal share of the bar, held in from the bar's edges by `comp.navigation-bar.container.padding` — the same box
for every destination, whatever it holds — and it is where the active indicator, hover, press and the focus indicator
are drawn. When the selection changes, the active indicator — one layer of the bar — slides at its full size from the
previous destination's item container to the new one's, and the covered copy of every destination's icon and label is
clipped to it in the same frame (NVB-15, NVB-23); where nothing was selected it fades in, in place.

A drag across the bar — by touch, a pen or a mouse, past 8 px and further sideways than up or down, while a
destination is selected — carries the indicator with the pointer, its place and the covered colors changing
continuously (NVB-27). Nothing is selected before the release, which chooses the nearer of the two destinations the
indicator lies between (or the one a fling is toward), activates it as a tap would — `value`, one `change` — or
returns the indicator and fires nothing; a release on a link is a plain press on that link (`change` with its
`href`, the link followed, `value` not written), so the indicator returns to the destination `value` selects and goes
on to the chosen one when the product sets `value`; Escape, a cancelled pointer, or `value` set meanwhile returns it
(NVB-28, NVB-29).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-navigation-bar-*` tokens: `variant` chooses the conditions the
destinations are drawn from (tonal: unselected and selected; filled: filled-unselected and filled-selected). How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`).
The color reaches under `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and the side insets; the destinations stay inside them.

declarations.name: drawerStyles
declarations.description:
The drawer (NVD-11, NVD-12, NVD-18, NVD-19, NVD-22, NVD-25, NVD-30, NVD-35, NVD-38, NVD-40). The panel is its form's
width (container.width expanded, collapsed.container.width collapsed) beside the start inset and the full height of
its parent (standard, or a collapsible modal drawer's column) or of the window (modal), on its variant's color and
elevation, its end corners rounded by its variant's shape and its start corners square, with its variant's end edge.
Inside it: the header, which stays in place, and then the items, which scroll. Logical, so right-to-left puts it at the
right edge, mirrored.

declarations.name: sectionStyles
declarations.description:
A section (NVD-16, NVD-17): the divider component before it, across the drawer's inner width in either form; its
heading in heading.typescale and heading.color in a row at least heading.height, the text centred and starting where
the labels of destinations without an icon start; then its cells. Collapsed, the heading's row keeps its height and its
text fades and is clipped (NVD-35).

declarations.name: cellStyles
declarations.description:
A cell — a destination's, or a group's row (NVD-4…10, NVD-13, NVD-14, NVD-27, NVD-31…35, NVD-41, NVD-43, NVD-44). The
cell is the native button or link: the drawer's full width (its current width, so its hit area follows the form) and
its height, with half of container.gap above and below it and at least the minimum target. In it, the row — laid out
for the expanded drawer, clipped by the cell: at least item.container.height, the icon on the icon column and the
cell's icon line (the row's centre), the label (wrapping) item.gap after it, the trailing content at its end — and,
placed around the same icon line, the item container (the row expanded; the pill collapsed) and the short label under
the icon.

declarations.name: groupStyles
declarations.description:
A group (NVD-44…48): its row is a cell (above), and under it its items, revealed and hidden over the disclosure motion
while it opens and closes (and over the change of form's while the drawer collapses: the collapsed drawer draws none of
them, and the cells below move up), container.gap from its row and between them.

One destination of a navigation drawer — the spec's item kind `destination`: an icon, a label (a short label
while the drawer is collapsed), optional trailing content at the end of its row and an optional badge on its icon. A
child of `<tanrei-navigation-drawer>`, of one of its sections or of one of its groups, in order.

It is a button, or with `href` a link (NVD-59): an `<a href>` in the shadow root, drawn exactly as the button
is, whose context menu, new-tab clicks, drag and address are the browser's own; Enter follows it and Space does not.
A link is not selected by a press (NVD-60): a plain activation makes the drawer fire `change` (or `reselect`) —
cancelable, with `detail.href`, before the browser follows the link — and the page shown next sets the drawer's
`value`; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new` and a download fire nothing. Without a `value`
a link's `href` is its value. `target="new"` opens a new tab, safely (`noopener`), ends the expanded row with the icon
set's `open_in_new` unless the row has trailing content, and says `targetLabel` (NVD-63).

Either is named by its label in both forms, the selected one `aria-current="page"`; its badge's description, then its
trailing content and then, for a link that opens a new context, `targetLabel` are its description. Its host is a
list item, its position counted among the items of its level.

declarations.description:
A panel of destinations at the start edge, in two variants — `standard`, a layout region beside the content,
and `modal`, a modal overlay over a scrim that closes itself after a destination is chosen — and, while `collapsible`,
in two forms: expanded, and collapsed to a column of icons, which is the expanded drawer with its labels gone: every
row is the same row cut after its icon, at the same height and with the same corners, and every icon exactly in place
while the drawer moves between the two. A collapsed cell shows its name in a plain tooltip on hover and keyboard focus;
`collapsed-labels` draws short labels under the icons instead, for a product or a system whose column is labelled.

Contract: specs/navigation-drawer.spec.json. `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-item>`, `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-group>` and
`<tanrei-navigation-drawer-section>` children, in order; header buttons (icon-only `<tanrei-button>`s) with
`slot="header-button"`, the main action (`<tanrei-main-action-button>`) with `slot="main-action"`, and the `header`
slot. The drawer's `value` is the selected destination's value; the drawer sets it when a button destination is
activated and fires `change`, or `reselect` for the selected one.

A site's sidebar (NVD-57…64): a destination with `href` is a link, and the selected destination is the current page
(`aria-current="page"`) — one state, which in a site of separate pages the page says, through `value` (a link without
a `value` takes its `href`). The drawer never writes `value` for a link: a plain activation fires `change` or
`reselect` with `detail.href`, cancelable, before the browser follows the link (a router cancels it and goes to
`detail.href` itself), and then closes a modal drawer; a modified or a middle click, a link whose `target` is `new`
and a download fire nothing and close nothing. The row that shows the selection is brought into view when the drawer
first appears and whenever `value` changes — centred if it was not wholly in view, untouched if it was, without motion
and without moving focus — and `reveal-selected` opens the groups that hold it (each fires `toggle`). `scrollOffset`
reads and writes how far the items are scrolled; the scroll does not chain to the page. Nothing is stored: a site keeps
each group's `open` (from `toggle`) and `scrollOffset` (read on `pagehide`) itself and gives them back as attributes.

Forms (NVD-30): not collapsible, always expanded. Collapsible and standard: `expanded` chooses. Collapsible and modal:
collapsed — its column in the layout, drawn as a standard drawer's — while closed, and expanded over the content while
open. The first header button is then the menu button: the drawer sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on its
native button (`ariaExpanded`, `ariaControlsElements`), and its activation asks for the other form: the drawer sets
`expanded` (or `open`) and fires `expandedchange`. The main action's `extended` follows the form. The read-only
`collapsed` attribute reflects the form.

Standard: a `<nav>` named by `label`, taking its form's width in the layout while `open` and none while closed (sliding
while the content beside it resizes). Opening it moves focus in; closing it with focus inside returns focus to where it
was; Tab leaves it without closing it.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root, opened with `showModal()` while `open` — in the top layer over its
`::backdrop` (the scrim), everything else inert, the page held from scrolling, focus kept inside. Escape, the platform's
back, a press on the scrim, a drag toward the start edge past half its width (or a fling), the menu button and a
destination's activation close it: the drawer sets `open` to false itself and fires `close`. Focus returns to where it
was.

Responsive (NVD-53…55): with `responsive`, the window's width chooses what the drawer is, and `variant` is ignored —
a standard drawer, shown whatever `open` says, from `comp.navigation-drawer.breakpoint.expanded` (1024 px at the
default text size); its column, widening over the content while `open`, from `breakpoint.collapsed` (600 px) while
`collapsible`; a modal drawer below that. The read-only `presentation` says which (and the `presentation` attribute, for
styling); `presentationchange` fires when it is first decided and whenever the width changes it. A change of
presentation is drawn at once, is entered closed (an open overlay closes: `open` is false and `close` fires once), and
keeps `expanded`, `value` and every group's `open`. The presentation is derived from the width alone: it is never
written to `variant`, `open` or `expanded`, and the element stores nothing — a product that wants the user's choice of
form remembered keeps what `expandedchange` carries and sets `expanded` from it.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-navigation-drawer-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-*)` at the start, top and bottom.

members.name: open

members.name: collapsible
members.description: Gives the drawer its collapsed form, the icon column. Reflected.

members.name: expanded
members.description: The form of a collapsible standard drawer: true for the full drawer, false for the icon column (`expanded="false"`). The user's choice: a change of the window's width never writes it. Reflected.

members.name: collapsedLabels
members.description: Which cells draw their short label under the icon while collapsed: `never` (the default: a collapsed drawer is the expanded one with its labels gone), `selected` or `always` (anything else is `never`).

members.name: density
members.description:
How much room a row takes (NVD-65): `regular`, a menu item's row, for a product used by touch as well as by pointer;
`compact`, a tree view's compact row, for a tool used with a pointer whose drawer lists many places. The rows, the
headings, the gaps, the nesting indent and the collapsed column follow it; for touch a row is never lower than the
touch target. A value a design system added is drawn from its own tokens; one the active system lacks is drawn as
`regular` and reported (NVD-26). Reflected.

members.name: chevron
members.description: Where a group's chevron is drawn (NVD-68): `start` (the default), `end` or `none`. A collapsible drawer draws start as end. Reflected.

members.name: guides
members.description: The guide line beside an open group's items (NVD-73): `none` (the default), `shown` or `hover`. Reflected.

members.name: indent
members.description: How much further each level begins (NVD-69): null (`indent="auto"`, the default) lines a row up with its group's label; a number of pixels; 0 none.

members.name: highlight
members.description: How far a nested row's fill and state layers reach (NVD-70): `indented` (the default) or `full`. Reflected.

members.name: iconSpace
members.description: Whether a row without an icon keeps the icon's room (NVD-71): `auto` (the default), `always` or `never`. Reflected.

members.name: expandable
members.description: Whether groups open and close at all (NVD-72); `expandable="false"` shows every group open, without chevrons. Reflected.

members.name: labelWrap
members.description: Lets labels wrap (NVD-75); while false a label is one line, cut, with its full text in a tooltip. Reflected.

members.name: supportingWrap
members.description: Lets supporting text wrap, as labelWrap lets labels. Reflected.

members.name: stickyParents
members.description: Pins the rows of the open groups the top rows belong to while their items scroll under them (NVD-77). Not while collapsed. Reflected.

members.name: stickyMax
members.description: At most how many group rows are pinned, the innermost winning (NVD-77).

members.name: loadingLabel
members.description: What the loading row under a group that is fetching its items says, and its name ("Loading…", NVD-76): your words.

members.name: responsive
members.description: Lets the window's width choose the drawer's presentation (NVD-53): standard where it is wide, its column where it is narrower (while `collapsible`), modal where it is narrow. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value of the selected destination, wherever it stands; empty selects none. The selected destination is the place
being shown, exposed as the current page. The drawer sets it when a button destination is activated; it never sets
it for a link (NVD-60) — in a site of separate pages each page sets it to its own destination (a link's `href`
stands as its value while it has none).

members.name: revealSelected
members.description:
Opens the groups that hold the selected destination when the drawer first appears (in its first frame, without
motion) and whenever `value` changes, whatever their `open` said; each fires `toggle` (NVD-58). The user may close
such a group again: it then stays closed until `value` changes. While false a closed group stays closed and its row
shows the selection (NVD-47).

members.name: selectableGroups
members.description:
Lets a group be a destination as well as a row that opens and closes (NVD-66): a setting of the product's, off by
default. While set, a group with a `value` or an `href` is selected by `value` and fires `change` or `reselect`
from its row, which is a link with an `href`; its chevron becomes a button of its own that alone opens and closes it
(NVD-67). A group without either still only opens and closes.

members.name: scrollOffset
members.description:
How far the items are scrolled from their start, in CSS pixels (NVD-61). Reading it gives the present distance;
setting it scrolls there at once, without motion, held inside the scroll range — before the drawer first appears
included, when it is where the first frame is drawn (the `scroll-offset` attribute is read once, for that frame).
No event is fired while the user scrolls, and nothing is stored (NVD-62): a site reads it when the page is left and
gives it back on the next page.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the navigation landmark and, while modal and open, the dialog ("Mail").

members.name: items
members.description: The drawer's destinations, in reading order, in sections and groups or not (its items: a group that is a destination is not among them).

members.name: groups
members.description: The drawer's groups, in reading order.

members.name: collapsed
members.description: The form the drawer is in (NVD-30): collapsed to the icon column, or not. Read-only; reflected as the `collapsed` attribute.

members.name: presentation
members.description:
NVD-53, NVD-55: what a responsive drawer is at the window's current width — `standard`, `column` or `modal` — or
null while it is not responsive. Read-only, derived from the width alone and never stored in a prop; reflected as
the `presentation` attribute, for styling.

events.description: A modal drawer closed: the scrim, Escape, back, a drag, the menu button, or after a destination was activated. `open` is already false.

events.name: expandedchange
events.description: The user asked a collapsible drawer for its other form (its menu button, or a group's cell while collapsed): `detail.expanded`. `expanded` (or, for a modal drawer, `open`) already holds it.

events.name: presentationchange
events.description: A responsive drawer decided its presentation for the first time, or the window's width changed it: `detail.presentation` (and `presentation`) is `standard`, `column` or `modal`. A product shows its own menu button while it is `modal`.

The user activated another destination: `detail.value` (and, for a button destination, the drawer's `value`) is its value. For a link it is fired before the link is followed, only for a plain activation of a link that opens in place, carries `detail.href`, leaves `value` to the page, and is cancelable: `preventDefault()` stops the browser's navigation.

declarations.description:
Lets people enter a number as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Number input
(`<tanrei-number-input>`) it frames: the box — the number, its unit and its two steppers — under the Field's label,
or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in it; with the Field's requirement mark, its help
and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/number-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-number-field name="quantity" label="Quantity" min="1" max="99"
required supporting-text="Up to 99 per order." increment-label="Increase"
decrement-label="Decrease"></tanrei-number-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, `--tanrei-comp-number-input-*` and, for the two steppers, `--tanrei-comp-button-*` value reaches the members by
inheritance, and one number field is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each property is its
member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`,
`disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the
number input's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Quantity" required
supporting-text="Up to 99 per order."><tanrei-number-input name="quantity" min="1" max="99"
increment-label="Increase" decrement-label="Decrease"></tanrei-number-input></tanrei-field>` — and the box alone,
where a label stands elsewhere (beside a slider, in a cell of a table), is `<tanrei-number-input>` with a `label`
of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (NUM-47): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the number input's — a number, or null while it holds none — and the four events are
that input's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener of
`change`. It dispatches none itself, and coordinates nothing: the input tells its Field that it floats the label,
where its number's line starts and ends, and its refusal of a text that is not a number, exactly as it does one
level down.

Form-associated (NUM-48): it submits the value under `name` as a plain decimal number ("12.5") whatever the locale
shows — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows a disabled
`<fieldset>`, and reports what its number input reports: a missing value while `required` is set and it
holds none, and a bad input while it holds a text that is not a number. Enter presses the default button of this
element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, the field is one stop in the focus
order, and its name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label
row, on the box or on a floating label focuses the input; a press on a stepper steps and moves no focus; a press on
the help or the error text does nothing.
