members.name: formAssociated
members.description: NUM-48: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: required
members.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

members.name: optional
members.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant
members.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of its Field; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the number input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

members.name: size
members.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

members.name: value
members.description: The committed number, or null while the input holds none. It changes when the person commits — focus leaves, Enter, a step — not on every keystroke; `input` carries what is being typed. The `value` attribute is a plain decimal number ("12.5"), and the value a form reset returns to.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The number can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but not changed: no key steps it and no stepper is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

members.name: min
members.description: The lowest number a commit keeps; a lower one is raised to it. Null for no limit. It is also where the steps are counted from.

members.name: max
members.description: The highest number a commit keeps; a higher one is lowered to it. Null for no limit. A `max` below `min` is no limit.

members.name: step
members.description: How far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number; Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far. It does not limit what may be typed. 0 or less, or not a number, steps by 1.

members.name: noSteppers
members.description: Draws no steppers (`no-steppers`: the spec's `steppers`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for an input in a row too narrow for them, or beside a slider that does their work. The keys still step. Reflected.

members.name: incrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps up (`increment-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ incrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: decrementLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps down (`decrement-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ decrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

members.name: prefixText
members.description: Fixed text before the number, not part of the value (`prefix-text`): a currency sign. Written before the number along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, the prefix asked first, and left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction.

members.name: suffixText
members.description: Fixed text after the number, not part of the value (`suffix-text`): the unit. Read to assistive technology with the number. Written after the number along the run's direction: at its right for a unit in Latin letters or signs, at its left for one in a right-to-left script or one that begins with a right-to-left mark (U+200F).

members.name: valueText
members.description: The value as words (`value-text`: "12 pixels"), given to assistive technology in place of the number with its prefix and suffix. The same text a slider beside the field takes.

members.name: align
members.description: Where the number stands in the input: at the `start`, the field's start edge, as the text of every other field; or at the `end` of the number's run — the edge at which the suffix stands or would stand, the right for a number alone or with a unit in Latin letters or signs in every layout direction — for a number against its unit or in a column of numbers. Anything else is `start`. Reflected.

members.name: minFractionDigits
members.description: The fewest digits shown after the decimal separator; zeros fill them (`min-fraction-digits`: 2 for an amount of money).

members.name: maxFractionDigits
members.description: The most digits kept after the decimal separator (`max-fraction-digits`): a commit rounds to it. 0 makes the field hold whole numbers and asks for a keyboard without a separator.

members.name: locale
members.description: A BCP 47 language tag ("de-DE", "ar-EG") for how the number is shown and read: its digits and its decimal separator. Empty reads the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language. The value itself is a number in every locale.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a text that is not a number (`invalid-text`: "Enter a number"): what the Field that frames the input shows in its supporting row while the entry error lasts — its own `errorText` while this is empty — and the input's description where no Field frames it.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the text in the input, as the number input's `select()` does.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description:
NUM-48: a form's reset returns to the first value and, as in the number input placed in a form by hand, the same
value as the one held is still a new one — the text the person left and an entry error go.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

events.description: The person changed the text, or a step changed the value. `detail.value` is the number the text reads as — not clamped, not rounded — or null while it reads as no value or as not a number. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`.
events.name: input

events.description: A commit changed the value: focus left the input, Enter was pressed, a key stepped it, or a pressed stepper was released; `value` is already the new one. Composed and bubbling. Never fired when the product sets `value`.
events.name: change

events.description: The person pressed Enter; after any `change` it caused. Cancelable: unless it is cancelled, the form the number input stands in is then asked to submit.
events.name: action

events.description: The person committed a text that is not a number. `detail.reason` is `invalid`, `detail.text` the input's `invalidText` (empty where none was given). Composed and bubbling.
events.name: entryerror

attributes.description: The id of the form the number field belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
label
attributes.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

attributes.name: supporting-text
attributes.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

attributes.name: optional
attributes.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

attributes.name: required-mark
attributes.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

attributes.name: required-text
attributes.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

attributes.name: optional-text
attributes.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: The look, as the text inputs beside it: `stacked` is a filled box whose label is the row of its Field; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. Use one style per form. A value the number input does not know by name is laid out as stacked. Reflected.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The container's minimum height: `medium` or `large` (48 / 56 in the default system), the text input's two sizes. The hit area always meets the minimum target. Reflected.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The committed number, or null while the input holds none. It changes when the person commits — focus leaves, Enter, a step — not on every keystroke; `input` carries what is being typed. The `value` attribute is a plain decimal number ("12.5"), and the value a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: A hint shown while the input is empty and the label is not in the input line. Never a replacement for `label`.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The number can be focused, selected and copied, and is submitted, but not changed: no key steps it and no stepper is drawn. The attribute is `readonly`.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The lowest number a commit keeps; a lower one is raised to it. Null for no limit. It is also where the steps are counted from.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The highest number a commit keeps; a higher one is lowered to it. Null for no limit. A `max` below `min` is no limit.

attributes.name: step
attributes.description: How far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number; Page Up and Page Down move ten times as far. It does not limit what may be typed. 0 or less, or not a number, steps by 1.

attributes.name: no-steppers
attributes.description: Draws no steppers (`no-steppers`: the spec's `steppers`, inverted, because a boolean attribute cannot default to true): for an input in a row too narrow for them, or beside a slider that does their work. The keys still step. Reflected.

attributes.name: increment-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps up (`increment-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ incrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

attributes.name: decrement-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the stepper that steps down (`decrement-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ decrementLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the stepper is drawn, works for a pointer and is kept from assistive technology, where the spin button steps by itself.

attributes.name: prefix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text before the number, not part of the value (`prefix-text`): a currency sign. Written before the number along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, the prefix asked first, and left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction.

attributes.name: suffix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text after the number, not part of the value (`suffix-text`): the unit. Read to assistive technology with the number. Written after the number along the run's direction: at its right for a unit in Latin letters or signs, at its left for one in a right-to-left script or one that begins with a right-to-left mark (U+200F).

attributes.name: value-text
attributes.description: The value as words (`value-text`: "12 pixels"), given to assistive technology in place of the number with its prefix and suffix. The same text a slider beside the field takes.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Where the number stands in the input: at the `start`, the field's start edge, as the text of every other field; or at the `end` of the number's run — the edge at which the suffix stands or would stand, the right for a number alone or with a unit in Latin letters or signs in every layout direction — for a number against its unit or in a column of numbers. Anything else is `start`. Reflected.

attributes.name: min-fraction-digits
attributes.description: The fewest digits shown after the decimal separator; zeros fill them (`min-fraction-digits`: 2 for an amount of money).

attributes.name: max-fraction-digits
attributes.description: The most digits kept after the decimal separator (`max-fraction-digits`): a commit rounds to it. 0 makes the field hold whole numbers and asks for a keyboard without a separator.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: A BCP 47 language tag ("de-DE", "ar-EG") for how the number is shown and read: its digits and its decimal separator. Empty reads the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language. The value itself is a number in every locale.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a text that is not a number (`invalid-text`: "Enter a number"): what the Field that frames the input shows in its supporting row while the entry error lasts — its own `errorText` while this is empty — and the input's description where no Field frames it.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${INPUT_BOX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (NMI-43): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported
in debug builds.

declarations.name: INSET
declarations.description:
NMI-45, FLD-26: how far the line of the number stands from the input's own start edge and from its end edge, as
lengths — its inline padding at each (`--_text-start` and `--_pad` below), written from the size's token so that the
Field that is told them resolves them where it stands: custom properties are inherited. The same with and without
steppers: a line of help is aligned with the text above it, not with a button. A size a layer added falls back to
the default's token, as its styles do.

declarations.name: numberOrNull
declarations.description: A finite number, or null: what `value`, `min` and `max` are whatever they were given (a string of an attribute, undefined, NaN).

declarations.name: NUMBER_OR_NULL
declarations.description: An attribute that holds a plain decimal number ("12.5"), or nothing: a property that is a number or null.

The box of a number: lets people enter a number as a number — typed in their locale's form or stepped by a key or a
button, kept within limits, with its unit beside it — and draws no row around it. A `<tanrei-field>` frames it with
a label, a requirement mark, help and an error, or the product names it with `label` where its visible label is
elsewhere: the head of a table's column, a toolbar, the title of a row that also holds a slider.
`<tanrei-number-field>` is the two as one element.

Contract: specs/number-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a token: the box is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (NMI-47), and where the steppers stand and how
a hold repeats from `--tanrei-comp-number-input-*`; the steppers are `<tanrei-button>`s, drawn from
Button's own tokens.

```html
<tanrei-number-input label="Scale" value="1.5" min="0.25" max="4" step="0.05" suffix-text="×" value-text="1.5 times" align="end" no-steppers></tanrei-number-input>
```

`value` is a number, or null while the input holds none. It changes on a **commit** — focus leaves, Enter, a step —
and never while the person types: the text is theirs until then, and nothing typed is refused, reformatted, clamped
or rounded. `input` carries what the text reads as meanwhile (what a slider beside the input follows). A commit
raises the number to `min`, lowers it to `max`, rounds it to `maxFractionDigits` and writes it back in the locale's
form — its digits and its decimal separator, no grouping separators. A text that is not a number is kept, marked as
an error, reported with `entryerror` and told to the Field that frames it, which shows `invalidText`.

`step` is how far Up Arrow, Down Arrow and a stepper move the number (Page Up and Page Down ten times as far), to
the next number on the step's grid counted from `min`; it does not limit what may be typed. Home and End stay the
caret's, and the wheel never changes the number.

It is a block as wide as its place, with no width of its own: give it a narrower place for a narrower box. In a
Field it takes the Field's name, description and required, invalid and disabled states, floats the Field's label
in the filled and the outlined look, and tells the Field where its number's line starts and ends. It is a
form-associated element: it takes `name`, submits its value as a plain decimal number ("12.5") whatever the locale
shows, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports
`valueMissing` while its Field says it is required and it holds no value, and `badInput` while it holds a text that
is not a number.

To assistive technology it is a spin button: its value the committed number, its limits `min` and `max`, its value
text `valueText` or the number as shown with its prefix and suffix. The two steppers are named buttons outside the
focus order.

declarations.name: decimalFromString
declarations.description:
A plain decimal string — ASCII digits, a period, an optional sign and exponent ("12.5", "-0.25", "1e-7") — as a
decimal; null for anything else. The form of the `value` attribute, of a form's value, and of a number as JavaScript
writes it.

declarations.name: decimalOf
declarations.description: A number as the decimal its shortest text names (0.1 is one tenth, not the binary fraction nearest to it); null for what is not a finite number.

declarations.name: canonical
declarations.description: The plain decimal string of a decimal: ASCII digits and a period, never an exponent, never the locale's form ("12.5").

declarations.name: numberOf
declarations.description: The number a decimal is (the nearest one a JavaScript number can hold).

declarations.name: clamp
declarations.description: NMI-20: held within the limits — raised to `min`, lowered to `max` — where each is given.

declarations.name: round
declarations.description: NMI-20: rounded to `digits` digits after the separator, a half away from zero.

declarations.name: stepped
declarations.description:
NMI-22: the `count`th number from `from`, in `direction`, that is `base` plus a whole multiple of `amount` (which is
above zero) — so a number between two such numbers goes to the nearer one in that direction, and not past it, and
each further count is one more `amount` (NMI-23: a page key's ten steps stay on the step's grid, 42 → 62 by 2).

declarations.name: numberForm
declarations.description: The form of a locale `Intl` knows (a tag `supportedLocale()` of src/primitives/locale-date.ts returned).

declarations.name: format
declarations.description:
NMI-17: the number in the locale's form — its digits and its decimal separator, its minus sign before a negative
number, at least `minDigits` and at most `maxDigits` digits after the separator with no other trailing zeros, no
exponent and no grouping separators: what is shown can be typed back.

declarations.name: read
declarations.description:
NMI-18: reads a text as a number, leniently, by the locale's form.

- Spaces, around the number and inside it, and marks of direction are ignored.
- A hyphen-minus or a minus sign before the digits, or a plus sign, is its sign — before or after a prefix.
- `prefix` before the number and `suffix` after it are ignored where they were typed or pasted with it.
- ASCII digits, the locale's own, full-width digits and the decimal digits of other scripts are digits.
- The locale's decimal separator, once, is the separator. So is a period, the separator of a plain decimal number,
  wherever the locale does not group with it: a period in a locale that groups with periods is a grouping separator
  ("1.500" is 1500 in German), and never a guess.
- The locale's grouping separator is ignored wherever it stands between two digits before the separator.
- An empty text, or one of spaces only, is no value. Anything else is not a number.

Asks for a short code sent to the person as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the
One-time-code input (`<tanrei-one-time-code-input>`) it frames: the input under the Field's label, with the Field's
help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/one-time-code-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-one-time-code-field name="code" label="Verification code"
supporting-text="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone." group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*` and
`--tanrei-comp-one-time-code-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one instance is set apart by
setting such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged. One level
down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Verification code"><tanrei-one-time-code-input name="code"
group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-input></tanrei-field>` — for something of the product's own inside the frame.

`value` is at every moment the One-time-code input's, and the four events are that input's own, with this element
as their target: `event.target.value` is the code in every listener. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the code under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `required` is
set and it is empty. Enter in the cells presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the cells, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`.

declarations.name: readCharacter
declarations.description:
OTC-4: one character as the field reads it — a decimal digit of any script and a full-width digit or letter as its
ASCII form, a lower-case letter as its upper-case form — or `null` where the type does not permit it.

declarations.name: readPermitted
declarations.description: The permitted characters of `text`, each read by OTC-4, in order; what is not permitted is dropped.

declarations.name: readValue
declarations.description: OTC-18, OTC-19: a value the product set as the field holds it, and whether anything of it was dropped.

declarations.name: readCode
declarations.description:
OTC-11: a whole text — pasted, dropped, dictated or given by autofill — read as one code, or `null` where it holds
none. White space, hyphens and dashes go; if every remaining character is permitted (and there is one) the code is
the first `length` of them. Otherwise, for digits only, the text is searched: exactly one run of exactly `length`
digits that no other digit adjoins is the code ("Your code is 123456."). Anything else is no code.

declarations.name: furthest
declarations.description: OTC-5: the furthest cell that can be active — the first empty cell, or the last cell while all are filled.

declarations.name: settle
declarations.description: The state with its active cell brought inside what the value allows.

declarations.name: typeCharacter
declarations.description:
OTC-6, OTC-10: one permitted character typed — it stands in the active cell, in place of what the cell holds, and the
active cell moves on (it stays on the last); typed over a selected value it replaces the whole value.

declarations.name: typeText
declarations.description: Characters typed one after another (OTC-6: text an input method commits is read character by character).

declarations.name: removeBackward
declarations.description:
OTC-9, OTC-10: Backspace — a filled active cell loses its character and stays active; an empty one loses the
character before it and the active cell moves there; a selected value is emptied. The rest closes the gap.

declarations.name: removeForward
declarations.description: OTC-9, OTC-10: Delete — the active cell loses its character; a selected value is emptied.

declarations.name: removeRun
declarations.description: The platform's removal of a word or a line: everything before the active cell, or everything from it on.

declarations.name: replaceAll
declarations.description: OTC-11, OTC-18: a whole value taken at once; the active cell is the first empty cell, or the last.

declarations.name: CARET_BLINK_MS
declarations.description:
OTC-7: how long the caret the element draws is shown and hidden for, in milliseconds. The platform's own caret rate
is not exposed to the web; this is the rate browsers' text carets use where the system gives them none. A behaviour
of the platform, not a design value.

Takes a short code sent to the person — a sign-in or verification code — as one text value drawn in separate cells,
so that its length and what is still missing can be seen, and the browser can fill it in one step.

Contract: specs/one-time-code-input.spec.json. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-one-time-code-input-*` token.

One field, not one input per character: in the shadow root there is exactly one native `<input>`, laid over the row,
whose own text and caret are not drawn; the cells, the caret and the group marks under it are a drawing of its value
and are hidden from assistive technology. So it is one Tab stop and one text box whose value is the whole code, and
an input method, the browser's autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), the clipboard and dictation meet one text
input. It has no `maxlength` and no `pattern`: a code pasted as "123 456" would be cut before it could be read.

It has no label, help or error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it, describes it, marks it
required and puts it in its error condition; where the visible label is elsewhere (a dialog's headline), give
`label`, which is never drawn. `<tanrei-field label="Verification code"><tanrei-one-time-code-input name="code"
group-size="3"></tanrei-one-time-code-input></tanrei-field>`.

A permitted character fills the active cell — replacing what it holds — and moves on; other characters are dropped.
Text that is pasted, dropped or filled is read whole as one code ("123 456", "123-456", "Your code is 123456.").
`input` fires on every change by the person, `complete` once after the `input` that leaves the value `length` long,
`change` when a changed value is committed (focus leaves, or Enter), `action` on Enter. Nothing else happens when the
code is complete: checking it is the product's.

Form-associated: it submits the code under `name`, resets to its `value` attribute, is restored on navigation,
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while its Field says it is required and it is empty.

declarations.description:
The head of a page's content: the page's title as its heading, with a sentence that says what the page is, a line of facts about it, the actions for the whole page and the way back up above it — in the content, scrolling with it, laid out by its own width, and never a control. Contract: specs/page-header.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the page's own elements, which stay in the document. The title is the page's own heading — the `h1` a crawler, a reader mode, a page without script and a screen reader all find — and is never hidden, repeated or given another level. ```html …

Announcements

Tokens are derived, and design systems are layers

One value changes in one place, and everything built on it follows.

20 September 2026 The Tanrei team 4 min read
EditShare
 ``` Parts are found by what they are, among the element's children, and are written in the order they are read (PGH-11): `tanrei-breadcrumbs` or `[data-part="breadcrumbs"]`; `[data-part="eyebrow"]`; the title — the heading (`h1` to `h6`), or `[data-part="title"]` for one that is not a heading; the description — the first `p` without a `data-part`, or `[data-part="description"]`; `[data-part="meta"]`, each of whose element children is one item; and `[data-part="actions"]`. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/page-header.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-page-header-*` token — which draws the head before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. Nothing is shown differently before the element is defined. The script adds two things a reader does not see on a content page: the parts of a head **built by script** — `headline`, `description` and `eyebrow` each write their element where the children have none, the heading at `level` — and the debug reports of PGH-23 and PGH-24. The head takes no input and emits no event.

declarations.description:
PGN-2: the places of the numbered form — the pages 1 to `boundaries`, `count − boundaries + 1` to `count`, and the
current page with `siblings` on each side, with an ellipsis in place of the pages left out between two runs, a page
in place of an ellipsis that would stand for that page alone, and more pages on the far side of a current page near
an end, so that the row holds 2 × boundaries + 2 × siblings + 3 places whenever `count` is at least that many. The
algorithm of MUI's `usePagination`, as most pagination of the web counts it.

Moves through the numbered pages of one list — search results, the posts of a blog, the rows of a table: a row of
page numbers with the current page marked and the pages that do not fit left out behind an ellipsis, previous and
next, first and last where the product asks for them, and a short form that says which page of how many.

Contract: specs/pagination.spec.json. The shadow root holds a `nav` named by `label` around one ordered list; each
page and each control is an `<a href>` while `href` holds the place `{page}` — every link the browser's own — and a
`<button>` otherwise. The current page carries `aria-current="page"`; a disabled control is a disabled button, or an
anchor without `href`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`, out of the focus order.

```html
<tanrei-pagination label="Pages" page="3" count="10" previous-label="Previous page" next-label="Next page" page-label="Page {page}"></tanrei-pagination>
```

`change` is fired when the person asks for another page, before the page changes and, for a link, before the browser
follows it; cancel it and the page stays and nothing is followed (a router takes the navigation). Not cancelled, the
element takes the page itself — it needs no listener to page.

`variant="numbered"` draws the compact form where the width its layout gives it is less than its numbered row needs:
the element keeps a copy of that row in its layout at no height, so a layout that sizes it by its content gives it
the row's width, and it compares the two whenever either changes. Every visual value is a
`--tanrei-comp-pagination-*` token; how a press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices
of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.
declarations.name: TanreiPagination

declarations.description: POP-15: how the actions sit (`dev.tanrei.enum`): the first is the fallback.

Shows content a person can read and operate on a small surface that opens beside the control they pressed and stays
with it, without dimming or blocking the rest of the page.

Contract: specs/popover.spec.json. The product owns the control: `anchor` is the id of the element the popover stands
beside, in the popover's own tree (`anchorElement` for an element an id cannot reach), and that element is also the
opener — the one that carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and takes focus back —
unless `opener` / `openerElement` names another (a field that anchors the surface, with a button inside it that
opens it). The product sets `open` when the opener is pressed, and to false when the popover fires `close`: the
popover never opens or closes by itself, on hover, on focus or after a time.

The drawn popover is a `popover="manual"` element in the shadow root, in the top layer (above an open modal
`<dialog>` the element stands in), holding a `role="dialog"` container that is not modal: no scrim, no focus trap,
nothing behind it inert. It is placed against the anchor by script — the side and the alignment `placement` names,
`offset` away and moved along the side by `crossOffset`; flipped to the opposite side, limited to the room where
neither side has enough (its content then scrolls between the header and the actions), shifted along the side and,
in a window smaller than its least size, moved back over the anchor — and follows the anchor while open. When
nothing of the anchor can be seen it fires `close` with the reason `anchor-hidden`.

Focus: opening moves focus to the slotted element marked `autofocus`, else to the container (`initialFocus="anchor"`
leaves it where it is). The popover stands in the focus order directly after its opener wherever it is in the
document: Tab on the opener enters it, Shift+Tab from its first element returns to the opener, Tab from its last
element moves on to what follows the opener. Escape, a press outside, focus leaving, the close button and the
anchor going out of sight each fire `close` once, with the reason; an action never does. An overlay opened from an
element inside it (a menu, a tooltip, another popover, a dialog) is its own: a press or focus in it is not outside,
Escape closes it first, and it closes with the popover. Closing returns focus to the opener if it was inside.

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive` where it is one,
placed as a Button group places them; a Button without a `variant` attribute takes the popover's
(`comp.popover.actions.variant`). `arrow` draws a triangle that points at the anchor, one shape with the container
(unset, the system's `comp.popover.arrow.visible` decides).

Content taller than the room scrolls between the header and the actions, with a divider below the header and one above
the actions (POP-8): for as long as it scrolls while `divider-visibility` is `always` (the default system's), only
while content lies beyond each line while it is `scroll`; `auto` takes `comp.popover.divider.visibility` (POP-38).

In a window narrower than `comp.popover.compact.window-width` (600 in the default system) it takes the bottom
sheet's appearance instead (POP-39 to POP-42): a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, docked to the window's
bottom edge in the bottom sheet's color, elevation and top corners, sliding up over the bottom sheet's scrim — a modal
dialog, with everything behind it inert and focus kept in; Escape, a press on the scrim and the close button fire
`close`. `compact-presentation="own"` keeps it beside its anchor in every window, as `initial-focus="anchor"` always
does. Crossing the width while open changes the presentation at once, focus kept.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-popover-*` tokens, and as a sheet from `--tanrei-comp-bottom-sheet-*`.

declarations.name: styles
declarations.default: [ rangeTrackStyles(PREFIX), css` /* PRG-2, a bar: a segment two fifths of the track long crosses from beyond its start to beyond its end once per cycle, clipped to the track. It is moved by a transform alone — its own length back (two fifths of the track) to two and a half of its lengths on (the whole track) — so no frame of it lays anything out: an inset would be laid out sixty times a second for as long as the bar is shown. --_way is the inline direction (PRG-13). */ .bar.indeterminate { overflow: hidden; --_way: 1; } :host(:dir(rtl)) .bar.indeterminate { --_way: -1; } .bar.indeterminate .track { inset-inline-start: 0; } .bar.indeterminate .indicator { inline-size: 40%; animation: bar-cross ${unsafeCSS(T('motion-cycle-duration'))} ${unsafeCSS(T('motion-cycle-easing'))} infinite; } @keyframes bar-cross { from { transform: translateX(calc(var(--_way) * -100%)); } to { transform: translateX(calc(var(--_way) * 250%)); } } /* PRG-2, a ring: an arc a quarter of the circle long turns clockwise once per cycle at constant speed. */ .ring.indeterminate circle.indicator { stroke-dasharray: max(0px, calc(var(--_c) / 4 - var(--_cap))) var(--_c); } .ring.indeterminate .spin { animation: ring-turn ${unsafeCSS(T('motion-cycle-duration'))} var(--tanrei-sys-motion-easing-linear) infinite; } /* PRG-7: under reduced motion (a value change shows at once: the shared drawing) the indeterminate form stands still — the indicator over the whole track, its opacity easing from 1 to 0 and back once per cycle, over a track that does not move. */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .bar.indeterminate .indicator { inset-inline-start: 0; inline-size: 100%; } .ring.indeterminate circle.indicator { stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-dashoffset: 0; } .bar.indeterminate .indicator, .ring.indeterminate circle.indicator { animation: pulse ${unsafeCSS(T('motion-cycle-duration'))} ${unsafeCSS(T('motion-cycle-easing'))} infinite; } .ring.indeterminate .spin { animation: none; } } /* PRG-14: off screen, nothing runs — over every animation above, the reduced-motion pulse included. */ :host .paused .indicator, :host .paused .spin { animation-play-state: paused; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .bar .track, .bar .indicator, .bar .stop, circle { forced-color-adjust: none; } .bar .track { background: GrayText; } .bar .indicator, .bar .stop { background: Highlight; } circle.track { stroke: GrayText; } circle.indicator { stroke: Highlight; } } `, ]

declarations.description:
Shows how far a task has come, or that it is under way when how far is unknown, as a bar or a ring.

Contract: specs/progress-indicator.spec.json. As a native `<progress>`: no `value` attribute (or removing it, or
`value = null`) is indeterminate. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-progress-indicator-*` token — the bar's
thickness and the ring's size and stroke per size, the track and indicator colors, the ends' shape, the gap after the
indicator, the stop indicator, and the motion of a value change and of the indeterminate cycle. Whether the gap is
drawn at all is `separation` (PRG-17): `auto` follows `comp.progress-indicator.track.separation`, and so the design
system's `sys.behavior.separation`. Whether the stop indicator is drawn is its size alone, under either (PRG-5).

The host is the progressbar (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-label` from `label`, `aria-valuemin` / `-max` / `-now` and
`aria-valuetext` from `value-text` while determinate; `aria-busy="true"` and no value while indeterminate). It is
never focusable and never announces a change by itself. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` a value change shows
at once and the indeterminate form pulses in place; off screen, its animation is paused.

declarations.description: The condition drawn follows what the native radio says, so what is drawn and what is announced cannot disagree.

Lets people choose exactly one option from a small group shown all at once.

Contract: specs/radio-button.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-radio-button-*` tokens, one set
per condition (unselected, selected) and state: how a state looks is the active design system's decision.

A group is the options with one `name` in the same form — or, outside any form, in the same document or shadow root —
as for a native radio. The options keep it themselves: selecting one clears the others (RAD-3), the arrow keys move
through the enabled ones and select as they go (RAD-4), and the group has one tab stop (RAD-5). Put the options in an
element with `role="radiogroup"` and a name (`aria-labelledby`), or in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` (RAD-16).

Form-associated: while selected it submits `value` under `name`, resets to its `checked` attribute and follows a
disabled `<fieldset>`. It selects itself before it fires `input` and `change`; the option it replaced fires nothing.
declarations.name: TanreiRadioButton

declarations.description:
Asks one question that has exactly one answer among a few options shown all at once. Built from a field group
(`<tanrei-field-group>`) and radio buttons (`<tanrei-radio-button>`): the field group itself, in its radio-group
kind — its label, requirement, description and one error — around the product's own radio buttons, whose chosen
value the group holds under one name.

Contract: specs/radio-group.spec.json. `<tanrei-radio-group label="Delivery" name="delivery" value="express">
<tanrei-radio-button value="standard" label="Standard"></tanrei-radio-button>…</tanrei-radio-group>`: the radio
buttons are the element's children and stay in the product's light DOM; inside the group they need no `name`
(RAD-25).

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the field group's own element, with
`kind="radio-group"` and `spacing="controls"`, around a slot, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every
`--tanrei-comp-field-group-*` and `--tanrei-comp-radio-button-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one
instance is set apart by setting such a property on this element. Each of the eleven props of the frame is the field
group's, set on it unchanged. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field-group kind="radio-group"
label="Delivery"><tanrei-radio-button name="delivery" value="standard" label="Standard"></tanrei-radio-button>…
</tanrei-field-group>` — the same picture and the same radio group, without the one value, the one `change` and the
place in a form as one control.

It holds one value. `value` decides which radio button is selected; a person's selection sets `value` and fires
`input` and one `change`, and the radio buttons inside it fire nothing of their own. The arrow keys move through the
enabled radio buttons, wrapping, and select as they go; the group is one stop in the focus order — the selected
radio button, or the first enabled one.

Form-associated: it submits `value` under `name` — also while the radio button of that value is one the product
disabled by itself — returns to its `value` attribute when the form is reset, is restored on navigation, follows
`<fieldset disabled>`, and reports `valueMissing` while `required` and `value` is empty, in the
browser's own words for an unanswered set of radio buttons. It never sets `error` itself.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the radio button that is the stop, and the
radio group that assistive technology is told of — its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled
states and its orientation — is the field group's own element (`label`, never `aria-label` on this one).
declarations.name: TanreiRadioGroup

declarations.description: A suggestion element is data, as an `<option>` in a `<datalist>`: the search draws the row.

declarations.name: rowStyles
declarations.description:
A result's row (SRC-42): a suggestion's row, from the suggestion tokens — the same geometry, colors, states, focus
ring and press answer — drawn by the result itself, because the row is its own anchor. A linked group heading is the
same row (SRC-44).

declarations.name: groupStyles
declarations.description:
A result group (SRC-44): its heading — a quiet title, or a result's row while it has a destination — then its
results, group.gap from what stands above and below it in the view; under a linked heading they step in by
group.indent, hit areas and highlights with them.

A suggestion the search offers while the person types — the spec's item kind `suggestion`: a query they searched
before, or a completion. Choosing it fires `select` and the product sets the value; a thing the product opens is a
`<tanrei-search-result>`. It is data, as an `<option>` in a `<datalist>`: the search draws the row, names it and
answers it; the element itself draws nothing.

declarations.description:
A thing the search found that the person can go to — the spec's item kind `result`: a page, a section of a page, a
message, a file. It is a link, never an option: with `href` its row is an `<a>` in its shadow root, which the browser
follows as it follows any link; without one it is a `<button>`, and `select` is all that happens.

The excerpt is its child content — text with `<mark>` elements around the matches, which is what search engines hand
back (`<tanrei-search-result headline="Layers" href="/tokens/#layers">A layer changes a <mark>token</mark>.</tanrei-search-result>`)
— or, while it has no child content, the `excerpt` runs. Putting an engine's HTML there is the product's act: the
element never parses a string as markup.

Place it in a `<tanrei-search>` or a `<tanrei-search-result-group>`: the search answers its press and its keys (Down
and Up Arrow move through the results; typing returns to the input) and fires `select` when it is activated in place.

Results that belong together, under one heading — the spec's item kind `result-group`: the sections found in one
page, or the results of one kind. With `href` its heading is itself a result (the page), drawn as a result's row, and
its `<tanrei-search-result>` children are inset under it as its parts; without one its heading is a quiet title.

declarations.description:
Lets people search the product from a bar or a compact trigger, and offers suggestions and results while they type in
a view under the bar, in a dialog or over the whole screen.

Contract: specs/search.spec.json. The value is edited in a native `<input type="search" enterkeyhint="search">` in the
shadow root, as the text field's, with the browser's own cancel button hidden: the search draws its own
clear button. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-search-*` tokens, its one condition's parts by state.

Opening and closing: a press on the bar, typing or Down Arrow opens the view (focus alone never does); Escape, a
chosen suggestion, submitting, the back button, and — docked — a press outside, Tab and focus leaving close it. The
element sets its own `expanded` and then fires `toggle`, whose `detail` holds `expanded` and, when closing, `reason`.
Set `expanded` yourself to open or close it without an event.

`docked` (the default) opens a view under the bar: a manual popover in the top layer, placed by script (flipped above
the bar when there is more room there), following the bar. Focus stays in the input — the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern:
the input controls the suggestions' listbox and names the active suggestion as its active descendant. A press outside
closes it AND reaches the element under it. `full-screen` opens a modal `<dialog>` over the whole window with its own
header (a back button, the input, the clear button); it takes focus, keeps it, and gives it back to the bar's input.

A site search. `bar="button"` draws a trigger shaped like the bar — the search glyph, the placeholder
and the shortcut hint — and `bar="icon"` an icon-only Button; a trigger opens a modal view, where the input is
(`presentation="dialog"`: a `<dialog>` hung from the top of the window over a scrim, a press on which closes it,
its header starting with the same back button as the full-screen view's, so it can be left by Tab and Enter alone;
`docked` with a trigger opens as `dialog`). `shortcut` (chords separated by spaces, as the keyboard shortcut's `keys`)
is written as a hint — a line of text, no keycaps — and exposed as `aria-keyshortcuts`; it makes the keys work only with `bind-shortcut`, which adds one
`keydown` listener on the window while the element is connected and enabled. The results are
`<tanrei-search-result>` and `<tanrei-search-result-group>` children: links, never options, reached from the input
with Down Arrow (real focus), left with Up Arrow or by typing. `status` and `status-text` draw the status row — a
`role="status"` element that exists from the first render (`role="alert"` while `status="error"`). The search never
runs a query: listen to `input`, then set the results, `status` and `status-text`.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value`, and Enter (with no suggestion active) requests its form's
submission after `submit`, unless `submit` was cancelled. The `inline` attribute, for tests and documentation, draws
the open view in place: the docked view under the bar, the full-screen view filling the element.

members.name: bindShortcut
members.description:

is in an element that takes text are left alone. Off by default.

members.name: focus
members.description:

removes the element that held it, as the search's own clear button does (SRC-10): behind an open modal view the

Lets people choose one option, or several, from two to five related options drawn side by side as the joined
segments of one control.

Contract: specs/segmented-button.spec.json. `<tanrei-segment>` children are the segments, in order. The selection is
the set's: `value` names the selected segment while `selection` is `single` (`null` selects none), and
`values` the selected segments while it is `multiple`. The set sets them itself when a segment is activated — by
pointer, touch, Enter, Space, or (single) the arrow keys, which select the segment they reach — and then fires
`change`, as a native control does.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-segmented-button-*` tokens: the set's fill, outline, corners and
padding, the dividers, per size the segments' height, paddings, gap, label style, icon and check sizes, and per
condition (unselected, selected) and state each segment's colors and elevation. How a press is answered and how
keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`), read from the cascade.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose one value from a closed list as one complete field of a form. Built from a Field
(`<tanrei-field>`) and the Select (`<tanrei-select>`) it frames: the trigger and its list under the Field's label —
or, in the filled and the outlined look, with the label floating in the box — with the Field's help and its error,
tied together for assistive technology and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/select-field.spec.json.

```html
<tanrei-select-field name="country" label="Country" required supporting-text="Where your invoices are addressed.">
  <tanrei-option value="jp">Japan</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="ke">Kenya</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-select-field>
```

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-select-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one select field is set apart by setting such a property on this
element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`,
`error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the
Field's, every other one the select's. One level down, the same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Country"
required><tanrei-select name="country">…options…</tanrei-select></tanrei-field>` — and the box alone,
where a label stands elsewhere (a bar, a toolbar, a column of a table), is `<tanrei-select>` with a `label` of its
own.

The options are its `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` children, exactly as a select's: they stay the
product's, are never moved or copied, and reach the select inside through the default slot, which the select reads.
Replacing them by hand works as on a select.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (SEF-1): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` and `open` are at every moment the select's, read through to it and never copied, and the two events are
that select's own, with this element as their target: `event.target.value` and `event.target.open` are new in every
listener. It dispatches none itself. `toggle` is composed and does not bubble: it is heard on this element and by no
ancestor.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports a missing value while `required` is
set and the value is empty.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the select's trigger, and its name is `label`
(with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row focuses the trigger and
opens nothing; a press on the trigger opens the list; a press on the help or the error text does nothing.

declarations.description:
The open axes (SEL-60): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same
functions as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported
in debug builds.

Lets people choose one value from a closed list: a trigger that looks and measures like a text input's box and
shows the chosen option, and a list of options, optionally grouped, that opens from it. The bare control: it draws
no label row, no requirement mark, no help and no error text.

Contract: specs/select.spec.json. The options are `<tanrei-option>` children, optionally in
`<tanrei-option-group>` elements (the pair a combobox holds too); the select reads them — and reads them again when
they change — and renders the rows itself. Every visual value is a token: the trigger is drawn from
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set every input box is drawn from (SEL-65), and the list from
`--tanrei-comp-select-*`, which hold the menu's values in every shipped design system.

```html
<tanrei-select size="small" label="Theme" value="auto">
  <tanrei-option value="auto">Follow the device</tanrei-option>
  <tanrei-option value="light">Light</tanrei-option>
</tanrei-select>
```

Alone it is for a place where its label stands elsewhere or is plain from where it stands — a theme or a language
in a bar, a toolbar, a column of a table — and `label` names it for assistive technology; a filled or an outlined
select also draws that name, floating in its box. In a form it stands in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it,
describes it and marks it: that pair as one element is `<tanrei-select-field>`. The select says to its Field what
only it knows (`src/primitives/field.ts`): that it draws the label while its look floats one, where its value
starts and ends, and that it is drawn focused while its list is open.

Bare and given no width it is an inline box as wide as its widest option; in a Field it is a block that fills the
Field's width.

It is a form-associated element: it takes `name`, submits `value`, resets to the `value` attribute, is restored on
navigation, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while the Field that frames it says it is
required and `value` is empty. It never validates beyond that: `error` is the product's to set.

The options may also reach it through a `<slot>` among its children: the elements assigned to that slot stand in
the slot's place. That is how a select field's options reach the select inside it, and how a product's own element
passes options on (`<tanrei-select label="Plan"><slot></slot></tanrei-select>` in its shadow root).

The pattern is the select-only combobox. Focus stays on the trigger while the list is open and one option is the
active one: Enter, Space, Down or Up Arrow, or a printable character open the list; the arrow keys, Home, End, Page
Down and Page Up and typing move the active option; Enter or Space choose it; Escape, Tab, a press outside or on the
trigger close the list without choosing. The value changes only when the person confirms an option.

An option is a value, never a destination: a list of places to go is a menu or links.

declarations.name: sideSheetRelease
declarations.description:
SSH-4: whether a released drag asks to close — past half the sheet's width toward its end edge, or flung that way.
`distance` is how far the sheet is drawn from where it rests, toward the end edge; `velocity` the pointer's speed that
way at the release, in px per ms.

Shows supplementary content or a secondary task in a panel at the end edge, with a headline, a close button and
actions: `standard`, beside the content in the layout (a layout region), where actions are optional, or
`modal`, over the content with a scrim, holding focus until it closes (a modal overlay), with at least one
action (SSH-16).

Contract: specs/side-sheet.spec.json. The content is the default slot. The header holds `headline` (the sheet's
accessible name, a heading) and, while `closable` (the default; the attribute `not-closable` turns it off), an
icon-only `<tanrei-button>` of the small size showing the close glyph, named by `close-label`, in the variant
`comp.side-sheet.close-button.variant` names (tonal in the default system), as every host's close button is.

The actions are `<tanrei-button slot="actions">` children, each marked `confirming` or `dismissive`, placed below a
divider as a full-width Button group places them: dismissive at the start and confirming at the end of a row the
actions share equally, confirming on top of a column when a label does not fit its share (or, where the system's
`actions.arrangement` is `start`, at their own widths from the start edge). Focus and assistive technology follow that
order. A Button without a `variant` attribute takes the sheet's (`comp.side-sheet.actions.variant`, tonal in the
default system). Actions never close the sheet: close it from their handlers.

Controlled: the sheet never closes itself. It fires `close` with a reason — its close button in either variant, and for
a modal sheet a press on the scrim, Escape, the platform's back or a drag toward its end edge — and you set `open` to
false. A product that does not close it after a drag sees it slide back.

Standard: an `<aside>` (a complementary landmark) named by the headline; place it as the last item of a flex row (the
full height of that row). Its width animates while open changes, the content beside it resizing. Opening it moves focus
in, closing it with focus inside gives focus back, Tab leaves it open, and Escape and drags do nothing.

Modal: a native `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with `showModal()`, at the window's end edge in the top layer over
`::backdrop` (the scrim), everything else inert, the page held from scrolling and focus kept inside. Focus goes to the
slotted element marked `autofocus`, else the sheet (also when it is mounted open), and returns where it was when it
closes.

The content scrolls between the header and the actions. The divider below the header is drawn whenever the header is
while `divider-visibility` is `always` (the default system's), as the one above the actions is, and only while the
content is scrolled from its top while it is `scroll`; `auto` takes `comp.side-sheet.divider.visibility` (SSH-19,
SSH-23). While the on-screen keyboard covers the bottom of the sheet, the actions sit directly above it (the
`visualViewport`).

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-side-sheet-*` tokens. The color reaches under
`env(safe-area-inset-*)` at the end, top and bottom.

declarations.description:
Stands where content will be while it loads: quiet placeholders in the shape of what is coming — lines of text, a block, a circle — that keep the box the content will take, in a region that says once that it is busy. Contract: specs/skeleton.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the box around the product's own layout, and a placeholder is the product's own empty element with the class `tanrei-skeleton-placeholder`. ```html

``` A placeholder: `data-shape` (`text`, the default and what an unknown value draws; `block`; `circle`), `data-lines` (text: how many lines) and the CSS properties `inline-size` and `block-size` for its sizes. A text placeholder takes the text style of where it stands — the inherited `font` — so it goes where the text will be, and is exactly its lines high. Placeholders that are the skeleton's own children are stacked, `container.gap` apart; anything else is the product's own layout inside the skeleton. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/skeleton.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-skeleton-*` token — which draws the skeleton before and without this script: the shapes, the show delay (the skeleton is hidden for its length, with its box kept), the pulse, stillness under reduced motion, outlines in forced colors. The element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, and what a stylesheet cannot say: once the delay has passed it is a progressbar with no value (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-label` from `label`, else from the product's words, `loadingLabel`) — unless `decorative`, or inside another skeleton, when it is kept from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`); what it holds is `inert`; its animation is held while it cannot be seen; a wave, which has to be measured, is drawn (before the element is defined a wave is a pulse); and a debug build reports what it ignored. A page that must be right before its script runs writes `role`, `aria-busy` and `aria-label` itself, and the element leaves what it finds. Insert it when the wait starts and remove it when the wait ends. It takes no input and emits no event.

declarations.description:
Lets people choose a value, or a range of values, on a scale as one complete field. Built from a Field
(`<tanrei-field>`) and the Slider (`<tanrei-slider>`) it frames: the track under the Field's label, with the value
in words at the end of the label row, the Field's help and its error, tied together for assistive technology and
taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/slider-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-slider-field name="text-size" label="Text size"
supporting-text="Applies to every page." min="50" max="200" step="10" value="120"></tanrei-slider-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*` and `--tanrei-comp-slider-*`
value reaches the members by inheritance, and one slider field is set apart by setting such a property on this
element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`, `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`,
`error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`, `required-text` and `optional-text` are the
Field's, every other one the Slider's — `end-label` is the Slider's `label`, the name of a range's end handle,
because `label` is the visible name here. It has no orientation: the track runs along the line. One level down, the
same by hand: `<tanrei-field label="Text size" value-text="120"><tanrei-slider name="text-size" min="50" max="200"
step="10" value="120"></tanrei-slider></tanrei-field>`, with the product writing the Field's `value-text` at each
`input` (`field.valueText = slider.shownValueText`).

That is the one thing it does that the pair by hand does not: unless `value-hidden` is set it gives its Field, as
the value text at the end of the label row, the words its Slider gives each handle — `value-text` (and
`start-value-text`), or what `formatValue` writes, or the number in the page's locale — at every change, a range's
two in reading order with an en dash between. `formatValue` is a property, never an attribute: a function the
product gives once, from a value to its words (`field.formatValue = (value) => percent.format(value / 100)`). It
writes no number, unit or word itself.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its track fills it: give it a narrower place for a shorter track.

`value` and `startValue` are at every moment the Slider's, and the two events are that Slider's own, with this
element as their target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener. It dispatches none itself.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — a range the start value and then the value, under the one name;
nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` and `start-value` attributes, is restored on navigation and follows a
disabled `<fieldset>`.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the handle — a range's start handle — and its
name is `label` (with `label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A range's two handles are named by
`start-label` and `end-label`. A press on the label row focuses the handle and changes no value; a press on the
help or the error text does nothing.

declarations.name: TOUCH_SLOP
declarations.description:
How far a touch travels along the track before it is a drag, or across it before it is left to the page's scroll
(SLD-2: "the platform's touch slop"). The web does not expose the platform's value; this is Android's
`ViewConfiguration` default, as React Native's slider uses. A behaviour of the platform, not a design value.

declarations.name: sliderScale
declarations.description:
The slider's numbers (SLD-1, SLD-3, SLD-22): the range, the keyboard step, and the snap of a value — clamped between
`low` and `high` (min and max by default), and while step is above 0 on min plus a whole multiple of step, the nearest.

Lets people choose a value, or a range of values, from a continuous or stepped scale by dragging a handle along a
track.

Contract: specs/slider.spec.json. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-slider-*` token: per size the track's
thickness and corners, the handle's height and the stop dots' size; the round state layer, the handle's width, fill,
outline color and elevation, the track, active track and stop-dot colors in each state; the outline's width, the gap,
the value indicator and the motion. The handle is its fill with its outline drawn over it, inside its edge (SLD-24).

Each handle is an element with `role="slider"` in the shadow root (its own Tab stop, the start handle first), named by
`label` (a range's start handle by `start-label`), with `aria-valuemin` / `-max` (bounded by the other handle in a
range), `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext` (`value-text`, or what `formatValue` writes, or the value in the page's
locale) and `aria-orientation`. `formatValue` is a function the product gives once, as a property, from a value to
its words (`slider.formatValue = (value) => percent.format(value / 100)`): it is asked for each handle at every
change of a value. `shownValueText` (and `shownStartValueText`) is the value text of a handle as it is spoken now,
read-only: what a product that frames the slider by hand gives its Field's `value-text` at each `input`.
The whole slider is the hit area: a press moves the nearer handle there and a drag follows it; the arrow keys, Page
Up / Down, Home and End move the focused handle. It sets its own `value` (and `startValue`) before it fires `input`
(every change) and `change` (a finished change). A value the product sets fires neither and moves over the value
motion.

Form-associated: it submits `value` under `name` (a range submits `start-value`, then `value`, under the same name),
resets to its attributes and follows a disabled `<fieldset>`.

Contract: specs/snackbar.spec.json. Shown by a `<tanrei-snackbar-host>` (`host.show({ message, action })`), which
queues, places, times, announces and closes it. Drawn outside a host (a documentation page, a test) it is drawn in
place, at rest: no timeout, queue, entrance or announcement (SNK-19); it still fires `action`, `dismiss` and
`expandedchange`.

chooses (`--tanrei-comp-snackbar-container-inverse`, off in the default system). That and its `status` make its form,
one of ten, and the form changes colors only (SNK-30).

bar from `--tanrei-comp-snackbar-container-*`, or its form's `-<status>-*`, `-inverse-*` or `-inverse-<status>-*`. The
expand and close buttons are icon-only `<tanrei-button>`s of the small size (SNK-34), in the variant
`--tanrei-comp-snackbar-close-button-variant` names and in the form's tone: its message color and its focus color,
which they draw their glyph, their circle and their states in (BTN-45). The keyboard focus indicator's outer stroke is
the form's `-focus-ring-color` (SNK-3). The content is aligned to the top of the bar (SNK-29).

declarations.description:
Shows snackbars, one at a time, in the order they were asked for (SNK-12), at the bottom of the window (SNK-13) or,
with `placement="top-end"`, at its top end (SNK-35) — below a sticky header of `<tanrei-app-shell>`, whose height it
reads from `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset` on the document's root.
Place it once, as the last element of the page: its place in the focus order is where a snackbar's controls are
(SNK-11). It holds the two live regions their messages are announced in (SNK-10) — polite (`role="status"`) for the
default, info and success forms, assertive (`role="alert"`) for warning and error — so it must be in the document
before the first one.

declarations.description: The handle's progress from its unselected position (0) to its selected one (1): what a drag writes on `.root`.

Turns one setting on or off, taking effect at once, with a handle that follows a finger dragged along the track.

Contract: specs/switch.spec.json. Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-switch-*` tokens, one set per condition
(unselected, selected) and state — the handle's color, size and elevation included: how a state looks is the active
design system's decision. The handle travels to the inline end when on (the left in right-to-left layouts).

A tap switches it. A drag along the track (touch, pen or mouse; from the track, the handle or the target around them,
not from the label) carries the handle with the pointer, and every part that differs between off and on is drawn at
the handle's progress between the two, with no threshold. `checked`, the form value and the exposed state change
when the pointer is released — to the nearer side, or the side a fling is toward — with one `input` and one `change`;
Escape, a cancelled pointer, `disabled` or a `checked` set meanwhile return the handle and fire nothing.

Form-associated: while checked it submits `value` (default "on") under `name`, resets to its `checked` attribute and
follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, as a native checkbox does. It switches its own `checked` before it fires `input` and
`change`. The semantics are a native checkbox with the role switch in the shadow root, named by `label`; a click on
the visible label toggles it.
