declarations.description:
The view (TBV-11) is a column: its own row (TBV-16), slotted at the top across its whole width at the row's own
height, and the container directly below it with no space between them. The row is outside the container, so no
switch moves, fades, blurs or clips it (TBV-5), and the container's touch-action does not reach it (TBV-3).

The container (TBV-5, TBV-11): every panel in the same grid cell, so the view is as tall as its row plus the panel it
shows — and the taller of two while a switch draws both — or, when the product sizes the view, the container fills
what the row leaves and each panel scrolls inside it. It clips the panels to its corners (comp.tab-view.container.shape), so neither the travel nor the blur is
drawn outside it. While a swipe is possible its touch-action leaves only vertical panning (and zoom) to the browser,
so a sideways drag reaches the view's pointer events (TBV-3).

The probe draws nothing: the view reads the switch's look and timing through its real properties when a switch or a
drag starts (TBV-4…7) — the travel's distance as a width, the blur as a height, the share of the width as a flex
factor, the opacity as itself, the motion as a transition that names no property — so a token is never parsed, and
a bare `0` a layer writes for a dimension reads as 0. Where motion is reduced the distance, its share and the blur are
0 and the motion is the fade's (TBV-7). The fade's own motion is read through the probe's animation, which names no
animation: it is what a view whose transition is fade switches over (TBV-22).

Shows the view of the selected tab under its own row of tabs, or linked to a row of `<tanrei-tabs>` placed elsewhere,
and lets a person swipe from view to view with the tabs' indicator following the finger.

Contract: specs/tab-view.spec.json. The view's `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children are its panels. By default (`tabs` empty)
the view draws its own row (TBV-16): a `<tanrei-tabs>` it places as its first light-DOM child, in its `tabs` slot above
the panels, with one `<tanrei-tab>` per panel made from the panel's `value`, `label`, `icon`, `label-hidden` and
`disabled`; the row's `variant`, `size`, `track`, `full-width` and `label` are the view's. The product does not edit that row. Linked
(TBV-17): `tabs` is the id of a `<tanrei-tabs>` in the same tree (as `popovertarget` is), and the `tabsElement` property
sets the element itself; either one set means the view draws no row, even while that element is missing. Either way
the panels are matched to the tabs by `value` and take the place of the row's own panels (TAB-13), and the selected
panel is the view's `value`, kept equal to the tabs' `value` in both directions without an event.

Every selection is announced once. With its own row the view fires `change` for a tab and for a swipe; the row's own
`change` never fires (TBV-18). Linked, a selection on the tabs is announced by the tabs' `change`, and a swipe by the
view's. The view sets its `value` (and the tabs') before `change` fires, as a native control does.

A switch — from the tabs, the product, or the rest of a released swipe — runs over `motion.switch-duration`: the old
panel moves `transition.distance` (plus `transition.distance-fraction` of the width) toward the edge it leaves by,
fading toward `transition.opacity` and blurring toward `transition.blur`, while the new one arrives from the other side.
Where motion is reduced only the fade is left, over `motion.fade-duration`. A drag by touch or pen that goes further
sideways than up or down holds the switch under the finger and sets the tabs' `indicatorOffset` in every frame; it
commits past half the width or on a fling toward the tab. Mouse, trackpad and wheel never swipe: the tabs are the way.

`transition` names the form of a switch: `slide` as above, `fade` — the two panels crossfade in place, over
`motion.fade-duration` — and `none`, which shows the new panel whole in the frame the selection is made and gives the
row the view draws the tabs' `transition="none"`, so that its indicator is on the new tab in that frame too; a swipe
is still taken, the panel staying at rest under it while the indicator follows the finger. `auto`, the default, is
the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-tab-view-motion-transition`).

A drag across the row — the view's own, or the linked one — is the tabs' (TAB-28): their indicator follows the pointer
and the view takes no drag meanwhile. The shown panel stays at rest for its whole length, because no tab is selected
before the release; the release switches to the chosen tab's panel as any selection does, and with its own row the
view announces it, once.

declarations.description:
Lists the headings of the page being read as links to them and marks the one whose section is being read. Sub-headings are set in under their heading; where there is no room beside the text, the compact presentation is one row that names the current section and opens the same list. Contract: specs/table-of-contents.spec.json. The items are the product's own nested list of anchors, which stay in the document (TOC-6): before the element is defined, and with scripting off, the page holds a plain list of links that work. ```html
  • Install
    • npm
  • Configure
 ``` An item is an `
  • ` whose first child is its anchor — `href` is the anchor's own attribute and the label its text — and the item's own items are a list after the anchor, inside the same `
  • `. Everything drawn on the list is `@tanrei/web/table-of-contents.css` (every value a `--tanrei-comp-table-of-contents-*` token), which draws it before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The shadow root holds only what the product did not write: a `
    ` named by `label`, the title, and the compact presentation's block and row. Which item is current (`tracking="auto"`, TOC-9 to TOC-16): the last item, in the page's order, whose target has reached the line — where the browser itself rests a target it is sent to: the top of the view that scrolls the targets, plus that view's `scroll-padding-block-start`, plus the target's own `scroll-margin-block-start`. So a fixed header and the space a heading keeps above itself are declared once, in CSS, and never passed to the element. It reads the view on `scroll` (one passive listener, coalesced to a frame), on `resize` and when what it holds changes size; at rest it runs nothing. It never scrolls the view that holds the targets, never writes the address and never focuses anything in the content.

declarations.description:
Presents data that has rows and columns, with named columns, optional row headers, a caption and footer rows. A price list, a comparison, a list of settings, a status of many things. It scrolls in its own box when it does not fit. A column's header can ask for the rows in its order (`sort`); the table itself never sorts, filters, fetches or pages: it draws the rows it is given, in the order it is given them. Contract: specs/table.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: it is the scroll box around the product's own native table, which stays in the document and is never given another `display` — its semantics, a crawler's reading, copy and paste as a table and a screen reader's table navigation are the browser's own. ```html
Visits by region
RegionJanuary
Islands212
All regions6,846
``` A column is a `` of the `` row: its text is the header, `data-align="start | center | end"` says where the column's cells sit and `data-wrap="false"` keeps them on one line. A row is a ``; a footer row is a `` in ``. A cell is a ``, or a `` for the header of its row, and holds text, any view of the product's, or nothing. A cell may name its own `data-align` and `data-wrap`; a Markdown renderer's `align` is read as well (left and right as start and end). Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/table.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-table-*` token — which draws the table before and without this script; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: while the box scrolls it is a focus stop and a region with the table's name (`tabindex`, `role`, `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`), and the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End scroll it as the browser scrolls a region; a hairline along an inline edge of the box says that columns lie beyond it; a column's alignment reaches its cells; a first column that is kept in view lets go where it would take more than half of the box. A column that can be sorted: its header cell says the order the rows are in — `aria-sort="none"`, `"ascending"` or `"descending"` — and holds the product's own ` ``` No rows: `…`, holding the product's Empty state (or its sentence, in an element). The status line: `

1–20 of 132

…
` after the table, inside the element, holding the product's sentence and its pagination; the `status` attribute is a convenience that writes the paragraph. Rows that can be chosen: `selection="multiple"`, and a first cell `` in every row — in the header row holding the checkbox for every row, in a body row that has a `data-value` holding that row's checkbox (``, or a native ``), and empty in a footer row, a placeholder row and a row that cannot be chosen. A chosen row carries `data-selected`. The table holds the selection: a change of a checkbox writes `data-selected` on its row and emits `selectionchange` with the values of the chosen rows; the product writes `data-selected` to choose a row itself, and nothing is emitted for it. The header's checkbox is kept checked, mixed or unchecked, disabled with no row to choose, and named by `select-all-label` or the product's words (`selectAllLabel`). A row's checkbox that has no name of its own is named by the row's header cell. The table stays a table: no grid, no selected state on a row. For a pointer the whole row is its checkbox's target: a click anywhere on it changes the checkbox, except on what a cell holds that answers a press itself (a link, a button, a field), at the end of a drag or a text selection, with a modifier key, or on the second click of a double click; the row is drawn hovered and pressed as one. The keyboard stays on the checkbox. One row at most: `selection="single"`, and in each body row's selection cell a radio button in place of the checkbox (``, or a native ``); the header row's selection cell stays empty. The radio buttons share one name — the element gives one to those that have none — so they are one group: one Tab stop, the arrow keys move the choice from row to row. Choosing a row lets the chosen one go, and `selectionchange` carries the one value; the chosen row's radio button, or a press on that row, changes nothing (a radio is not cleared by its own activation). To choose no row again, remove `data-selected` yourself. ```html
Name
Kettle
``` Loading: `loading` says that the product is fetching rows. The table is exposed as busy (`aria-busy` on the table) and draws what it is given — the rows it had, or rows `` whose cells are empty or hold a Skeleton's placeholder (``). Nothing is dimmed or disabled. Without a sortable column and with `selection` none the table takes no input and emits no event. A table inside a cell is the product's content and is not drawn by this one. Cells that span (`colspan`, `rowspan`) and a second header row work as HTML does and take the same cell styles.

declarations.description:
The row (TAB-14, TAB-15, TAB-20, TAB-21, TAB-27): the tab list; the divider along its whole bottom; and the track,
which is the scroller — one constant color per variant, its corners track.shape, no outline — that lays the tabs out
track.padding in from its ends, each its content's width (hug, the default: the track then ends with its last tab)
or an equal share of the row (`full-width`), and scrolls them sideways inside itself when they do not fit, clipped to
its shape. The panels follow the row.

declarations.name: tabStyles
declarations.description:
One tab (TAB-3…6, TAB-8…10, TAB-14, TAB-16, TAB-18, TAB-19, TAB-23, TAB-24): the whole tab answers the pointer; its
container (.box) — the state layer and the ripple — is drawn in the box the active indicator has on this tab, or would
have if it were selected, never on the tab's rectangle; its icon and label on one line, centred and kept clear of the
underline; the covered layer over them, which is the indicator's piece on this tab and carries the covered copy of
the icon and label; the underline's piece on its bottom edge (both clipped by the row to where the indicator is,
TAB-17); and, above them all, the focus ring around the same box (.ring).

declarations.name: panelStyles
declarations.description:
A tab panel (TAB-13, TBV-9, TBV-10): shown only while its tab is selected; a Tab stop itself when it holds nothing
focusable. A panel of a `<tanrei-tab-view>` (`.inside`) draws its ring inside its edge — the view clips what is drawn
outside it — with its corners following comp.tab-view.container.shape; the tabs' own panel draws it around its edge.

One tab of a row — the spec's item kind `tab`: a label, an optional icon, and the value that selects it.
Placed as a child of `<tanrei-tabs>`, as `<option>` in a `<select>`; the row decides whether it is selected, which tab
is the Tab stop, and answers its activation.

The host carries the tab's semantics — the tab role, its selected state, its position, the number of tabs and its
name, its label whether or not the label is drawn — and takes focus itself.

A label that does not fit its tab (a row that fills) is truncated with an ellipsis and shown whole in a plain tooltip on
hover and keyboard focus; it stays the tab's whole accessible name, and the tooltip is not exposed a second time.

declarations.description:
Switches between views of the same subject with a row of labelled tabs, one of them selected, above the view it shows.

Contract: specs/tabs.spec.json. `<tanrei-tab>` children are the tabs, in order; `<tanrei-tab-panel>` children after
them are the panels, matched to tabs by `value` — or, where a `<tanrei-tab-view tabs="<this row's id>">` is linked to
the row, the view's panels take their place (TAB-13), and the view draws the indicator between two tabs while it is
swiped (`indicatorOffset`, TAB-26). The row's selected tab is its `value`, as a `<select>`'s: `null`
selects the first enabled tab. The row sets it when a tab is activated — by pointer, touch, Enter, Space, or the arrow
keys, which select the tab they reach (automatic activation) — and then fires `change`.

Three variants say how much the selection weighs — `primary`, `secondary`, and `tonal`, the quiet row whose indicator
is a soft layer under a darker label — and are one control in everything else. `size` is the row's height (`medium`,
the default, and `small`, which stands in a header beside small controls: it stays as low as it is, and a press just
above or below it, on nothing that would answer the press itself, still selects the tab in line with it).

The row sits on a track: one constant color per variant, the same whichever tab is selected (a capsule in the
default system); `track="false"` fills none and changes nothing else, `track` draws it whatever the design system
says, and without the attribute the system decides (`--tanrei-comp-tabs-track-visible`). The tabs hug their content and scroll sideways inside the track (the default), or share the row's
width (`full-width`), truncating a label that does not fit. The selected tab's active indicator — the thumb on the
track: as tall as the row less the track's padding on every tab, a capsule as wide as the tab's content plus its
padding or a circle where that content is not wider than it is tall, and the tab's whole share in a row that fills —
slides to a newly selected tab with the underline, and each label and icon it passes over takes its covered colors
where it is covered.

A drag across the row — by touch, a pen or a mouse, past 8 px and further sideways than up or down — carries the
indicator with the pointer, its place, its width and the covered colors changing continuously. Nothing is selected
before the release, which chooses the nearer of the two tabs the indicator lies between (or the one a fling is
toward), sets `value` and fires `change` once; Escape, a cancelled pointer, or `value` set meanwhile returns it.

`transition` says how a new selection is drawn: `slide` as above, `none` whole in one frame — nothing travels and no
color fades between selected and not, a tab out of view is brought in at once, and a drag still carries the indicator
and lands at once on release — and `auto`, the default, as the design system says
(`--tanrei-comp-tabs-motion-transition`). Hover, focus and press are answered the same under each.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-tabs-*` tokens, per variant, look (selected or not) and state. How a
press is answered and how keyboard focus is drawn are the system's choices of kind (`--tanrei-sys-behavior-*`),
read from the cascade.

members.name: track

declarations.default: [ { name: 'spacing', core: CORE_SPACINGS, default: DEFAULT_SPACING, rules: (value, selector) => spacingBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SPACING), probe: (value) => `${PREFIX}-gap-${value}` }, ]
declarations.description: The open axis (TGR-16): a spacing the active design system does not have is drawn as `tags` and reported.

Lays out a set of tags or chips in lines that wrap, spaced for what it holds, and exposes the set as one named list.

Contract: specs/tag-group.spec.json. It reads four tokens (`--tanrei-comp-tag-group-gap-*` and `-row-gap-*`, one pair
per `spacing`) and draws nothing of its own: no container, no fill, no edge, no padding, and not its `label`. Its
members are `<tanrei-tag>` and `<tanrei-chip>` children, which stay in your DOM where you wrote them, drawn from
their own tokens at their own size, with their own states, events, names and Tab stops (TGR-6). The group takes no
focus, handles no key, keeps no selection, does not make filter chips exclusive and fires no event.

It is a list (TGR-7): the shadow root holds one element with the list role, named by `label`, around the slot, and
each member is given `role="listitem"` while it is in the group — the attribute is written on your element where it
has no `role` of its own, and taken back when it leaves. A chip's button or link, with its state, is inside its item.

`spacing` says what the set holds. Lines of tags stand as close as the tags along a line; lines of chips stand far
enough apart that each chip keeps its whole touch target, and a chip in a group ends its hit area at the middle of
the gap to its neighbour — along a line, and between two lines while the set wraps (TGR-5). A set of chips wants
`spacing="chips"`.

When a member leaves while focus is on it — on a chip or on its remove action — focus goes to the chip that followed
it, or to the one before where none follows (TGR-9). The group removes nothing itself: on a chip's `remove` you take
the element out. When the last member that takes focus has gone the group has nowhere to put it; move it yourself to
the control the set belongs to. A group with no member draws nothing, takes no space and exposes nothing (TGR-8).

It supplies no words: the name of the set is yours, in `label`.

Names a category or a status with a short static label, quietly, outlined or filled, in the colors of a status where it has one. It is text, never a control. Contract: specs/tag.spec.json. ``, with a glyph of the icon set in the `icon` slot (`sell`) or a `dot` before the label. Every visual value is a `--tanrei-comp-tag-*` token, one set per variant and status; how far its corners ease is the system's amount (`--tanrei-sys-shape-corner-smoothing`). A tag has no role, no name, no state and no event: its label is read where it sits, as text. It takes no input and no focus, and input over it reaches the element that holds it — a link, a button, a list item — which draws its own states. A label that must be pressed, switched or removed is a chip; one that leads somewhere is a link; a dot or a count on another element is a badge. Inside something disabled — a disabled field's label, a disabled row — `disabled` draws it in its look's disabled colors, so that it fades with what holds it; it changes nothing else. A status changes colors only, and color alone never says it: the label does ("Failed"), or `statusLabel` adds it in words for assistive technology ("Error", read as "Error, 3 builds") without drawing it. An outlined tag with a status always draws the dot, because nothing else in that look shows the status. The glyph and the dot are decorative. The label is one line. declarations.description:
Lets people enter and edit text as one complete field. Built from a Field (`<tanrei-field>`) and the Text input
(`<tanrei-text-input>`) it frames: the box under the Field's label — or, in the filled and the outlined look, with
the label floating in it — with the Field's help, its error and the count, tied together for assistive technology
and taking part in a form as one control.

Contract: specs/text-field.spec.json. `<tanrei-text-field name="email" label="Email" type="email"
autocomplete="email" required supporting-text="We never share your address."></tanrei-text-field>`.

Composed (`src/primitives/composed.ts`): its shadow root holds the two members' own elements and nothing
else, so it draws nothing of its own and has no token — every `--tanrei-comp-field-*`,
`--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-text-input-*` value reaches the members by inheritance, and one text field is set apart by setting
such a property on this element. Each property is its member's, set on that member unchanged: `label`,
`label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`,
`required-text` and `optional-text` are the Field's, every other one the text input's. One level down, the same by
hand: `<tanrei-field label="Email" required supporting-text="We never share your address.">
<tanrei-text-input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email"></tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>` — and the box
alone, where a label stands elsewhere, is `<tanrei-text-input>` with a `label` of its own.

It is a block as wide as its place, and its box fills it (TXF-62): give it a narrower place for a narrower box.

`value` is at every moment the text input's, and the five events are that input's own, with this element as their
target: `event.target.value` is the new value in every listener. It dispatches none itself. The one thing it does
that the pair by hand does not: while `counter` is set it gives its Field the count its text input keeps, at every
change (TXF-67) — by hand a product writes `field.countText = input.countText` in its `input` listener.

Form-associated: it submits the value under `name` — nothing while disabled —, resets to its `value` attribute, is
restored on navigation, follows a disabled `<fieldset>`, and reports what its text input reports: a missing value
while `required` is set and it is empty, and a date's or a time's entry error. Enter in a single-line
field presses the default button of this element's form.

The element is not focusable itself and has no role: `focus()` goes to the input, and its name is `label` (with
`label-hidden` where it is not drawn), never `aria-label`. A press on the label row, on the box or on a floating
label focuses the input; a press on the help, the error text, the count or the gap between a row and the box does
nothing.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: TXF-63: the one control the form meets. Its members stand in its shadow root, outside every form.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name (`label-hidden`). For a control whose visible label is elsewhere.

members.name: supportingText
members.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description (`supporting-text`). While the field is in error it gives way to `errorText`, unless the design system keeps both (`--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement: append`).

members.name: errorText
members.description: Shown while `error` is true, in `supportingText`'s place (below it, which stays, where the design system says `append`): what is wrong with this answer and how to put it right, in words (`error-text`).

members.name: error
members.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. The field never sets this itself.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

members.name: required
members.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates.

members.name: optional
members.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds `optional-text` to the control's description; ignored while `required` is true (FLD-32).

members.name: requiredMark
members.description: How this control shows that it is required (`required-mark`): `tag` is a small filled tag with `requiredText`, `asterisk` is "*" after the label, `none` draws nothing and keeps the semantics; `auto` takes the design system's answer (`--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark`, which follows `--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark`).

members.name: requiredText
members.description: The text of the required tag (`required-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ requiredText })`). Tanrei has none: without them the asterisk is drawn in the tag's place and the required state is kept.

members.name: optionalText
members.description: The text of the optional tag, also part of the description (`optional-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ optionalText })`). Tanrei has none: without them no tag is drawn and nothing is said.

members.name: variant
members.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

members.name: size
members.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

members.name: type
members.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

members.name: value
members.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

members.name: placeholder
members.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

members.name: readOnly
members.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

members.name: multiline
members.description: Accepts line breaks and shows several lines, sized as `resize` says. Ignored for password, date, time and date-time.

members.name: minRows
members.description:
The fewest lines a multi-line field shows (`min-rows`): the height of an empty auto-resized field, the starting and
smallest height of a manually resized one, and the height of a fixed one.

members.name: maxRows
members.description:
The most lines an auto-resized field grows to before it scrolls, and the tallest a manually resized one can be made
(`max-rows`); 0 is no limit. Ignored while `resize` is fixed.

members.name: resize
members.description:
How a multi-line field gets its height. `auto`: it follows the number of lines between `minRows` and `maxRows`, with
an animated change, and has no grip. `manual`: it starts at `minRows` lines and the person resizes it with the grip
in its bottom end corner. `fixed`: it stays at `minRows` lines, with no grip.

members.name: resizeAxis
members.description: What the person can resize by hand (`resize-axis`): the height only, or the height and the width. Ignored unless `resize` is manual.

members.name: resizeLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the resize grip (`resize-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ resizeLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the grip is drawn and works, and has no name.

members.name: noWrap
members.description:
Keeps every line of a multi-line code field on one row (`no-wrap`; the spec's `wrap: false`): a line wider than the
input scrolls sideways inside the container, and widens nothing. Without it a line that does not fit continues on
following rows; the value is the same either way. Read only while `type` is `code` and `multiline` is set: prose
always wraps, and a single line always scrolls in its line (reported in debug builds).

members.name: maxLength
members.description: The most user-perceived characters the user can enter; 0 is no limit (the `maxlength` attribute). Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: counter
members.description: Keeps a character count (with `maxLength`, when set: "12/40"): part of the description, announced when typing pauses, and readable as `countText`. The input draws none: a Field draws it at the end of its supporting row, given it as `count-text` — which `<tanrei-text-field>` does by itself.

members.name: counterText
members.description:
The count said to assistive technology while `counter` is set and `maxLength` is above 0 (`counter-text`): your
sentence with the places `{count}`, `{limit}` and `{remaining}` ("{remaining} characters left"). Empty reads the
product's words (`setWords({ characterCountText })`); with neither the count is said as its digits ("12/40"). It is
drawn as digits whatever is said: `countText` stays "12/40".

members.name: counterNoLimitText
members.description: The count said while `counter` is set and there is no `maxLength` (`counter-no-limit-text`): your sentence with the place `{count}` ("{count} characters"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ characterCountNoLimitText })`); with neither, the digits.

members.name: prefixText
members.description: Fixed text before the value, not part of it (`prefix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written before the value along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction; beside any other value it stands at the field's start edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the left of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: suffixText
members.description: Fixed text after the value, not part of it (`suffix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written after the value along the run's direction (see `prefixText`); beside any other value it stands at the field's end edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the right of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

members.name: autocomplete
members.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

members.name: locale
members.description:
A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for how a date, time or date-time field shows and reads its value: the order of its
segments, the separators, the clock, the digits and the names of the units. Empty uses the nearest `lang`
attribute, then the browser's language. The calendar is the Gregorian calendar in every locale.

members.name: min
members.description: The earliest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

members.name: max
members.description: The latest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

members.name: disabledDates
members.description:
Dates inside `min` and `max` that a date or date-time field does not accept from the person, as ISO 8601 calendar
dates — the same list the product gives its date-time picker. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated
list or a JSON array. Ignored by a time field.

members.name: invalidText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with some segments filled and others empty (`invalid-text`): shown by the Field that frames it as its error text, and part of a bare input's description.

members.name: unavailableText
members.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with a value before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates` (`unavailable-text`): shown and described as `invalidText` is.

members.name: segmentEmptyText
members.description: What assistive technology reads as the value of a date or time segment that holds nothing yet (`segment-empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ segmentEmptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them an empty segment has no value text.

members.name: picker
members.description:
Shows the picker button in a date, time or date-time field. The field presents no picker itself: it fires
`pickerrequest`, and the product presents one and sets `value` to what was picked.

members.name: pickerLabel
members.description: The accessible name of the picker button ("Choose date", `picker-label`). Required while the button is shown.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects the whole value, as the text input's `select()` does: a date or a time field's first segment takes focus.

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

events.description: The user changed the value (typing, deleting, pasting, dictation, autofill, an input method); `value` is already the new one. A date or time field fires it when its value changes — its last segment is filled, a filled row is edited, or it is emptied — not for a segment that leaves the value empty. events.description: The action key (Enter) was pressed in a single-line field. Cancelable: cancelling it keeps an enclosing form from being submitted.

events.description: The user activated the picker button of a date, time or date-time field. The product presents the picker and sets `value` to the picked value.
events.name: pickerrequest

attributes.description: The accessible name of the resize grip (`resize-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ resizeLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the grip is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: no-wrap
attributes.description:
Keeps every line of a multi-line code field on one row (`no-wrap`; the spec's `wrap: false`): a line wider than the
input scrolls sideways inside the container, and widens nothing. Without it a line that does not fit continues on
following rows; the value is the same either way. Read only while `type` is `code` and `multiline` is set: prose
always wraps, and a single line always scrolls in its line (reported in debug builds).

attributes.name: maxlength
attributes.description: The most user-perceived characters the user can enter; 0 is no limit (the `maxlength` attribute). Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: counter
attributes.description: Keeps a character count (with `maxLength`, when set: "12/40"): part of the description, announced when typing pauses, and readable as `countText`. The input draws none: a Field draws it at the end of its supporting row, given it as `count-text` — which `<tanrei-text-field>` does by itself.

attributes.name: counter-text
attributes.description:
The count said to assistive technology while `counter` is set and `maxLength` is above 0 (`counter-text`): your
sentence with the places `{count}`, `{limit}` and `{remaining}` ("{remaining} characters left"). Empty reads the
product's words (`setWords({ characterCountText })`); with neither the count is said as its digits ("12/40"). It is
drawn as digits whatever is said: `countText` stays "12/40".

attributes.name: counter-no-limit-text
attributes.description: The count said while `counter` is set and there is no `maxLength` (`counter-no-limit-text`): your sentence with the place `{count}` ("{count} characters"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ characterCountNoLimitText })`); with neither, the digits.

attributes.name: prefix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text before the value, not part of it (`prefix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written before the value along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction; beside any other value it stands at the field's start edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the left of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: suffix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text after the value, not part of it (`suffix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written after the value along the run's direction (see `prefixText`); beside any other value it stands at the field's end edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the right of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description:
A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for how a date, time or date-time field shows and reads its value: the order of its
segments, the separators, the clock, the digits and the names of the units. Empty uses the nearest `lang`
attribute, then the browser's language. The calendar is the Gregorian calendar in every locale.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The earliest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The latest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description:
Dates inside `min` and `max` that a date or date-time field does not accept from the person, as ISO 8601 calendar
dates — the same list the product gives its date-time picker. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated
list or a JSON array. Ignored by a time field.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with some segments filled and others empty (`invalid-text`): shown by the Field that frames it as its error text, and part of a bare input's description.

attributes.name: unavailable-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with a value before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates` (`unavailable-text`): shown and described as `invalidText` is.

attributes.name: segment-empty-text
attributes.description: What assistive technology reads as the value of a date or time segment that holds nothing yet (`segment-empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ segmentEmptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them an empty segment has no value text.

attributes.name: picker
attributes.description:
Shows the picker button in a date, time or date-time field. The field presents no picker itself: it fires
`pickerrequest`, and the product presents one and sets `value` to what was picked.

attributes.name: picker-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the picker button ("Choose date", `picker-label`). Required while the button is shown.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

declarations.name: EMPTY_SEGMENTS
declarations.default: { year: '', month: null, day: null, hour: null, minute: null, period: null }

declarations.name: holds
declarations.description: A segment holds something (TXF-43's "first empty segment"); a year with one digit does, though it gives no value yet.

declarations.name: rangeOf
declarations.description: The range a segment steps and types in (TXF-44), or null for a day period (its two names).

declarations.name: segmentsOf
declarations.description: The segments of an ISO value of the row's kind (TXF-31); every segment empty for an empty or malformed one.

declarations.name: valueOf
declarations.description: TXF-28, TXF-46: the ISO 8601 form of what the segments give, or empty while one of the row's is empty.

declarations.name: fill

type.text: { held: number; whole: number; of: number }

declarations.description: How many of the row's segments hold something, and how many there are (TXF-30: half-filled is some, not all).

declarations.name: shownOf
declarations.description: What a segment shows while it holds something (TXF-42), in the locale's digits; empty for an empty one.

declarations.name: sizersOf
declarations.description:
What a segment's cell is as wide as (TXI-42): the widest of these copies, none of which is drawn — its widest filled
form (four digits for a year, two for the month, the day, the hour and the minute, either name of a day period) and
its placeholder, whatever it holds now. "mm" is wider than two digits in most faces: a cell as wide as the digits
alone would let the placeholder run into the separators, and one that changed with what it holds would shift the row
at the first digit typed. So the row never moves as it fills or empties; an hour of one digit stands at the end of
its cell ("2:30 PM").

declarations.name: rowText
declarations.description: TXF-29, TXF-30: the row's text as drawn — the locale's form, an empty segment's placeholder left out.

declarations.name: spoken

type.text: { name: string; min: number; max: number; now: number | null; text: string | null }

declarations.description: TXF-47: a segment as assistive technology hears it.

declarations.name: PAGE
declarations.default: { year: 5, month: 2, day: 7, hour: 2, minute: 15, period: 1 }
declarations.description: TXF-44: what Page Up and Page Down step by.

declarations.name: stepped
declarations.description:
TXF-44: a segment raised or lowered by `by` within its own range, wrapping from the last value to the first and
back; an empty one is filled from the device's clock instead. No other segment changes, except a day beyond the last
day of the month and year the row now gives.

declarations.name: edged
declarations.description: TXF-44: Home and End set a month, day, hour or minute to the first and the last value of its range.

declarations.name: typed

type.text: { segments: Segments; typed: string; advance: boolean }

declarations.description:
TXF-45: a digit typed on a number segment. `typed` is the digits typed since the segment took focus: the digit is the
number's next one while they still form a number in the segment's range, and starts the number again otherwise. A
leading zero of a month, day or 12-hour hour waits for its second digit ("09"). `advance` says that no further digit
could extend the number.

declarations.name: erased
declarations.description: TXF-45: Backspace or Delete removes the last digit of a number segment, or the whole of a day period.

declarations.name: periodTyped
declarations.description:
TXF-45: a letter typed on a day-period segment — the first letter of the locale's name for the morning or for the
afternoon (where the two differ), or a or p in any case. Null for any other character.

declarations.name: SEPARATORS
declarations.description: TXF-45: the characters that move on from a segment that is not empty: a separator's.

declarations.name: CORE_VARIANTS
declarations.description: The values every design system has. A layer may add more; those get their styles on demand.

declarations.name: AXES
declarations.default: [ { name: 'size', core: CORE_SIZES, default: DEFAULT_SIZE, rules: (value, selector) => sizeBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_SIZE), probe: (value) => `${BOX}-container-height-${value}` }, { name: 'variant', core: CORE_VARIANTS, default: DEFAULT_VARIANT, rules: (value, selector) => variantBlock(value, selector, DEFAULT_VARIANT), probe: (value) => `${BOX}-${value}-container-color` }, ]
declarations.description:
The open axes (TXI-9): a size or variant a layer added gets its block on demand, built by the same functions
as the core blocks and falling back to the default's tokens; a value the active system lacks is reported in debug builds.

declarations.name: INSET

type.text: { leading: boolean; trailing: boolean; lead?: string }

declarations.description:
TXI-62, FLD-26: how far the input's text stands from its own start edge, and the padding it keeps at its end edge,
as lengths — the sums the box itself is laid out by (`--_text-start`, `--_end` below), written from the size's
tokens so that the Field that is told them resolves them where it stands: custom properties are inherited. Beside a
leading icon the text starts after the icon's padding, the icon and its gap; a trailing icon or the picker button
changes the end padding. A size a layer added falls back to the default's token, as its styles do. `lead` is the
measured length of the leading box where what the product slotted is wider than an icon (TXI-22): it stands for the
icon's size in the sum, as `--_lead` does in the styles.

declarations.name: DISABLED_DATES
declarations.description: `disabled-dates`: a space-separated list or a JSON array (src/primitives/values.ts). An element composed around the input declares the same converter.

The box people type in, and everything typed in it — one line, or several that follow the text or are resized by
hand, or a date or a time entered unit by unit in the locale's form — with optional icons, a prefix and a suffix, a
picker button, and, in the two looks that have one, the label that floats inside the box. It has no label row, no
help and no error text of its own: put it in a `<tanrei-field>`, which names it, describes it and marks it — or use
`<tanrei-text-field>`, which is the two as one element. Bare, it is for a place whose label stands elsewhere: a
filter in a toolbar, a cell of a table, a row with its label beside it; give it `label` there.

Contract: specs/text-input.spec.json. `<tanrei-field label="Email"><tanrei-text-input name="email" type="email">
</tanrei-text-input></tanrei-field>`, or bare: `<tanrei-text-input name="q" type="search" label="Filter tokens">
</tanrei-text-input>`. The box is drawn from `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*`, the one set of
tokens every input box is drawn from (TXI-68), one set per variant, look (plain or error) and state — how a state
looks is the active design system's decision — and what a text input alone draws (the resize grip, a segment, the
code face, the entries place) from `--tanrei-comp-text-input-*`. The text is edited in a native
`<input>` — a `<textarea>` while `multiline` — in the shadow root, so input methods, autofill,
selection and the clipboard work as the browser does. The name (its own `label`, else its Field's), the description
(the prefix and the suffix while shown, the count, then what its Field gives) and the invalid, required, read-only
and disabled states are set on that element.

It is a block as wide as its place, framed and bare alike (TXI-63): it has no width of its own. A narrower box is a
narrower place.

It tells the Field around it what only it knows, through the Field's own connection (`src/primitives/field.ts`):
that it draws the label itself while its look floats one, how far its text stands from its edges — the Field's
supporting row starts and ends there — and its own refusal of a date or a time, with its words (TXI-62). It takes
from that Field its name, its description, the required, invalid and disabled states, whether the label is hidden,
and whether an asterisk or the optional word follows a floating label. `countText` is the count it keeps while `counter` is set, as text
("12/40"): it describes and announces the count and draws none — a Field draws it, given it as `count-text`.

`stacked` (the default) draws no label — the label above it is its Field's row — and marks focus and error with a
line inside the container's edge; `filled` and `outlined` float the label inside the box. A design system may leave some out
: they still work, and a debug build says so.

`multiline` with `resize="auto"` (the default) follows its lines between `min-rows` and `max-rows` with an animated
height; `resize="manual"` draws a grip in the bottom end corner that is dragged, moved with the arrow keys, or
activated to fit the text (`resize-axis="both"` resizes the width too); `resize="fixed"` stays at `min-rows`.

`type="code"` is a field whose value is written for a machine — a pattern, a key, a snippet of configuration — on one
line or, with `multiline`, on many: the input line (prefix, value, placeholder, suffix) is one left-to-right row in
the code face that begins at the left in every layout direction, while the label, the icons, the messages and the
grip follow the page; the browser is asked not to correct, capitalise, spell-check, translate or complete it; a paste
is plain text, character for character; Tab still moves focus. `no-wrap` keeps each line of a multi-line code field
on one row and scrolls it sideways inside the container. It is a field, not an editor: no syntax colors, no line
numbers, no Tab that indents.

`date`, `time` and `date-time` are the stated exception to the native element: a row of segments — one spin button
per unit, in the locale's order — that are focused, stepped, typed into and cleared on their own, held as ISO 8601
(`2026-09-27`, `14:30`, `2026-09-27T14:30`) or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. A whole
date can be pasted. With `picker`, the field shows a picker button that asks the product to present a picker
(`pickerrequest`); the field presents none itself.

Form-associated: with a `name` it submits `value`, resets to its `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins
constraint validation (a missing value while its Field says it is required; a date or time field's entry error as badInput,
rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow or a custom error) and is left out while disabled — its own or a `<fieldset>`'s.

members.name: variant
members.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

members.name: size

members.name: type

members.name: error

events.description: The user committed a changed value: focus left the field (a date or time field's segments and picker button), or the action key was pressed in a single-line field.

events.name: entryerror
events.description: The user committed a date, time or date-time field that is half-filled (`invalid`) or whose value is not available (`unavailable`: before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates`), with the row's text as drawn.

events.name: pickerrequest
events.description: The user activated the picker button of a date, time or date-time field. The product presents the picker and sets `value` to the picked value.
The action key (Enter) was pressed in a single-line field. Cancelable: cancelling it keeps an enclosing form from being submitted.
events.name: action

attributes.description: The id of the form the text input belongs to, where it stands outside it: the platform's own attribute, which then wins over a form around it. The `form` property is read-only and returns the form element.
attributes.name: form
variant
attributes.description:
Stacked is a filled box that shows focus and error with a line inside its edge, under the label its Field draws
above it; filled and outlined float the label inside the box, marked by a tinted box and a bottom line, or by a
border. Use one style
per form. A design system may leave some out (the default system ships stacked only) or add values.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Minimum height of a single-line field's container (48 / 56 in the default system). The hit area always meets the minimum target.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
What the value is: chooses the keyboard, autocorrection, obscured entry and semantics. `code` is text written for
a machine rather than for a reader — a snippet of configuration, a pattern, an identifier, a query, a key: a
left-to-right run in the code face that the browser does not correct, capitalise, check for spelling or complete,
on one line or, with `multiline`, on many. `date`, `time` and `date-time` are entered segment by segment in the
locale's numeric form. The value is always a string.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
The text in the field; for date, time and date-time, the ISO 8601 form of what its segments give (2026-09-27, 14:30,
2026-09-27T14:30), or empty while a segment is empty or the value is not available. Setting it shows it and fires
nothing. The `value` attribute is what a form reset returns to.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The input's own accessible name, for an input no Field frames or one whose visible label is elsewhere; a filled or an outlined input draws it floating. Inside a Field leave it empty: the Field's label names the input, and its own would win.

attributes.name: label-hidden
attributes.description: Does not draw the floating label of a filled or an outlined input, which stays the accessible name (the `label-hidden` attribute). Inside a Field, hide the label on the Field.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description:
A hint shown while the value is empty and the label is not in the input line (above, floated or hidden). Never a
replacement for `label`. In a code field it is an example of the code and is drawn as code; a hint in words
belongs in its Field's `supportingText`. Ignored by a date, time or date-time field, whose empty segments each show their own.

attributes.name: error
disabled
attributes.description: Prevents focus, editing and form submission. Inside a Field, disable the Field, so that its label follows.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: The value can be focused, selected and copied, but not changed (the `readonly` attribute).

attributes.name: multiline
attributes.description: Accepts line breaks and shows several lines, sized as `resize` says. Ignored for password, date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: min-rows
attributes.description:
The fewest lines a multi-line field shows (`min-rows`): the height of an empty auto-resized field, the starting and
smallest height of a manually resized one, and the height of a fixed one.

attributes.name: max-rows
attributes.description:
The most lines an auto-resized field grows to before it scrolls, and the tallest a manually resized one can be made
(`max-rows`); 0 is no limit. Ignored while `resize` is fixed.

attributes.name: resize
attributes.description:
How a multi-line field gets its height. `auto`: it follows the number of lines between `minRows` and `maxRows`, with
an animated change, and has no grip. `manual`: it starts at `minRows` lines and the person resizes it with the grip
in its bottom end corner. `fixed`: it stays at `minRows` lines, with no grip.

attributes.name: resize-axis
attributes.description: What the person can resize by hand (`resize-axis`): the height only, or the height and the width. Ignored unless `resize` is manual.

attributes.name: resize-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the resize grip (`resize-label`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ resizeLabel })`). Tanrei has none: without them the grip is drawn and works, and has no name.

attributes.name: counter-text
attributes.description:
The count said to assistive technology while `counter` is set and `maxLength` is above 0 (`counter-text`): your
sentence with the places `{count}`, `{limit}` and `{remaining}` ("{remaining} characters left"). Empty reads the
product's words (`setWords({ characterCountText })`); with neither the count is said as its digits ("12/40"). It is
drawn as digits whatever is said: `countText` stays "12/40".

attributes.name: counter-no-limit-text
attributes.description: The count said while `counter` is set and there is no `maxLength` (`counter-no-limit-text`): your sentence with the place `{count}` ("{count} characters"). Empty reads the product's words (`setWords({ characterCountNoLimitText })`); with neither, the digits.

attributes.name: no-wrap
attributes.description:
Keeps every line of a multi-line code field on one row (`no-wrap`; the spec's `wrap: false`): a line wider than the
input scrolls sideways inside the container, and widens nothing. Without it a line that does not fit continues on
following rows; the value is the same either way. Read only while `type` is `code` and `multiline` is set: prose
always wraps, and a single line always scrolls in its line (reported in debug builds).

attributes.name: maxlength
attributes.description: The most user-perceived characters the user can enter; 0 is no limit (the `maxlength` attribute). Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: counter
attributes.description: Keeps a character count (with `maxLength`, when set: "12/40"): part of the description, announced when typing pauses, and readable as `countText`. The input draws none: a Field draws it at the end of its supporting row, given it as `count-text` — which `<tanrei-text-field>` does by itself.

attributes.name: prefix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text before the value, not part of it (`prefix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written before the value along the direction of the run the two affixes make — that of their first strong character, left-to-right where they have none — in every layout direction; beside any other value it stands at the field's start edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the left of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: suffix-text
attributes.description: Fixed text after the value, not part of it (`suffix-text`). Beside one line of email, url, tel, number or password it is written after the value along the run's direction (see `prefixText`); beside any other value it stands at the field's end edge. In a code field it is code: in the code face, at the right of the value in every layout direction. Ignored for date, time and date-time.

attributes.name: autocomplete
attributes.description: The autofill hint, as an HTML autofill field name (email, current-password, one-time-code…). A code field left without one asks the browser to offer no remembered entry.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description:
A BCP 47 tag ("en-US", "ja-JP") for how a date, time or date-time field shows and reads its value: the order of its
segments, the separators, the clock, the digits and the names of the units. Empty uses the nearest `lang`
attribute, then the browser's language. The calendar is the Gregorian calendar in every locale.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: The earliest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: The latest value a date, time or date-time field accepts from the person, ISO 8601; empty for no limit.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description:
Dates inside `min` and `max` that a date or date-time field does not accept from the person, as ISO 8601 calendar
dates — the same list the product gives its date-time picker. The `disabled-dates` attribute is a space-separated
list or a JSON array. Ignored by a time field.

attributes.name: invalid-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with some segments filled and others empty (`invalid-text`): shown by the Field that frames it as its error text, and part of a bare input's description.

attributes.name: unavailable-text
attributes.description: The words of the refusal of a date, time or date-time input committed with a value before `min`, after `max` or listed in `disabledDates` (`unavailable-text`): shown and described as `invalidText` is.

attributes.name: segment-empty-text
attributes.description: What assistive technology reads as the value of a date or time segment that holds nothing yet (`segment-empty-text`): this instance's words, else the product's (`setWords({ segmentEmptyText })`). Tanrei has none: without them an empty segment has no value text.

attributes.name: picker
attributes.description:
Shows the picker button in a date, time or date-time field. The field presents no picker itself: it fires
`pickerrequest`, and the product presents one and sets `value` to what was picked.

attributes.name: picker-label
attributes.description: The accessible name of the picker button ("Choose date", `picker-label`). Required while the button is shown.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name it is submitted under.

declarations.description:
The open axis (TBR-13): a variant a layer added gets its values on demand, built by the same function and
falling back to docked's tokens, and takes the docked structure (the structure is not a value: only `floating` is
drawn as a floating toolbar); a value the active system lacks is reported.

Holds a short row of actions for the current screen or selection, docked across the bottom edge or floating over the
content.

Contract: specs/toolbar.spec.json. Every value it reads is a `--tanrei-comp-toolbar-*` token of its variant: the
container's color, elevation, corners, cross-axis size, end padding and minimum gap, and the edge's color and width.
It draws no text, glyph or state of its own. Its items are the product's `<tanrei-button>` children,
icon-only or labelled, drawn from their own tokens with their own states, events and semantics (TBR-9); the toolbar lays them out,
scrolls them when they do not fit (TBR-8) and makes them one Tab stop moved through with the arrow keys (TBR-10).

The roving Tab stop is the items' `tabindex` (0 on the stop, -1 on the other enabled items; none on a disabled one):
both items delegate focus to the native button in their shadow root, which a host whose tabindex is -1 takes out of the
Tab order. Between two items each item's hit area stops at the middle of the gap, which the toolbar measures and gives
its items through an internal channel (src/primitives/group-item.ts) — not a styling API.

A floating toolbar lays its items `container.gap.floating` apart — 0 in the default system — and keeps for each a
length of `sys.target.touch` along its axis that its neighbour's does not reach into (TBR-16): two medium Buttons (40)
stand 8 apart, two large ones (56) touch. It measures its items for that and lays the space between two items as an
element of its own container (src/primitives/kept-length.ts): it writes nothing on the items, and a page's reset
(`* { margin: 0 }`) leaves the spacing as it is.
declarations.name: TanreiToolbar

cssParts.description: The surface: the variant's fill, elevation, corners and edge, holding the items (it scrolls them along its axis when they do not fit).
cssParts.name: container

slots.description: The items, in reading order: `<tanrei-button>` elements — an icon-only one for an action (a toggle such as Bold is one with `toggle`), a labelled one for a text action. Anything else is still laid out, and reported in debug builds (TBR-12).

system adds is drawn with the docked structure and its own values; a value the active system does not have is drawn
as `docked` (reported in debug builds, TBR-13).

members.name: orientation

The direction the items run. `vertical` is for a floating toolbar beside the content on a large screen; a docked
toolbar is always horizontal (reported in debug builds, TBR-6). Anything else is horizontal (TBR-13).

declarations.name: placeTooltip
declarations.description:
Where the container goes, in viewport coordinates (TIP-9, TIP-20, TIP-22 to TIP-25): `placeAnchored()` with the
tooltip's own fallback (`top`) and `auto` order (top, bottom, end, start, centred). Larger than the room on its side,
it is still kept `margin` inside the window's edges (TIP-9), over the anchor; only a container larger than the window
gives up the margin, at its bottom and end edges first.

declarations.description: `comp.tooltip.arrow.visible` and each form's `container.inverse`: a choice's name. The first is what an unknown name is.

declarations.name: INVERSE_PROPERTY
declarations.description: TIP-26: the look as the host carries it: its `inverse` attribute's, or — unset — its form's choice (the choice's NAME).

declarations.name: ARROW_PROPERTY
declarations.description: TIP-25: whether an arrow is asked for, as the host carries it: its `arrow` attribute's, or — unset — the system's choice.

Describes an element in a few words when a person points at it, focuses it with the keyboard or long-presses it,
without taking focus or blocking anything.

Contract: specs/tooltip.spec.json. Wraps its anchor (the default slot). The drawn tooltip is a `popover="manual"`
element in the shadow root, in the top layer — above an open modal `<dialog>` — placed against the anchor by script:
on the side and with the alignment `placement` names, `offset` away and moved along the side by `crossOffset`, flipped
to the opposite side, shifted along it and, in a window smaller than itself, held inside it; it keeps the side it is on
while that side has room, follows the anchor while open and closes when nothing of the anchor can be seen. It is a
read overlay: it never takes focus and holds nothing focusable.

It opens after a fine pointer rests on the anchor for the show delay (at once while tooltips are warm: another is open
or fading, or one closed a moment ago), at once on keyboard focus, and on a touch long-press; it stays while the pointer
is over the anchor, the gap between the anchor and the tooltip, or the tooltip, or the anchor has keyboard focus, and
closes on Escape, an activation of the anchor, a press on it, the hide delay after the pointer left, or the touch
timeout after the finger lifted. The show delay, hide delay and touch timeout are `showDelay`, `hideDelay` and
`touchTimeout` in milliseconds (0 is at once), or the tokens `motion.show-delay`, `motion.hide-delay` and
`timeout.touch` while unset. Opening and closing by itself fires `toggle`; setting `open` does not.

It comes out of the anchor's side: it fades in while it grows from `motion.enter-scale` and travels
`motion.enter-offset`, the growth fixed where an arrow points or would point, and goes back the same way; a motion that
is interrupted turns round from where it is, a warm tooltip appears whole at once, and where motion is reduced it
fades alone. Its place is never animated.

`arrow` draws a triangle that points at the anchor, one shape with the container; `inverse` draws it in the opposite
scheme's colors (true) or on a surface of the scheme (false). Left unset, each takes the system's choice:
`--tanrei-comp-tooltip-arrow-visible` (off in the default system) and its form's `-plain-container-inverse` (on) or
`-rich-container-inverse` (off). `shortcut` writes the keys of the anchor's command after a plain tooltip's text and
gives them to the anchor as `aria-keyshortcuts`.

While `describes` is true (the default; the attribute `no-describe` turns it off) the text — after the title, for a
rich tooltip — is the anchor's `aria-description`, set on the first focusable element slotted in (a Tanrei component
forwards it from its host to its native element), whether or not the tooltip is open.

Every visual value comes from `--tanrei-comp-tooltip-*` tokens.

declarations.description:
A hierarchy of items that open and close: rows that begin further in at each level, a chevron at the start or the end of every row that holds others (or none, the folder glyph opening), names on one line shown whole in a tooltip where they are cut, the rows of the open parents above what is shown pinned at the top of the scrolling box; read and opened only, or with one item or several chosen. One stop in the focus order, moved through with the arrow keys. A file tree in a page, the tokens of a design system, the folders of a product. Contract: specs/tree-view.spec.json. The element has **no shadow root**: its items are the product's own nested lists, which stay in the document. Without script the page shows the whole hierarchy as the nested list it is. ```html
  • folder srcwhat is published 12 files
    • index.ts
  • node_modules
 ``` An item is an `
  • ` whose FIRST child element is its row and whose `
      ` holds its items. In the row, a `.tanrei-icon` is the icon, an element with `data-trailing` the trailing content, one with `data-trailing-text` the trailing text, and the rest is the label: the row's own text, or ONE element around it (a ``: text with inline content, a name whose direction is not the layout's). An element with `data-supporting-text` is the supporting text, inside the label's element or directly in the row. On the `
    • `: `data-value` (what identifies it; without one it cannot be chosen), `data-open`, `data-expandable` (it will hold items: give them at `toggle`), `data-loading`, `data-disabled`. The element sets and removes `data-open` itself when the user opens or closes a parent. Everything drawn is `@tanrei/web/tree-view.css` — every value a `--tanrei-comp-tree-view-*` token — which draws the whole look before this script runs; the element adds the same sheet to the root it is connected to. The script adds what a stylesheet cannot: the tree's roles and states, the single tab stop and the keys, the selection, `change` and `toggle`, the answer to a press, the motion of a list that is revealed or hidden, the loading row, opening for the browser's find-in-page, editing names in place and naming new items (`editable`, `edit()`, `create()`), and the debug reports. Only the rows that are shown are read: a closed parent's items are read when it first opens, so a tree costs what it shows. The ROW is the tree item (`role="treeitem"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, the tab stop and the focus); its `
    • ` has no role and a nested list is a `group`, so the level comes from the nesting. An `
    • ` holds every row under it, so what changes while the tree is used is said on the row: one row's change styles that row alone. A server that draws the selection in the first frame writes `aria-selected="true"` on the row.

members.name: iconGap

members.name: highlight
members.description: How far a row's fill, state layers and focus ring reach: indented (from its level), full (across the tree).

members.name: labelWrap

members.name: supportingWrap

members.name: stickyParents
members.description: Pins the rows of the open parents above what is shown at the top of the scrolling box. On by default; `sticky-parents="false"` turns it off.

members.name: stickyMax
members.description: The most rows pinned at once, the innermost parents winning.

members.name: editable
members.description: Lets people rename items in place: a double-click on a row's label, or F2, opens a text field; the tree emits `rename` and the product sets the label.

members.description: The accessible name of the field in which a name is edited or a new item named ("Name"). Tanrei ships none.

members.name: edit
members.description:
Opens the edit field on an item's name (TRV-45), as F2 and a double-click on its label do: only while the tree is

opened one.

members.name: create
members.description:
Asks for a new item (TRV-48): a row of the tree's own, at the level of the selected item and after its rows, with
an empty field in which the user names it. `create` carries the name; the product adds the item. Returns whether
the row was added (a tree with no list has nowhere to put it).

events.name: create
events.description: The user named the new item `create()` asked for: `detail.label`, `detail.parent`, and the `<li>` it goes under (`detail.within`, null at the first level) and follows (`detail.after`, null where it is first). The tree's own row is gone; add the item, and the tree moves focus to it.

events.name: change
events.description: The user changed the selection: `detail.value` (single) or `detail.values` (multiple) after the change.
Dispatched on an item's `<li>` (it bubbles): the user, or the browser's find-in-page, opened or closed it; `detail.open` is its new state. The moment to give the items of an `data-expandable` parent.
events.name: toggle

events.description: Dispatched on an item's `<li>` (it bubbles): the user gave it a new name in place; `detail.label` is the name (trimmed, not empty, not the old one) and `detail.previous` the label it had. The tree changes no label: set it to rename the item.
