declarations.description:
The base of a composed element (W1, W7, W8, W9). A subclass renders its members' own elements —
`<tanrei-field part="field" exportparts=${FIELD_PARTS.attribute} ${forward(this, FIELD)}>` — and says which of them
focus goes to (`control`).

The shadow root does not delegate focus (W7): a press on text that is not a control must move no focus. The host is
never focusable; `focus()` and `blur()` are the control's, a click that arrives on the host itself — a page's own
`<label for>` — moves focus to the control, and `autofocus` on the host reaches the control when the element first
renders.
declarations.name: ComposedElement

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

declarations.description:
A composed element with a value member (W5, W6). The subclass names the member (`valueMember`) and writes the
`value` accessor in place, on these two:

    get value(): string { return this.memberValue(''); }
    set value(value: string) { this.giveValue(value); }

**The value is the member's at every moment** (W5): what was last set on the element until the member has taken it
— the element's next render — and from then on what the member holds. So in every listener of a member's event,
capturing or bubbling, `event.target.value` is the new value, and a value the member changed is read back changed.

**The element is the form's control** (W6): its class says `static formAssociated = true`; it takes `name` and `form`, and repeats on its own
internals what its value member tells its own through `FormSays` (src/primitives/form-says.ts) — the value and the
state as they are, the validity flags, the message and the member's own anchor. It resets to its `value` attribute
(`firstValue()`), passes a restore on to the member, and joins a disabled `<fieldset>` with its own `disabled` for
its frame (`formDisabled`). Enter is the member's: it asks for the element's form (`formOf`).
declarations.name: ComposedControl

members.name: name
members.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

members.name: form
members.description: The form it belongs to, if any.

members.name: validity
members.description: The element's validity: its value member's (W6, item 3).

members.name: focus
members.description: W7, item 2: focus is the control's.

members.name: blur
members.description: W7, item 2: what has focus inside the control loses it (an engine does not take it from inside a host it blurs).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Web only: the name the value is submitted under.

declarations.description:
A destination of a bar: a subclass gives its tag, its styles (`destinationStyles()` with its prefix, and the
cell's layout in the region) and nothing else. The region tells it whether it is selected, its position and whether
its label is drawn; it fires `DESTINATION_UPDATE` when a prop the region reads changes.
declarations.name: NavigationDestination

members.name: value
members.description:
What identifies the destination: the region's `value` selects it by this, and `change` / `reselect` carry it. While
it is given none, a link's `href` stands for it, as written (NVB-30) — so a page sets the region's `value` to its
own address and nothing on the items.

members.name: label
members.description: Its name, drawn under the icon (as the region's label visibility says) and always its accessible name. Required.

members.name: icon
members.description: The name of a glyph of the system's icon set: outlined while unselected, filled while selected. Required.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Unavailable: it keeps its place and its disabled look, cannot be activated and leaves the focus order.

members.name: badge
members.description: Draws a Tanrei badge on the icon, from `badgeCount` and `badgeLabel`.

members.name: badgeCount
members.description: The badge's count: null (no attribute) draws the dot, 0 nothing, above 0 the number (999+ above 999).

members.name: badgeLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads after the destination's name and state ("3 unread"). A dot needs one.

members.name: href
members.description: The address the destination leads to: a URL, a path or a fragment. Not empty, the destination is a link and not a button (NVB-30), and the region does not select it by a press (NVB-31). White space is no address; a `javascript:` address or one that cannot be read is refused and reported (NVB-33).

members.name: target
members.description: Where a link opens: `same` (here) or `new` (a new tab or window, with `noopener`), which a cell has no place to mark and says through `targetLabel` (NVB-32). HTML's `_self` and `_blank` are read as those; anything else is `same` and is reported (NVB-33). Ignored without `href`.

members.name: targetLabel
members.description: What assistive technology reads at the end of the link's description while `target` is `new` ("opens in a new tab"): your words, in your language. Required then; ignored otherwise.

members.name: rel
members.description: Web only: the anchor's `rel`. `noopener` is added while `target` is `new`; `noreferrer` is yours to add.

members.name: download
members.description: Web only: the anchor's `download`. A link that asks for a download is the browser's: the region fires nothing for it (NVB-31).

members.name: selected
members.description: Whether the region draws this destination as its selected one.

members.name: click
members.description: `element.click()` activates the destination as a person would; a disabled one does nothing.
